# @astryxdesign/cli

# 0.7.17

#### Experimental APIs

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` offers a font asked for on a part as its preset's whole stack ("monospace numbers in tables" gives `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`), so systems without its first family show the next one of its kind. It no longer offers `ui-monospace` alone, which only Apple systems draw.
- `astryx experimental theme` pictures (`--png`) say when this machine has no font of the kind a stack names, for example headings set to the serif preset on a system with no serif font, which the picture shows in a sans-serif font. The font dial's help no longer says system presets always show.
- The `astryx experimental theme` font dial's help names `rounded` as Nunito, an open font that loads once its package is installed, no longer beside the system presets. It also says exactly when a picture names a missing font: a serif, monospace or cursive stack drawn in a font of another kind.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a whole-theme token the base theme draws past on a part (neutral's neutral badge fills with its own gray, not `--color-neutral`) is no longer reported as reaching it. `set` says that part does not use the token and gives the command that does; `how <token>` lists those parts under `notIn`; and a value question about the part answers what it draws there, the theme's own setting on it first.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data now knows the context menu (and its dividers): each part is right-clicked when a press opens nothing and it holds a layer, as one drawn in its own place is, so `how` reads what a context menu draws instead of saying it is unknown.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a role color too dark to stand out on the dark page still draws dark mode at the documented shade 70, and the set result now offers the shade nearest it that passes as a one-line dark-mode choice. `how` for a deeper or darker role color includes a dark-mode line that stands out on the dark page, so dark mode goes the way the color asked instead of turning paler.
- `astryx discover` lists the icon sets your discover sources offer even where icon features are off (no icon-set package installed and no `experimental.iconSet`), so an app can compare packs before it picks one. A pack shows in the Available list (`iconSets`), in a search, and on its `discover <package>/<set>` page, with the catalog's display name, description, license and icon count. When the catalog lists the set's definitions, the page's text says how many of the CLI's icon definitions it maps (`definitions: 152/180`, as `experimental icon --list` prints it); the definitions themselves are listed only where icon features are on. Each listed set is marked `[experimental]` in text and carries `experimental: true` in JSON (a package entry names its experimental `iconSets` in `experimentalFields`). The page gives the project's install command, then `astryx experimental icon use <package>/<set>`. Installed sets, their pages and `--type icon-set` still need icon features on, `astryx search`'s discover line never points at an icon set while they are off, icon-set fields on other kinds are ignored, and a catalog with no icon set gives the same output as before. Discover catalogs may give an icon set's `license`.
- Doctor's new `icon-imports` check names each icon import that no longer matches the app's icon sets after the list changes or a set is uninstalled: an icon from a set the list leaves out, or from a backup when an earlier set draws the same meaning, warns with the icon of the list that replaces it; an icon import or re-export of an npm package that is not installed, not declared, and not mapped by a `paths` or `baseUrl` entry in the app's tsconfig or jsconfig fails, since it breaks the build, even when that package is the main set itself. The check runs where icon features are on and a main set is decided.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> --color-border <color>`: the emphasized border (input and selector frames) follows a border only where that makes it stronger on the surface, never fainter, and the result now says it follows; `show` names it as following your `--color-border`, not as a change in the theme's own source.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: secondary text set exactly for the whole theme (in one mode or both) no longer turns off the readable shade on the parts that lift it (selected items and rows, a dropzone, numbered citations). Where the exact color reads on what those parts sit on it is used as written; where it does not, they take the gray nearest it that does, or, with no color dial, the base theme's own lift.
- A run of one `astryx experimental` command loads only that command, as `astryx <command>` already does. `astryx experimental export` and `astryx experimental import` no longer load the theme editor first, so each run starts about 0.2 seconds sooner. `astryx experimental` alone, its help, and an unknown word still load every command, so they print the same answers.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> accent <color>` keeps the color you gave as the link and accent text color wherever it reads at 4.5:1 on what that text sits on, in each mode its fill is your exact color; only where it does not do links move, to the nearest shade that reads, and the result says so with the ratio. Text on the fill stays white or near-black by contrast (button and badge labels are normal-size text, which needs 4.5:1, so white on iOS blue #007aff, at 4.02:1, is not picked), and the note now names how to keep the other one exactly.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every way an amount is said ("a quarter bigger", "half again", "2x", "×2", "x0", "4 times", "by a factor of 2", "+50%", "-25%", "50 percent", "½") as a factor of what is there now, never as a length and never with an extra dial step; keeps fractions of a pixel; scales a part's line height and opacity the asked way ("50% more transparent" lowers the opacity and leaves the fill); answers whole-theme radius and border width amounts with exact token values (a whole-theme spacing or text amount it can only step says so); says when a part has no width to scale instead of giving a fixed cap; scales an own side padding with the rest; keeps the state and variant of a "2px rounder on hover" move and of a padding step; reads a corner percent with an amount ("50% of now", "20% bigger") as an exact radius, never a CSS percent; says when a corner amount can only step; and reads "no inner spacing", "zero padding" and "no gap" as zero of that thing, in the state asked.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: amounts read the way they are said. Zero, none and no set that property to 0 or none in any position ("card corners zero", "zero border", "opacity zero", "no letter spacing", "remove the top padding"), and a padding side reads its own value now. One amount reader takes "up 20%", "increase by 50%", "2/3", "two thirds", "three quarters", "twice as small", "a third again" and a lone "½" as a share of now; a bare percent radius is refused with the command that scales the radius instead. "Two steps bigger" gives two dial steps, "2 spacing units" is twice the spacing unit token, a size such as "24x16px" on padding is that exact padding, and "+4px", "-2px" or "4px more" on padding, gap, radius or text size is the value now plus or minus that length. See-through amounts set opacity ("half transparent", "10% transparent", "50% opacity"), "more opaque" raises it, and "5% gray" is gray at 5% alpha. Color amounts apply to text and hover colors; warmer and cooler move the hue, not the lightness; lighter and darker change the color of borders, dividers and links, and keep the alpha of rgb(), hsl() and oklch() colors. Small, secondary and supporting text and fine print change the supporting text size; "h1 800" is a weight; "h2 through h4" changes each level; "h1 800 and the other headings 600" sets every other level; "h1 twice as big as body text" and "h3 the same size as h2" take the other size times the amount; "and the active one blue" keeps that state. Thinner text is a lighter weight, a sharper shadow halves the blur of the part's shadow and a softer one doubles it, a thinner scrollbar says there is no scrollbar part, the overlay's lighter or darker changes only its alpha, and wider no longer sets a made-up 720px width. `how paddingLeft`, `how borderRadius` and other camelCase names look up that property.
- `astryx experimental theme compile`: `--check` of an editor theme also checks its app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` and fails with `ERR_THEME_STALE`, saying why, when the copy is kept back, missing a file, gone, or not the current build. Each theme's copy follows its own build, so a later theme failing no longer leaves an earlier one's copy behind. The copy's files are not theme sources: compiling its descriptor, a copy build file or `src/astryx-themes.ts` names the theme to compile, the copy's source from a subfolder names the app root, and an `--out` into the copy folder is refused. A copy left with only its build outputs is still the editor's, a copy file that is gone is written back by the next `set`, and a folder the copy could not be made in is named. The compile help says it writes and checks the app copy.
- `astryx experimental theme compile`: a successful compile of an editor theme always writes its app copy from what it just built, a hand edit of `<theme>.theme.ts` included, with the copy's font stylesheet from the fonts the theme loads now (a font package installed or removed since; a `set` that changes nothing refreshes it too). `--check` reads the copy as a checkout writes it (CRLF line endings pass), compares it only once the theme's outputs are current (a hand-edited theme output is named by the outputs check), and a stale copy keeps the documented check result: `upToDate: false`, code `ERR_THEME_STALE` and `appCopyStale` saying why. The copy's source and folder are no compile targets, an `--out` at the copy folder (any case, with or without a slash) is refused and suggests the same compile without `--out`, and a refused compile writes no copy. The help says so.
- `astryx experimental theme`: every command that builds or checks an editor theme says when its app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` is behind: `compile` warns, `compile --check` fails while the copy is kept back or gone, and a `set` that changes nothing still carries `appCopyStale`. A link or a folder of yours at a copy file name stops the copy like a file of yours does, and a copy that cannot be written says why (not writable, disk full, a file where the folder goes). A copy whose descriptor was deleted is still the editor's and is written back. Compiling the copy's source takes the theme's lock and writes the copy again; with the copy gone it names `editor show`. Fonts the copy's font stylesheet loads are not called unloaded. The editor and compile help say the copy rule.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` is written around a file of yours at another name (a note, a swap file); only a file of yours at one of the copy's names, or a link on the way to it, stops it, and then every change's result and `wiring` say the copy was not updated and why. The copy's `<theme>.fonts.css` is always there (a comment only when the theme loads no font stylesheet), so the app theme module's import of it holds when fonts or the base change; `compile` writes the whole copy, that file included. `new` refuses a name the theme commands skip (`a--b`, `b-`) and suggests the cleaned one. The package commands give true answers for an editor theme: `eject` says its source is yours already, and a path (`themes/<theme>`) is answered with the command by name.
- The in-app theme preview's top bar draws the theme's name with Core's `TopNavHeading`, as an app's top bar does, so a setting on the header (such as its text color) shows in the preview as it does in the app.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: asks that name parts by reference or in two states read as Core draws them. "The disabled one" after an element in a place ("the hovered item of menus … and the disabled one") is that element; "the others" are the part's other variants, or the part not in the state named; states said together read by their kind, a condition among them (checked, selected, disabled) meaning all at once and moment states alone (hovered, pressed) meaning each, with the other reading offered as a second line; a selected table row hovered sets the selected wash's token for hover; a switch's "on color" is its checked look; tighter table rows lower the cells' block padding one spacing step. A border asked of a list inside an overlay's surface (a typeahead's) points to the overlay's edge, and `set` refuses a border's color or width on a part that draws no border (a divider), offering the token its line reads.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`'s pictures and contrast checks take a toast's text side by Core's own rule for the fill the toast draws: the theme's text where it reads at 3:1, else the on-color that reads better; a see-through fill is composited onto the page first, and a gradient falls back from the inverted surface, as the app does. A problem there comes with a `color` line on the toast, which set takes. A transparent part on a lightbox's dark island is measured on that island. Parts drawn open keep the custom properties their inline styles set (a dialog's maximum size, a popover's gap to its trigger), and a plain element in a doc example (the Overlay's media) draws.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set … surfaces`: a panel whose outer frame paints nothing (the banner) gets the dial's line and shadow on the part inside that paints its rounded fill, so `surfaces outlined` no longer draws a square border around the banner's rounded corners, and a border setting on the banner reaches that line. `how` never reads "Windows" named with a version ("Windows 11 accent #0067c0") as the containers.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the "thick borders on everything" answer and a whole-theme `--border-width` also reach a framed control (a segmented control), the parts that draw a box only when selected (nav items, segments), on that state, and the indicator lines (a tab's underline), at the border width.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a size ask with a bound that the part is already past the way the words ask ("rounder but at most 16px" on 42px corners) writes nothing and says so, never a move the other way; a direction beside a bound on a property with no scale of the theme's own (height) goes to the bound; "the body text … but at most 16px" is the base text size. A theme color with a way ("the accent color but lighter") is that color made that way in each mode. "The page color" as a gradient stop is the color the page is painted with, and the page is not changed. A role color made darker or lighter on a dark-only theme moves each of its tokens that way, its text included. "The same as" after a color property compares that color. "What color is the page" gives the page's color in each mode, and its pointer is the token that paints it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` names words the sample page's pictures break across two lines inside the word (a table word at a larger text size, "roadma" then "p"), measured in the page by the browser that takes the picture, as it names text cut short: a note, and a problem with the line that keeps the word whole when the browser measured one, else none.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a light-only or dark-only theme's build exports its one mode beside the theme (`export const colorModes = ["light"];`), and its app copy re-exports it, so `theme add` wires the theme in that mode. Older CLIs and Core ignore the extra export.
- `astryx experimental theme`: every build names the pictures it removed, so `editor show` and the preview commands say so too when they build a theme again. A picture run whose browser fails part way says which pictures it took and which it did not. A render that fails on two copies of React points at the package manager's listing of them instead of `doctor`. `show --section` offers a section only within a typo of what was typed, else the whole sheet; `preview add --top` offers the typed number read exactly or brought into range, else the default; `preview add --template` offers a default page (overview, components, colors) within a typo. A base theme whose fonts come from a remote stylesheet (Google Fonts) gets a note that the previews and their pictures show the next font, and how to install a copy they load. The sheet's template pages render (they bind their file's default export), and a part Core re-exports under a name of its own (ContextMenuItem) gets its module and a cell; a component no Core module exports gets no empty cell.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: one built-value check for a theme's own token values runs before every build (`set`, `undo`, `show`, the preview) and in `compile`, so a value one refuses the other never writes. A `[light, dark]` pair on a token that is not a color is refused however the file gives it (an import, a const, a spread), naming the file and line that hold it. Typography weights are judged as the tokens they build. A private variable (`--_*`) and a key that is no token name (`color`) are refused with their line. A pair in the theme file is shown by its light and dark values in notes. `undo` of a token the theme's own source sets names that file and line.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: `new` reads a built-in theme typed with another word (`theme neutral`, `neutral stone`) as the base, never as the neutral color dial, and a base or setting typed with its own quotes (`'base neutral'`, `"accent" red`, `'"base": "neutral"'`, `'padding: 8px'`) as that setting, never as words of the name. A setting `new` takes no option for points at the parts it is written on (`how '8px padding'`), in place of a `set` line `set` itself refuses. `undo` by a held value with a scope typed ranks the settings by how much of that scope they share, so `undo t red --on toggle-button` leads with a toggle-button setting rather than a whole-theme one.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` contrast-checks the button style (`buttons soft` and `outline`) like any other change: the primary button's text on the fill it draws, or on the page and surface where it draws none, in each mode, with the nearest readable color as its line, instead of a "not checked" note.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> padding '5px 0' --on dropdown-menu` (or any part whose padding Core reads inside `calc()`, where one length is all that works) now offers the sides it means. Before, it offered a pointer to `how` for two lengths, and for three or four lengths (or two variables) one line with the first value only, such as `padding 2px`, which dropped the other lengths. Now it offers `padding-block 5px` and `padding-inline 0` for two lengths, `padding-top`, `padding-inline` and `padding-bottom` for three, and each side for four, each with the length you typed for it. A repair gate fix lets such a refusal offer three or four side lines together.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the cached part data is keyed by a fingerprint of the code that builds it (the census source and every file it imports), beside the installed Core, so any change to that code builds it again; there is no version number to bump by hand.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`:
  - The part data reads overlays drawn open: a tooltip, a popover, a hover card, and the lists a menu's button or a selector's field opens, which render on the server as markers alone, so `how tooltip` names what it paints and the menus group is checked.
  - A fill set on a part says which fills Core gives its variants and states it now covers (a checked box's accent, a primary button's), with the line that changes only the fill at rest and the lines that fill one variant or state; a later color change says where the part's own fill keeps it from reaching.
  - `corners more` from round steps to half as round again before pill, and `corners less` from pill back.
  - A border color the theme sets is held to 3:1 against what it sits on in each mode.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` names more of what a change leaves unchecked or unreached: a part's text color for a state (a selected nav item's) is measured on the fill the part draws in that state, with the nearest readable color as its line; a color the base theme writes as its own accent rather than the accent token (butter's blue links and outline buttons) is listed under missed once the accent moves, with a line that points it at the accent; and a fill made from a status token the theme's status color does not reach (an error toast's red after the danger color is set) is listed, with a line that gives it the theme's status color.
- A change lists every custom property whose built value moved, in the JSON and the text: `changedTokens` keeps the theme's own tokens, the page included, and a new `changedPartTokens` lists the tokens the built stylesheet sets on parts (a readable text color on a selected row), each by its rule and mode, read from the stylesheet before and after the change. A dial that moves many tokens at once (vibrancy, a font) lists them all.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: one check for the token values a theme's own source gives, run by `show`, `set`, `undo` and `compile`, each refusing with the same message and writing nothing. A `[light, dark]` pair holds exactly two values in quotes (one, none or three is refused). Values from an imported module or written as an expression (`'ban' + 'ana'`, a template) are checked as a build evaluates them, naming the line. A second `tokens` key is refused, naming both lines (JavaScript keeps only the last). A family list in one pair of quotes is refused in the file as `set` refuses it (the browser reads it as one family by that whole name). The `typography` fields are checked: a family is one family name (the rest go in `fallbacks`), the scale's ratio is above 1 and at most 4, its base a positive size.
- `astryx experimental theme`:
  - Custom properties that read each other are refused at their line: a token and a local token reading one another, and a part's own custom property reading itself.
  - A pseudo-class after `::search-text` (`:current`) or `::scroll-marker-group` is accepted. A pseudo-element inside `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` or `:has()`, a pseudo-class after `::highlight()`, and `:window-inactive` after any highlight but `::selection` are refused. A pseudo-element near a known one (`::befor`) is refused as that one misspelled; one missing from the CLI's selector data and near none (`::column`, `::scroll-button()`) is noted as possibly newer than the CLI, and built.
  - A misspelled vendor property (`-webkit-line-clmap`, `WebkitApperance`) is refused, with the vendor property it is near.
  - A value read from another file through array or nested destructuring (`const [first] = arr`, `const {a: {b}} = cs`) is blamed on that file and line.
  - A null value is warned at its line and the theme keeps working, while a boolean, NaN, an object or an array, which mean nothing in CSS, are refused. The warning says what it builds: a null property leaves the base theme's value; a null token is kept by the browser as the token's value, so most properties that read it act as if they were not set (text keeps the surrounding color, a background goes transparent) and a font family reading it falls back to the browser's default font.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a color dial made lighter or darker steps from the color it grows its shades from, its saved color, else its token where that is a color of its own. "make the neutral color darker" no longer offers `neutral '#000000'` (a gray seed grows the same shades, so it changed nothing) nor an exact `--color-neutral` that turned every see-through neutral fill opaque; it says why and what to name instead. An exact-token alternative keeps the token's own strength.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set`: a color set with no `--mode` in a one-mode theme (`dark-only`) is saved for that mode, as it is built, so setting the theme back to both modes keeps it in its mode instead of painting the other mode with it, and a color saved for the other mode (the half a toast or a lightbox reads) is kept. An undo with no `--mode` removes that color.
- `astryx experimental theme compile`: the app copy guard reads paths as the build does, so an `--out` written with backslashes or through a link into an editor theme's copy is refused, and a copy file named with backslashes is answered with the theme to compile. A file of yours in the copy folder, without the editor's mark, compiles like any theme source. Refusals run from a subfolder suggest the compile from the app root. The note on fonts named but not loaded follows the font stylesheet this compile writes, and the copy's font file no longer says the system has a font no package loads. A check held up by a file of yours names it and never sends you to a command that does not move it.
- `astryx experimental theme`: the editor reads which theme a source defines from the export a build of it loads, so a helper theme exported beside the real one is refused before anything is written, and a name given by a const or a `//` inside a string no longer counts as damage. Font notes, the previews and the app copy load fonts for the families the theme builds, from one list. `compile` refuses an `--out` in the theme's own folder (other than its default stylesheet) before writing anything; an `--out` elsewhere says that the theme's folder and its app copy were not written or checked (`appCopySkipped`). A pointer to compile from the app root leaves off an `--out` the root cannot reach, and a family refusal from a subfolder suggests a compile that runs. Suggested commands stay bare in JSON (`astryx …`), as the text output starts them the way the project runs the CLI. The compile doc says what compiles.
- `astryx experimental theme`: the editor judges a theme's source by the theme a build of it loads, its name and the theme it extends after every spread and repeated key, so a spread or a second `extends` that replaces the settings is refused, a spread const or a namespace import of the settings is accepted, and a helper theme read first is named with how to make the build read the theme. `compile` takes an `--out` as the theme's default stylesheet only when it is that same file, refusing a name that differs only in case on a case-sensitive disk and a folder form of the stylesheet before anything is written; builds a source named through a folder link under its own path; says in JSON what the app copy write did (`appCopy`, `appCopyStale`); names the Fontsource package for an editor theme's fonts. Every suggested compile passes the same checks before it is shown. Fonts follow every family the build writes, a part's own font included. A module that imports a file beside the theme keeps the app copy as it was and says why. A change of mode on a theme the app lists names `theme add`.
- `astryx experimental theme compile`: a compile or `--check` of an editor theme whose source no longer imports or extends its settings, or names another theme, is refused with the same message `set` gives, so it never writes another theme's files or drops every setting. The app copy's font stylesheet imports the installed `@fontsource` package of every family the built theme uses, the theme's own source included, and compile's note on fonts named but not loaded follows it. A theme build counts the families the theme's own font stylesheet beside its source loads (the app copy's), so a build of the copy's source no longer names them as unloaded. A blank or whitespace-only `--out` is refused.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part word matches only as a word of its own, never as one half of a hyphenated compound, so "field-service app: large bold text, thick borders" is the whole theme's ask, not the inputs'.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the contrast check reads gradients, and `how` reads side nav section headings as the sections.
  - Text on a gradient background is measured against each of its color stops, the worst one counting; a background with an image, or a stop with no fixed color, is listed as not checked.
  - `how` reads "sidebar section headings" as the side nav's sections, whose title is drawn inside them, and says which inner parts an inherited text property also reaches.
  - `how <part>` says what the part is, from its component's doc.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the contrast check measures what draws the text. A toast's text on Core's media surface reads the on-dark or on-light color, so a low one is a problem with a fix that sets it; a color given as a theme token (`var(--token)`) is measured as that token's value in each mode; and text on different parts is a problem for each part, so following one fix line no longer turns up the others as new.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` fixes contrast problems at their source: a whole-theme text color too faint in many places gets one line on that token, the nearest color that reads everywhere it was too faint, instead of one line per part; a pale status or accent fill gets the nearest darker color that stands out from the page as its line; and a failure the base theme draws itself is said by `show`, not after every change.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: every contrast problem is listed in the JSON (`newProblems`, `openProblems`, `problems`); the text shows the first eight and counts the rest. A change's new problems are the ones the settings before it, read as the change reads them, did not have, so a base or part saved in other letters no longer loses the check or lists old problems as new. A fix line sets what draws the text: a plain `color` that wins over a token, else the text token, scoped to the variant the text is drawn in, so following it clears the problem; text written straight in a part with its own `color` is measured against the part's fill. `show` says a saved base in other letters reads as the base; an entry with a thing and no value gets its `undo` line; a dial name in other letters (`Corners`, `MODE`) is the dial; a theme typo on a step back with nothing to undo offers `show`; and `new`'s set repair for a theme it did not make follows its `new` line as the next step.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` contrast checks judge what the page draws, and every fix line fixes its problem without making another:
  - A fix line keeps the scope of the change it answers: after a setting with `--only`, its line carries `--only`, so following it changes the part named alone.
  - The text typed in an input (its value, or its placeholder) is measured on the input's fill like any other text, with a fix line.
  - Text that sits on a part whose variants draw different grounds (a heading on the app's header) is measured on each variant's ground, and its fix line names that variant, so a fix for one leaves the others readable. A new problem on another ground is named as new.
  - A base theme's own text color on a part (butter's nav item) is what is measured, before a text token set on the part around it; a line that would change nothing on the page is not offered, and a problem no single line can fix (the same text on grounds that need opposite colors) shows with no line.
  - `show`'s `missed` list offers only lines set takes: a part whose filled variants set cannot name is left out, never given a question.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the source, descriptor and font stylesheet of a theme's app copy (`src/themes/<theme>/`) name the exact command that writes them in their first comment, `astryx experimental theme editor show <theme>`, so a missing or stale copy is fixed with that command; the built `.css`, `.js` and `.d.ts` keep the build's header.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> corners <value>` now gives `--radius-chat` back to the container radius (`var(--radius-container)`, Core's own default), so chat surfaces (the composer, its drawer, message bubbles) follow the theme's corners instead of keeping the chat radius the base theme pins (28px on most bundled themes).
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: `corners rounded` is offered the `round` rung first, as the English word says, then Tailwind's 4px: on most bases 4px alone is sharper than the corners already are.
- `astryx experimental theme`: a font family name is read as CSS reads it, so an escaped name (`Gill\ Sans`, `"\5FAE\8F6F\96C5\9ED1"`) is a family, never a font file. A font stack is read as families: a trailing comma is dropped, a stack wrapped in one more pair of quotes is unwrapped, and an empty family is refused. `--mode` is cleaned like a value, and a near typo keeps `--mode` in the suggestion. "Outline buttons red" gives the outline look with the main button in red, never a border on every filled button. "All text 50% transparent" and "the text half transparent" set the theme's text colors at that opacity. A part's padding is read on its own pieces only (a table's cells, never a command palette inside a dialog), for value questions and comparisons alike.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - "the buttons the color of the links" fills the buttons with the link color, instead of turning their text the accent color.
  - A part's fainter or muted text, said with an owner ("the card's muted text") or a place, is that part's secondary text. "the card's fainter text lighter" changes how light that text is, not its transparency.
  - "the row hovered and selected" means the row in both states at once; neither state is dropped.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - "the card's fainter text red" colors the cards' secondary text. A color after an ask on a part's text applies to that text ("the card text bigger and red"), and "fainter and red" gives a faded red.
  - A word for a look before a part ("the borderless buttons", "the text-only buttons") means the button variants drawn that way, not a border to remove.
  - "the destructive button the primary button color" uses the primary button's fill.
  - "the dialog title red" colors only the title, not the subtitle.
  - "a third darker", "darker by a third" and "half as dark" are read as the amount said, and "a third as strong" shadows are labeled softer.
  - "the input's error border" means the error version of the input.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` now decides one way, for every clause in an ask, which part it changes, in which state, and in which mode:
  - **Part:** a clause that names no part changes the part before it only when it adds to that part. That covers "with a 2px border", the part's own colon list ("cards: white background, 1px border"), "and darker", a state of the part ("; when focused a 2px ring"), and the part's own text color ("buttons blue, white text"). A font, text size, spacing or "surfaces" clause, a new sentence, or a comma item with its own look ("big buttons, thick borders") changes the whole theme. A page's text is the theme's text.
  - **State:** "when off" on a switch changes its resting look and keeps the checked one, instead of changing every state.
  - **Mode:** "in dark mode:" at the start of a sentence covers every clause in it. A mode said at the end of a run covers the run. Light/dark pairs never reach across a sentence.
  - **Light and dark colors:** on a theme with both modes, a color that one mode can't carry is not written to that mode. This applies to a light fill whose dark-mode text would not read on it (cards, a button variant, a banner, a selected row), a dark card, and a light border. A color word said for dark mode ("subtle gray in dark mode") becomes that color's dark tone. Each answer says so.
  - **Wording fixes:**
  - "green text on a black page" now sets the page black and the text green.
  - "muted text" and link colors that the dark page can't read go to light mode.
  - "navy buttons" leaves alone the variants whose text would vanish.
  - "softer corners" now means rounder.
  - **Show's missed list:** a suggestion from show's missed list never contradicts the ask, and it comes after the ask's own answer.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` answers more consistently:
  - **No rounding anywhere:** "no rounding anywhere", "square corners everywhere" and "… badges and switches too" also square the parts drawn as pills (`--radius-full 0px`), and the answer names those parts.
  - **A part and an aspect with no change** ("toast background") say what to look at instead of "No match".
  - **Thick borders on everything:** "thick black borders on everything" sets the shared border width and both border colors (inputs draw the emphasized one). It also adds a border to the surfaces that draw none (dialogs, popovers, menus). "thick borders" moves the width one pixel up.
  - **Status and focus colors:** a border color written on a part keeps the colors Core gives it by status and focus (an error input's red border, the focus border).
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - What a color is read on is the background, not the thing changed: "the warning color darker so it reads on the page" darkens the warning color until it stands out 3:1 against the page.
  - A page color's second line also paints the main panel drawn over the page. Asking for the page color alone leaves the main panel as it was.
  - "table header text uppercase 12px" keeps the 12px as the text size.
  - "when inputs are focused, a 2px ring" is the inputs' focus ring.
  - "only a bottom border" removes the other sides. "A slightly darker bottom edge" darkens that side's color only.
  - "all text at least 7:1" checks the main, secondary and accent text.
  - "large text" and "small text" make the text larger or smaller. "grayscale" and "no color" set vibrancy to 0.
  - In a look typed as one line, "deep green" is a deep green, and a quiet color like sand becomes the neutral. "A theme that works in dark mode" no longer limits the colors to dark mode. "The app should open in dark mode" points to `<Theme mode="dark">`.
  - A purpose ("so readers see which page they are on") is never read as a part. "Make text more readable" makes the text larger. "Headings a bit lighter" moves one weight step. A color named before a part ("the brown content area") describes how it looks now.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a color word is the theme's own shade where the theme has a family for it. Grey (gray, neutral) is a shade of the theme's grays, which every theme has, and another hue a shade of the palette family of that name; the shade is the one nearest the word's usual color, in each mode. A hue the theme has no family for, or a word with a shade before it ("light grey"), keeps its usual color.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "2 steps more", "3 steps rounder" and "2 spacing units more" are that many steps (never a 2px or 3px value, never a "step" part); "avatars 24x24px" sets their width and height; a warmer or cooler accent moves only its hue (and says so when the accent is a gray), never the neutral grays; "headings 2-4" and "h2 to h4" change only those levels, each from its own size; variant words after except ("except transparent ones", "except success ones") keep that variant's own fill, never an overlay; a semi-transparent background is the part's own fill (never an overlay) mixed with transparent; "primary button text the same color as the secondary button text" takes that variant's own color; "bigger than 4px" goes past the bound from the value now, or says the part is already past it; and the answer check measures a part's color in the variant a command writes.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` judges a dial step by what it does, never by its own word: "more washed out colors" answers `vibrancy less` again. A typed value waives the way only for what it writes; every other value is still measured the way asked.
- On a theme that draws both modes, `astryx experimental theme editor how` now sets a clearly dark card or surface color ("cards #0f1011", "dark cards") for dark mode only, so light mode never gets a dark card under dark text. If the same ask also gives that part its own text, as in "a navy header with white text", the look applies in every mode. A clearly light whole-theme border color ("borders #e3e8ee") is set for light mode only, so dark mode keeps its own border. Each answer says so and shows how to set the other mode too.
- Fixes in `astryx experimental theme editor how` for themes that draw both light and dark modes, and for some common wordings:
  - **Page and surface colors:** a clearly light page or surface color (typed or named, such as "cream background" or "white cards") is set for light mode only, and a clearly dark one for dark mode only. The other mode keeps its own color, so its text stays readable. The answer says so and shows how to set the other mode too. A one-mode theme, or an ask that says "in both modes" or "everywhere", sets it for both.
  - **A part hidden by a new fill:** when a part inside the one being filled would end up nearly the same color as the new fill (a primary button in a navy header), the answer names it.
  - **Link colors:** a link color one mode's page would make unreadable (a dark blue on the dark page) is set for the other mode only, and the answer says so.
  - **Prohibitions:** "never use pure black for button text" moves the button's text off black where it is black, instead of writing black.
  - **Later clauses:** "make everything more compact", "text color #303030", "; 14px text", ", larger text", "; roomier spacing" and "; main text #f7f8f8" said after an ask about one part change the whole theme, not that part. A page's text is the theme's text, never the page.
  - **Trailing modes:** a mode said at the end of a run of clauses on one part ("… white with a 1px border and a small shadow in light mode") applies to the whole run. In "black with white text in light mode and white with black text in dark mode", each half keeps its own mode and its own fill.
  - **Size words:** a size word before the thing changed ("a small shadow", "large padding") sets the amount. It no longer picks the part's size variant.
  - **Show's missed list:** a fill or text color the ask gives now comes before a line from show's missed list.
- Fixes in `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - **Status text weight:** a status part's text weight ("the error banner's text bold") is set under that status.
  - **A part inside another part:** "the dialog buttons" and "the toast buttons" mean the buttons inside that part. A part kept to a place ("menu items in the dialog", "tabs in the card") writes nothing and says why, unless a token on the place holds the change.
  - **One size named:** "the medium buttons 36px tall" sets only that size's own control height. If the part data shows no control height for the size named, nothing is written. An icon's size is reported as unreachable, and the button is left untouched.
  - **More sizes and heights:** "The small buttons taller" steps that size's own height. "The selectors 4px taller" moves each size's height. A height on the inputs ("24px tall") is set through the heights the inputs read, so they can shrink, while a text area keeps its rows. Parts inside another part ("inputs in cards") are kept to that part or not written at all.
  - **Borders:** a thicker radio or checkbox border no longer offers one color for every state.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` checks that a write shows what the question names. A state, a mode, a typed color, a removal, an except, or the thing to change (a shadow, a border, corners, padding, an on-color) that is said in a clause but missing from every step means the clause was not read. Nothing is written, and the answer says what was read and what was not. For example, "card shadows at 30% opacity" no longer fades the whole card, and "on-accent text black" no longer changes the main text color.
  Other readings:

  - **Excepts said first:** "except cards, …", "other than …" and "apart from …" before the ask are read as excepts.
  - **Lists with articles:** "the blue, the green and the red ones" names each item.
  - **Removals:** "remove X from A and Y from B" removes both.
  - **Kept states:** a kept state keeps what Core draws there ("tabs blue except the selected one").
  - **States on part anatomy:** a state goes to a part of the part's own anatomy only, never to sample content.
  - **Examples:** a "for one, add --when" example stays in the answer's words. It is never listed as a step.
  - **One-word removals:** "borderless", "un-outlined" and "shadowless" are removals.
  - **"Ones" in a list:** "primary buttons and the ghost ones" names both.
  - **Mode pairs:** "the accent darker in dark mode and lighter in light mode" answers both halves.
  - **Keeps said as unchanged:** "…, buttons unchanged" is a keep.

  `set` reads an option written after `--` with the reason and the line without `--`. `undo` reads an unquoted list of settings ("undo t accent, corners and spacing") the same as a quoted one.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` keeps excepts apart truly:
  - **Excepts on another axis:** an except on another axis ("buttons blue except the small ones") says it cannot be kept apart. Before, it said there was nothing to keep, and the excepted buttons changed anyway.
  - **Comma-led excepts:** an except set off by commas is kept, as one with no part named is.
  - **Excepts after a list:** a part-less except after a list reaches every part of the list.
  - **Kept parts of a group:** a part of a group kept from a one-mode or status step is pinned in each status and mode of that step.

  Other readings:

  - **Mode pairs:** a mode pair is one subject wherever its part is said ("the text darker in dark mode and lighter in light mode on cards").
  - **Text already at its limit:** text that is already as light or as dark as it goes says so, instead of answering "no match".
  - **Heading levels:** "keep h1" is a keep.
  - **Neither/nor:** "neither a border nor a shadow" reads its articles.
  - **Removals:** "from menus and from tooltips" takes the thing of the item before it.
  - **Lists of parts:** every ask after a list of parts reaches each part.
  - **A second ask with only its value:** "rounder and red" and "bold and red" are two asks on the same part.
  - **Neither/nor with parts as the subject:** "neither cards nor dialogs should have shadows" removes the shadow from each part, and "… should be rounded" squares each one.
  - **Excepting an item of a list:** an except naming one item of a list leaves that item out of the change.
  - **Modes said first:** "in dark mode …, in light mode darker" answers both halves.
  - **Indicators:** "indicators" are the check and radio indicators.
  - **"Every" in removals:** "remove every shadow" reads as "all shadows".

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` now judges a kept look by what it draws. In "make the inputs bolder but keep the error inputs as they are", the error inputs had no weight rule of their own. Now `how` writes back the weight they inherit and answers, instead of refusing. A kept variant that draws no border in any of its looks ("remove the border from cards except the muted ones") is kept without writing a border back on it. A word between a part and what changes that names no part, state, variant, aspect, color or known modifier ("the card zorp border") now gets "no part or word called zorp", and nothing is written.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` guards its answers, so a phrasing it was never taught gives a named refusal instead of a wrong write.
  **Guards:**

  - **Direction:** an ask that makes something fainter, less visible or more see-through, or removes it, never adds or strengthens a border, outline, ring or shadow anywhere. A way asked of a line never adds one to a look Core draws without one. Each such step is left out and named.
  - **Keeps:** every kept scope is held after the whole in-order sequence, and that sequence runs the except with its keeps.
  - A compound except keeps that variant in that state only.
  - An except's mode or state stays with its own clause.
  - Several excepts, each with its own mode, are each kept in that mode.
  - **Questions:** a question with no clause that asks for a change never writes.
  - **Unknown parts:** an unknown part is said, never read as the whole theme or given the part said before it.

  **Readers the guards point to:**

  - **Fainter borders:** a fainter border is its color at a lower alpha. A part that draws no border says so.
  - **See-through text:** see-through text is the text colors at a lower alpha, never the page.
  - **Focus rings:** a see-through focus ring is its color at a lower alpha.
  - **Table row dividers:** thicker row dividers are the width token the cells read, set on the row.
  - **Blur:** "blurrier" shadows have more blur, not more strength.
  - **Removal lists:** the items in the middle of a removal list keep its thing.
  - **Links in a place:** links in a place take the link token set on that place.
  - **Outline buttons in a color:** outline buttons in a color get no fill, with that color as their border and text.
  - **A held theme color:** a bound holds a theme color's dial and keeps a tint's alpha.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every shadow color through the one shared color reader, so themes that write 8-digit hex shadow colors (butter, chocolate, gothic, matcha, stone, y2k) get an answer to "make shadows darker", "make shadows lighter" and "the shadows are too strong", each color's alpha scaled in the form it was written.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` checks a kept look against what it drew before, wherever Core wrote it (beside the variant and size), and compares a color token by name. A status except on inputs ("make inputs blue but keep the error border", "remove the border from inputs except error inputs") now answers on every base instead of being refused. An input that has no error look of its own takes no pin. In an except or a keep, "invalid" is the error status.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads "like" and "as" as a comparison only in comparison forms ("as round as buttons", "the same padding as cards", "rounded like buttons", "like the dialogs are"): "make components like dialogs and drawers rounder" changes those parts, and "use red as the button background" sets that value. A lighter or darker color role steps its dark half the same way from its own value, and the answer check holds colors (text and borders for contrast in dark mode) and sizes to the asked way in both modes. "A light tint of the accent" is the accent mixed with transparent, never the full accent.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more of each ask:
  - **Links in a container:** "links on cards", in a mode pair too, sets the token a link reads on the card, never app-wide. Before, one half of the pair changed card text instead of links.
  - **Lookups:** every lookup is a command that runs.

  Other readings:

  - **Removals:** in "the shadow from dialogs and popovers", the items after the last "from" join it.
  - **"Give neither … a thing":** "give neither the cards nor the popovers a border" removes the border from both.
  - **Compound excepts:** "except the disabled secondary ones" keeps that variant in that state only.
  - **An ask after an except:** "taller except the large ones and bolder" answers both asks, for every part of the ask.
  - **Lists matched to a reference:** "the header and the sidebar the same color as the page" matches each item to the page.
  - **An except said before its ask:** "all text except headings red" reads as one ask with its except.
  - **Steps that change nothing:** a step that changes nothing is left out of an in-order sequence and named there. The rest still runs.
  - **Step counts:** "2 steps rounder" stays two steps in the sequence.
  - **Keeps after a comma:** "…, keep h1 and h2" is a keep.
  - **Shadow excepts:** "remove every shadow except on cards" keeps the shadow tokens on the card, so elevated cards keep their shadow.
  - **A color in a keep:** "keep disabled ones gray" names the look they keep, not a variant.
  - **Excepts in one mode:** "except in dark mode" stays with its own clause, and "except the dialog in dark mode" leaves the dialog out in dark mode only.
  - **Prohibitions of a look:** "never use rounded corners on buttons" before an ask keeps the buttons.
  - **Tone words for text:** "card text dark in light mode and light in dark mode" reads dark and light as colors.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a whole look typed as one line ("a calm, Linear-like dark theme with a violet accent", "cream background, terracotta accent, serif headings", "a high-contrast compact enterprise theme in navy"):
  - Each part it understands gets its own line: the theme's mode, a named color for the accent or the page, density, contrast and fonts. A color on its own ("navy") is the accent.
  - Words that no setting covers ("calm", "Linear-like") are listed as not used.
  - Design color names are understood (terracotta, sage, rust, mustard and others). A blue-gray is a gray with a little blue in it.
  - A complaint describes how a part looks now ("the error toast is too bright red; make it calmer"). "calmer" makes a color less saturated. "the main content area" names the page's main panel.
  - A status color on one part ("the info banner navy") also offers that status color for the whole theme.
  - "sharper corners, almost square" gives small corners.
  - "the accent text #0033aa" sets the accent text color, not the main text.
  - "a rounded font" is a typeface and leaves corners alone. A color typed with "off-white" wins over it.
  - "light only", "dark only" and "no dark mode" set the theme's mode.
  - "a right-to-left app" explains that Core mirrors itself once the app sets `dir="rtl"`, and changes nothing.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "<part> match the theme" answers with the lines `show` lists for that part under missed (what the theme's own changes should have reached on it), each checked as set checks it, and says so when nothing was missed. A color named like another part's ("grey like the dialogs", "the same grey as the page") is that part's color, read from it, and the other part is never changed. "Hard", "no blur" and "flat" shadows keep their offsets with no blur, never no shadow.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` measures more of its answer: every variant and state a touched part shows (and only the mode a one-mode theme shows), the base theme's own rules for a variant, a kept variant in every state, and a painted background whichever way it is written; the plain answer of a clause with an exception is held to the exception too. A part whose variants read colors of their own ("button text darker", "buttons lighter") gets one step per variant from its own color, in each mode. It also answers: headings smaller (each level's own size when the type dial would change weights), "the text 2px bigger", "the card border 1px thicker", sizes written "48px by 48px", heading ranges for any property ("headings 1 through 3 bolder") and an excepted level ("all headings red except h1", which keeps h1 as it is), a heading level past 6 (said), "the dialog the same color as the page" (the page's own color; the page is not changed), "no shadow and no border on dialogs" (both on that part), "0 steps more" (nothing), "everywhere except", a backdrop more see-through (a lower alpha), a dialog shadow darker, lighter or with no blur from the shadow it has, "remove the card background" (transparent), "thicker borders" from the width there now, a token pointing at another token, a dark-only theme's accent from its dark value, "rounder cards without shadows", "slightly lighter than black", and value questions about a part's font, shadow, opacity and fill, in the variant and mode they name.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` measures its answer before it gives it: each suggested command is built in memory with the theme (the same build `set` makes; nothing is written), and the values the touched parts show, in light and dark, must change the kind of thing the question asks, the way it asks (a lighter fill is lighter in both modes, while text and borders step for contrast, so in dark mode they go the other way; a removal reaches none), while parts it excepts, compares against or forbids show the same values. A command that does not is left out, and the answer says plainly why. It also reads "besides", "save for", "but keep X as they are", "X excepted" and "without changing X" as except; "as well as" as and; "compared to" and "versus" as comparisons; "don't let X get smaller" and "never round the inputs" as keeping X; "X shouldn't be so small" as an ask; "remove the padding and border" as two removals; "black on secondary buttons" as text; "less sharp" and "less thick" as their opposites; value questions about space, gap, shadow, background and font size, and a question followed by an ask; a setting pasted with a colon as its lookup; "heading text lighter"; "the focus ring lighter" as its color; and a lighter or darker accent in both modes.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` and `set` handle one-mode and scoped asks more exactly.
  - **Shadows per mode:** a part's shadow given for one mode keeps every layer the part shows. Their colors stay in the other mode and go transparent in this one, and the new layers' colors show in this mode only. Each mode paints exactly what it did, or what was asked. `set` still takes `--mode` only for colors.
  - **Core's shadow layers:** a part whose shadow Core builds from layers of its own (a card's selection ring and elevation) keeps those layers under a theme's shadow, so a card shadow, or a shadow of none, never drops the ring.
  - **One-mode removals:**
  - "remove card borders in dark mode" makes the border color transparent in dark mode.
  - "no shadows in dark mode" makes the shared shadows transparent in dark mode only.
  - A border width in one mode is refused, with the reason and the border-color line that does work.
  - **Mode words:**
  - Mode words name a mode, never a direction: "darker in light mode" is darker.
  - A mode word that scopes another ask ("more colorful in dark mode") never changes the theme's modes.
  - **See-through colors:** a see-through role color, such as a 10% wash, stays see-through when it gets lighter or darker. A border made lighter or darker in a named mode reads that mode's page.
  - **Role words:**
  - "the accent text" is the accent text token, never the main text.
  - "labels on accent buttons" are the accent-filled variant's labels.
  - **Corners by a length:** a corner step in px starts from the radius the part shows. It passes `set`, and a pill stays a pill.
  - **Gradients:** a gradient of one named color uses that color.
  - **Keeps and excepts:**
  - "…but keep the inputs" keeps the inputs.
  - An except list keeps every variant, state and heading level it names ("except primary and ghost buttons", "except hovered or disabled", "except h2 and h3").
  - **Headings:** headings made bigger never grow the body text, and headings by a px amount move each level.
  - **Comparisons with the page:**
  - "darker than the page" keeps each card variant apart.
  - "as dark as the page" takes the page's color.
  - **No undo of a removal:** a removal the theme already has is never undone.
  - **Swaps:** a swap of two role colors swaps each mode, and a named mode swaps only its own colors.
- Fixes in `astryx experimental theme editor how`, mostly for themes that draw both light and dark modes:
  - **Page color words:** a page color given as a word ("make it gray", "make the page pink") becomes that color at each mode's own page lightness. Before, one mid-tone page was used for both modes, under text that could not be read on it.
  - **Borders:** a light border on a part keeps that part's own dark-mode border color (an input's emphasized border), instead of the theme's faint line.
  - **Unchecked and unselected:**
  - "when off", "unchecked" and "unselected" keep the checked or selected look as it draws (a switch's accent), instead of writing the off look back onto it.
  - If the ask says the selected look itself ("selected tab text white, unselected tabs gray"), each look is written as said.
  - **Reading the ask:**
  - The color a complaint names ("the pink page background is a bit much, …") is how the part looks now, never a value.
  - "X instead of outlined" takes that part's own outline away, never every border.
  - "table header row" means the header cells.
  - A ban on black text after a page clause is about the text.
  - A state with a value ("primary hover #4338ca") no longer passes its state to the next clause.
  - A token list item said subject first ("text #111827") is the theme's.
  - **Button variants:** when a fill like "navy buttons" goes to some button variants only, the destructive button keeps its red, and the answer says so.
  - **Color words for dark mode:** only a color word the ask actually says ("subtle gray in dark mode") is swapped for its dark tone. A color computed from a direction ("make the card background darker") is never swapped.
  - **Links:** a link color under 2.5:1 on one mode's page is set for the other mode only ("dark red links").
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a motion effect apart from a speed:
  - **Effects:** "fade in tooltips" and "slide in dialogs" now say what the part does now, read from Core's own animations and transitions (the tooltip fades in already). Nothing is written: the editor sets how long motion takes, not which effect a part uses.
  - **Speed:** "faster" and "slower" step the motion the part has (a tooltip's animation) from the time it takes now.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a negated word as what it says:
  - **Negated words:** "un-rounded", "non-rounded" and "unrounded" buttons are square, and "un-bold" headings are regular. "border-less" and "shadow-less" are removals, with or without the hyphen.

  Other readings:

  - **Comparisons:** "as round as the accent" names nothing with a shape, so it is refused with that reason.
  - **Removals:** a list of any length gives each item its own "from", so every item is removed.
  - **Kept sizes:** "bigger except the small ones" keeps the small size only. When a keep would take the whole change back, the answer says so instead of reporting it as done.
  - **Mode pairs:** the main text gets both halves of "darker in dark mode and lighter in light mode", as do typed colors per mode.
  - **Heading levels:** "every heading except h1 smaller" leaves h1's own size token out.
  - **Titles:** "dialog heading text" colors the dialog's own title.
  - **Neither/nor:** "neither rounded nor bordered" negates both words.
  - **Fully rounded:** "fully rounded" is the roundest rung.
  - **Keeps said first:** "keeping cards, …" and "keep the accent, …" said first are keeps.
  - **Except answers:** an except answer names the whole ask it belongs to.
  - **Mode splits:** the second half of a mode split keeps the part phrase and its state ("selected tabs red in light mode and blue in dark mode").
  - **Color words:** "dark gray in light mode" is a color, not a mode.
  - **Excepts in one mode:** an except holds in a one-mode answer too.
  - **Ghost buttons:** a hovered or pressed ghost button steps its own wash, never the primary's fill.
  - **Check marks:** "check mark" is the mark drawn inside the box, colored with its text color.

- In `astryx experimental theme editor how`, a plain fill color asked of a part that has colored or status variants now changes only its neutral variants. "white cards" changes the default, transparent and muted cards, and "blue tags" changes the neutral badge. Each colored or status variant (the blue card, the success badge) keeps its own color. The answer names those variants and gives a line to change each one too.
  A color that is worked out from another color, an answer that already keeps a variant apart, and a part whose variants are roles (a button's primary, secondary and ghost) are unchanged.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more phrasings through one shared grammar:
  - **Keeping a part as it is:** "keep cards as they are", "leave inputs alone" and "don't touch the dialogs" all use one keep grammar, whether they come beside an ask or alone.
  - **Density words:** cramped, airy, dense and the other density words come from one table that every density reading uses.
  - **A fill's color after "with":** "selected table rows tinted with the accent at low strength" gives the selected state's accent wash.

  `set vibrancy` now counts a color by whether its shades change. A warm or cool gray (neutral #78716c) takes vibrancy steps. A pure gray is refused, and the message names the color and says why.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads each ask through its shared readers and holds every answer to what the theme shows.
  - **Fills:** a fill of one color is written as `background-color`, so Core's hover and press tint stays.
  - **Keeps and excepts:** one reader takes every way of keeping something as it is, in any position, and joins them into the ask's one except list. That covers "…, but keep cards as they are", "keep the dialogs as they are and …", "…, not the primary ones" and a second keep.
  - A button group cannot be kept apart from the buttons in it, and the answer says so.
  - A removed border kept when focused keeps its whole border.
  - The shared border width is kept as the token on the part.
  - **Amounts and bounds:**
  - A decimal comma is a decimal ("1,5 times").
  - An amount with a bound is held to the bound ("8px more but at most 20px").
  - "Don't make X rounder than 8px" is that bound.
  - **Removals:** "the X and Y of cards" stays on the cards, and "cards, buttons or inputs" names each part.
  - **Asks with no change:** a swap is done exactly or not at all. A part and an aspect alone ("card corners") write nothing.
  - **Modes:** "at night" and "night mode" are dark mode. A one-mode shadow on a part moves only that mode. A part that shows no shadow at rest takes a one-mode shadow. The `--mode` refusal for a shadow now says that its color can still differ by mode, through light-dark().
  - **Colors and constraints:**
  - "Never use pure white" moves only what is pure white.
  - "With readable text" pairs a label that reads on the fill in each mode.
  - Vibrancy is measured on the accent wash too.
  - A typed color wins over a color word: a typed shadow color, and a typed color for text on the accent.
  - "A lighter purple" is that hue's light shade.
  - **Named dial rungs:** "make corners small", "spacing compact" and "text size large" are those rungs.
  - **Comparisons and measured values:**
  - "4px less round than buttons" is answered.
  - A value Core writes from several tokens (a card's padding) is measured whole.
  - A px amount on a part starts from the radius the part is built with.
  - Variant pairs need two real variants.
  - **No editor theme yet:** `how` starts from, and measures against, the theme the app shows now.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - A one-line look written as a list ("clean and trustworthy like a bank: blue and gray, lots of data on screen") takes each piece a setting reads and names the words none reads. "lots of data on screen" means compact spacing. "dark purple theme" sets dark mode and a purple accent. "at night" means dark by default, and "easy to read" means larger text. "pastel pink" is a light pink, "deeper blue" is a dark blue, and "red only for alerts" sets the danger color. "dark mode first" works like "dark by default".
  - "make the blue a bit darker" changes the theme color with that hue.
  - "buttons medium weight" sets a weight, not the medium size. "headings semibold, not bold" is one ask. "large bold headings" and "bigger, bolder headings" also make headings bigger. "table headers uppercase 11px" keeps the 11px. "use the system font" sets the font.
  - A border asked for one mode on a part that draws its own shadow becomes a border whose color is transparent in the other mode.

  `astryx experimental theme editor set`: a page background on the app shell keeps a background a setting gives the main content area, whichever was set first.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads every list through one list grammar:
  - **Variants and states:** a list of any part's variants or states names each item, whether it comes before the part ("blue, teal and red cards"), before "ones", with an Oxford comma, or after "when" ("orange when hovered or pressed"). A variant name in a list is never read as a color to paint.
  - **Parts:** a list of parts ("buttons, cards and inputs rounder") gives each part the ask.
  - **Excepts and keeps said first:** an except before the ask ("make everything except buttons rounder") and a keep said first ("without changing buttons, make everything rounder") are read as excepts of the ask. The change alone is no longer offered next to an except answer.

  Other readings:

  - **Parts:** A corners step on a group leaves out the members already at that end (checkboxes rounder leaves out the radios, which are fully round already). "Card titles" and "dialog titles" color their heading. A state that only a part's items take ("side nav selected items") goes to the items. "Outlined in <color>" is a border color. "Padded" is a spacing word, and "less padded" or "less roomy" is tighter. "Drop-down" reads as "dropdown".
  - **Corners:** on a pill base, a kept variant keeps the base's pill.
  - **Modes:** "in dark mode only" scopes the ask to dark mode, and never makes the theme dark-only.
  - **Shadows:** asks how cannot measure get a true reason. A softer shadow on a part the editor has not seen drawn is refused. A one-mode card shadow change says the card draws no shadow of its own at rest.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more of each ask the way it is said:
  - **Unknown part names:** a word that names no part, in the part's place ("the zorp padding", "from the blorp"), is named in the answer, never changed for the whole theme.
  - **Status excepts:** an except by status ("except error inputs") keeps that status's border on each input that draws one. An input that draws no border of its own is left without one.
  - **Fainter text on a part:** a part's text made more transparent, less visible or fainter is its text color at a lower alpha, never the part's opacity. A toast's text uses the on-dark and on-light colors its surface gives it.
  - **Danger badges:** "danger badge" is the badge's error variant.
  - **Separators:** "separator" is the divider.
  - **Keeping the focus ring:** "and keep the focus ring" is a keep.
  - **Outline buttons on hover:** "outline buttons blue on hover" colors the main button's outline in that state.
  - **Tokens:** "tokens square" changes the tokens.
  - **Text on a part:** in "the text on primary buttons 4.5:1", the buttons hold the text; they are not the background it is measured against.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - An "all of it, in order" answer leaves out any step that would change nothing on its own. Writing such a step would lock that setting in place, so a later dial change would not reach it.
  - "no heavy shadows" removes the shadows without also saying nothing was written. "Heavy" before shadows or borders is about their strength, not the font weight.
  - Asking for a text color a part already has says it is already that color, instead of giving an unrelated reason.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a see-through color's alpha with the one shared color reader, so an `rgba()`, `hsla()` or `#rgba` overlay gets more transparent or more opaque as asked, and the check measures it the same way. After a removal, a noun with an adjective ("rounded corners") is an ask of its own: "no shadow and rounded corners on cards" removes the card's shadow and gives it round corners.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` answers from what the theme shows on bases with rules of their own. An except keeps what the part shows: a whole-theme corner change pins the corner token on the part (a button group keeps its square joins), each heading level or variant with its own value keeps it, and a kept hover keeps its fill under Core's tint. A one-mode theme answers only for the mode it shows and never adds a mode. A gradient takes the colors named, in order. A text-size step starts from the base's body size, a variant's own literal fill is stepped from, and "more colorful" keeps each mode's accent hue. "Darker than the page" holds the page as a bound in each mode. "Remove the card border and shadow" removes both, "no bigger than 4px" is a target, a part's own tokens and its base rules count in the measured check, lighter or darker text with a mode named is read the same way by the answer and the check, a shadow typed for one mode goes into light-dark(), a length typed with no way is never a spacing step, and a color clause after an ask ("focus outline on text inputs, pink #db2777") is that ask's color.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more questions through its shared readers:
  - **Lists:** a two-item list of variants or states before a single ask names each one for that ask: "primary and ghost buttons rounder", "hovered and pressed buttons orange", in an except list too. "except disabled buttons" keeps that state. An except covers the whole ask before it. A prohibition said before the ask ("never round the inputs; make everything rounder", "don't make cards rounder, make everything rounder") is read the same as one said after it.
  - **One-mode shadows:**

  - **One-mode lines:** a line the part already draws (a border, one side of it, an outline) takes its color by mode. When `set --mode` refuses such a line, it now names working steps instead of ones that repaint the other mode.
  - **Accent colors:** on a theme whose modes show a color in different hues, or that shows only dark mode, a lighter, darker, warmer or cooler accent moves each mode's colors from their own values.

  - **Hyphens:** a part or phrase written with hyphens or underscores ("focus-ring", "table_row") reads the same as with spaces.
  - **Other readings:**
  - A text-only part's color is its text color ("the top nav heading white").
  - "What color is the header" answers its fill.
  - "Bigger but no more than 20px" takes one step of the theme's scale, held to the bound.
  - "Everything serif except headings" keeps the headings' font.
  - "The hover tint stronger" changes the shared hover wash, not the page.
  - "The body text 1px bigger" steps the text size.

  `box-shadow none` on a card now also removes Core's elevation shadow. The selection ring stays.

- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads a second item after a removal as a removal only when it carries its own removal word or is a plain removable noun ("no shadows and borders"); a noun with a comparative or an adjective is an ask of its own: "no shadow and rounder corners on cards" removes the card's shadow and makes its corners rounder, and "no border and bigger padding on cards" gives more padding, never none; the removal stays on the part named.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` now writes nothing for an element named in a place it cannot be kept to ("the dialog's buttons rounder") and says why, instead of changing every such part. "The controls 40px tall" and "all controls taller by 4px" move every control height together for the whole theme, each size by the same amount.
