A shadow answer that would look the same as now (a color already at full strength) is not offered.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads each ask through one shared reader and holds every answer to what the theme shows. A kept variant or state is pinned from the base theme's own rule (a kept hover keeps Core's tint, as a variant's fill is its background color). A color word before a part names that variant ("make blue cards rounder") or is refused when the part has none ("red buttons"). One removal-list reader takes "take away the card's border and shadow", "remove the card border, shadow and background" and "remove the dialog's shadow and the card border". "dark-mode" is "dark mode". "at most", "no more than" and "a maximum of" are limits, and a limit already met changes nothing. A button's radius is written as its corner token, so button groups keep their square joins. A one-mode shadow on a part that draws a shadow in the other mode (a card's selection ring) is refused. A part given a role color keeps a readable label in every variant. Vibrancy is measured on the accent colors the theme shows. State excepts ("except disabled", "keep disabled ones as they are") go through one state reader; an except set cannot keep, or a text size that differs by screen, is said, and the plain answer is not offered. A step aimed only at an excepted variant is left out. "Darker than the page" steps past the page in each mode; a page reference is never written. A link that reads a shared text color keeps it. "letter-spaced" is letter spacing, and "side nav section headings" is the side nav heading. A refusal's own command is offered when it does what was asked, and `--at` without a picture names a command that runs.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads mode phrases, bounds, shadow strength and prohibitions each through one shared reader, and holds every answer to the measured check: "darker … in light mode" gets darker; "weaker" shadows get softer; "at least 2px", "under 40px" and "no bigger than 12px" hold the bound from the value now; "…, in dark mode" and "light mode #eee, dark mode #222" scope each value; "but leave inputs alone", "don't touch inputs" and "keep their hover the same" keep that part or state; kept parts are checked in every variant and level; a token typed with a part stays on that part; "blue card background" is the color, not the blue variant; page gradients keep the colors named; thinner borders step down from the width now; and value questions that name a mode read that mode.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: padding side words are read with the part's name taken out, so "code block padding" and "top nav padding" set every side of that part. "Card padding bigger (or smaller) than button padding" gives a step past (or under) the button's padding, never a copy of it. A dimension pair such as "16 x 16" is a size, never an amount.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part kept from a spacing change keeps its gap, padding and height ("more compact except buttons"; its own padding shorthand is not yet held, so "bigger padding except cards" says it cannot), and one kept from a border change keeps its border width ("all borders thicker except on inputs"); whole-theme shadows move from each shared shadow's own layers, in both modes or only the one named ("make shadows darker in dark mode"); a part's own gradient and its own two-mode fill step each color; a shadow by a percent scales its colors; an example value has the kind the property takes; and the answer check holds a shadow's strength and a color's see-through to the way asked.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "the current page in pagination" (and "… of the pagination") changes pagination's current button, no longer the page background. The words before "in" or "of" name a part of what follows and its state, and "current" is the state Core paints for the page you are on.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` steps a part's text in a state, such as "make the disabled button text lighter", from each variant's own color. Questions about the shadows, the text weight, the background or how strong the borders are read the theme's value and change nothing. "Make the color of the text darker" is about the text. A variant your own source pads wins over an editor padding on the part's plain rule, whatever sides that sets.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a settings entry's `only` written as text (`"false"`, `"true"`) is read as what it says, with a note, and any other value that is not true is refused with the undo that removes that entry, so `show` and the build never disagree. A theme typed after the setting (`set --color-accent '#123457' t`) is refused with the same `set` or `undo` with the theme first, never a `new` of the setting's name. `undo <theme> vibrancy` says the default vibrancy applies now. `new` with several bad dial flags suggests one command that fixes or drops each of them; `new --base` points to `--like`; `show` names a show that works and its help for an option it does not take. Dial words are read in any case (ROOMY, MORE, BOTH). `set t 'corners pill'` is read as the thing and its value. With no theme named in an app with one theme, show and undo name that theme. A preview page file that is not a regular file is named so, with what fixes it, and its page stays so the same remove runs again. Beside `--template`, a description is offered only when it relates to a page.

A change without `--png` removes it with the other pictures, and names `show --png`, which takes it again. A typeahead, whose doc requires a search source, is rendered with a sample one in the catalog the part data is read from, so its list (`typeahead-dropdown`) is recorded and `how` reads it.
- `astryx experimental theme`: an option typed before a group's real subcommand (`preview --theme t list`, `editor --mode light set t …`) is read as that: the refusal names the option and the subcommand, offers the command with the options the subcommand takes moved after it, and says which options it takes none of. An option's value is never reported as an unknown subcommand, and the line offered is the subcommand typed, never another one.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: every dash form of an option (a hyphen before a dash, minus signs) is read as the option, never glued into a value. A family spelled near a system font the build knows (`arail`, `Menol`) is kept as typed, with a note naming that font. `undo t headings wdie` removes the half its reading names. show, and undo with no history, on a damaged saved value offer its undo and set's repair beside it; a saved base in other letters or with a typo of a base that is not installed reads as that base, with its install first, in show as in a change. - `astryx experimental theme editor`: every `new` a refusal offers is checked as `new` checks its options before it is offered (a value never typed, such as a stock font, is not offered; a flag new refuses is left out and named; a line still refused is not offered), and a change of another dial is named for after the theme is made. `new` with no name offers a free name; a built-in theme among the extra words (`new t3 like neutral`, `new neutral t3`) is the base. set, undo, new, how and show read their options one way: in other letters, with one dash or a typed dash, or one slip off (`--On`, `-only`, `--olny`) they are named and the command offered with them. - `astryx experimental theme editor`: the refusal of a theme's own token values no longer ends a reason with two periods.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a padding or gap amount ("50% bigger", "20% smaller", "double", "150%") is an exact value from the one the part has now (its own setting, else its rule or the token it reads, each side of an unequal padding scaled), never a CSS percent padding; and with no amount, a part with an exact padding gets a step of that padding (said to be a step), since the spacing dial does not move an exact padding.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a theme whose palette names a palette recipe this CLI doesn't know is now refused plainly, and the file is left exactly as it is. Any other name is said to be no recipe Astryx makes, and the refusal says to set `recipe` in the file to one of the recipes this CLI knows, naming them.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a panel's text color ("the drawer text red", a bottom sheet's, an alert dialog's, a hover card's) is answered with the text color tokens its heading and text read for their color role, never a color property they paint over; a fill set on inputs lands where each member paints its box, a date and time field's two boxes included.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's conditions come from what its theming target declares. - `astryx experimental theme editor`:

  - A part kept from a corner change pins every corner token its shapes read.

  - `how` answers striped or no striped rows with the token Core paints every other row with, on the row.

  - A border on a part that draws none of its own, whose edges its inner parts draw (a date-time input), is refused, pointing to those parts; `how` reads "date and time input" as that part and answers for its date and time boxes.
  - A checkbox's indeterminate look is reachable with `--when checked:indeterminate`, and `how` adds it beside `--state checked`.
  - A text property CSS inherits, set on a part, says which parts inside it also take it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part that another component places somewhere (the current page's button in a pagination, a pressed toggle) records that place as a condition, so what that component paints it with there is never read as the part's look at rest. A ghost button reads no fill at rest, as Core paints it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: padding and corners reach the elements Core draws them on.

  - In an editor theme, a pseudo key that is no single selector is refused at its line: one that leaves a parenthesis, bracket, quote or comment open (`':nth-child(2n'`, with the closed form offered), one no browser reads, and a selector list (`':hover, :focus'`), which is named with one key per member. A plain theme's `compile` warns them, as `theme build` does.
  - In an editor theme, a custom property with capitals in a part's block is refused: the build writes a part's property names in kebab case, so `--myColor` would be set as `--my-color` while `var(--myColor)` reads the name as written. A plain theme's `compile` warns it.
  - A variable a component sets on its own element is refused in `localTokens` and in another part's block, with the part that sets it. On its own part, `var()` of that variable reads it.
  - `editor set` on a theme whose stylesheet is a named pipe gives the pipe refusal, never a failed module load.
  - A value read through an imported object's member (`all.toks`), a destructure of one, an imported function's return, or an imported typography object is blamed on the file that holds it.
  - A null value in the theme's own file builds as it is with a warning at its line, as in any theme; a null part or style key is still refused.
  - `compile` of a missing file near the theme source (`themes/t/t.theme`, `t.them.ts`) offers that source.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads more questions the way they are asked:
  - "make cards the color of the page" gives cards the page's color and never changes the page ("but 10% darker" steps that color in each mode; an amount before "lighter" or "darker" after "but" stays with the ask);
  - "make dialog shadows 50% more transparent", "20% less opaque" scale each shadow layer's own alpha, in each mode, instead of writing one alpha on every layer; a part that draws no shadow of its own says so;
  - "make borders 3:1 contrast" gives the border color at the lowest strength that measures that ratio against the page, surfaces and cards in each mode, instead of a fainter border;
  - a bound on a whole-theme ask holds: "padding bigger but at most 2px" (the base spacing step is past it) and "corners square but at least 8px" (square is 0px) write nothing and say why;
  - "make shadows use 20% black" sets each shared shadow's layers in that color, offsets kept, and a color written as a function (color-mix(…, transparent)) is never read as a "transparent" ask;
  - "what color is the text", "what color is the accent", "what is the body text size" answer with the theme's value in each mode it shows;
  - "more colorful" and "less saturated" are judged by how colorful the accents look (OKLCH chroma, the measure vibrancy moves), so a pale accent such as butter's dark yellow can be made more colorful.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` checks its answer against what the question means: a part the question only compares against ("rounder than buttons", "darker than the page") is never changed, and the answer says so; a prohibition ("don't make the cards bigger", "buttons should not be rounder") changes nothing and says what stays; a question about a value ("how much padding do buttons have", "what color is the button") answers with the value now. Comparisons write onto the first part only, with a typed offset ("4px rounder than buttons"), its variant and state, and the property the words name ("button text the same color as the card text", "input border the same color as the button background"); two parts that should match copy one value, or say they already match. "Except" keeps an exact radius change, a text size change, a variant beside a part, small and muted ones, and a state. A side border ("remove the top border"), close icons and header titles, "inputs with errors", a heading level ("red h1"), a part's own radius, text colors for two button variants, an elided second clause ("… and darker when pressed", "… and half on ghost ones") and "buttons inside cards" (the container is kept, and the answer says the part changes everywhere) are read as asked. A theme name typed in another case keeps the question.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: on an installed Core that draws a radio's circle with the pill token (`--radius-full`), squaring the pills ("no rounding anywhere", the square-corners note) keeps the radio marks round with that token at Core's value on them. On a Core that draws the circle at 50%, no pin is written. The "thick borders on everything" answer also frames the label boxes (badges, tokens).
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the cached part data is rebuilt once more, so a calendar's range band is read in a cache built before it was drawn.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the part data draws a component whose look names its value's kind (a calendar's range mode) with a sample of that kind (a range of days), so what Core draws for it, the band behind the days in a range, is read: "the calendar range band blue" sets the token it paints with on the calendar. A shadow or border asked of a part drawn inside an overlay that paints its edge for it (a typeahead's list, in its popover) points to that overlay, saying a change there reaches every one, and writes nothing.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: one reader for each kind of input, on every path.
  - A family list reads each family from its end, on the font dial, a family token and a part's `font-family`: a size, a weight or a style after a family's name (`Inter 16px`, `Inter Italic`) is refused with the family and the size's, weight's or style's own line; a bare number in a list (`Lato, 16`) is a weight only as a whole hundred; a misspelled generic (`sansserif`, `serf`, `system ui`) or, on the font dial, preset (`sytem`) is offered as that name, never saved as a family. A family the editor knows keeps its last word (`Source Sans 3`, `Arial Black 900` is Arial Black and a weight).
  - A swapped setting and value is offered only when set takes it as typed, with the scope typed, never a sample command on a part nobody named.
  - A property written with `_` or spaces (`font_size`, `"border radius"`) reads as the property, as camel case does, and gets the same answer.
  - One yes/no reader for a flag given a value and a saved `only`: the documented spellings of yes and no, or a typo of one; any other word is refused with no line guessing it. The line offered is checked as every repair is.
  - `--mode` reads a word that names one mode (`dark-only`, `darkmode`, `dark mode`) as that mode, in set and undo alike.
  - A pasted object of one entry gets that entry's repair.
  - A saved value that set repairs (`headings "blod"`, `spacing "romy"`, `text-size "16px"`) is offered that repair beside the undo.
  - A damaged base or mode is offered the lines that set it again (each installed base, each mode), never a default that drops it; a base written with `theme` (`neutral-theme`) is that base.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a typo of a font preset reads as that preset when the preset and the system family it names both match (`Verdena`, `Segoe IU`); a family near a system font only (`Times New Romna`, `Arail` in a list) is kept as typed, with a note whose line sets that font. `show` and `compile` give set's repair for a damaged saved value beside its undo, as every change does, and an entry saved in a typed form (`corners: pill`, `red --on card`) gets the reading set gives it. The editor's own printed setting line pasted back (`corners = pill (whole theme)`, `opacity = 0.5 on card`) carries its scope. A dial saved for one mode is refused as `set` refuses `--mode` on it, never built for both modes or for none. `set mode night` reads as dark only; `undo` compares colors as colors (`#F00` is the saved `#ff0000`); two headings words (`bold wide`, `bold and wide`) are one `new` line, and set's second line is the next step; a token in another style (`--color_accent`) or with a typo is offered as the token.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set` points at a line that works and says what happened. A word that names a dial and its value (`shadows none`, `elevation none`, `dark-mode true`) offers that dial's line (`set t surfaces flat`, `set t mode dark-only`) whatever the theme has now. A state a part does not have names the part drawn inside it that does ("today" on a calendar offers the line `--on calendar-day --state today`). A no-op `mode` or `base` set says nothing was built and no undo step was added, as every other no-op does. A theme with one color mode lists its own mode's token changes first.
- Receipts say what happened: `astryx experimental theme editor set` of a value the theme already has reads "font = system (whole theme) was already set; nothing changed" in place of "system -> system"; an `undo` names a setting that still applies where the removed one did ("#fef3c7 in light mode and the base theme's value in dark mode"), never the base value alone; and a theme set to one color mode says `astryx theme add <theme>` records the mode and its wiring passes it, in place of reading as a manual step. A dial already at its last rung names an exact size that goes past the rungs (`set t text-size 18`), beside the step the other way.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a refusal offers `new` to make a theme again only for a settings file `new` itself remakes; a setting listed twice gets its keep and remove lines, and a `lifted` field that is no list of text is dropped (the build writes it again). `new` repairs a value as set does: a line never adds a setting nobody typed (a mode read from a color's words), a did-you-mean reads the whole value typed, `how` is named for a value no reading makes work, and a repaired value (`ff0000` as `#ff0000`) stays in the line. Words of a flag value typed unquoted on `new` (`--font Open Sans`) belong to that value, and the line offered is checked as new checks it. show and the preview commands read their options with the one option reader, so a did-you-mean always matches the command offered. A base that is not installed leads with the install, then the set, and a theme already on a base is not offered no base. A part and its variant written in other letters together get the line that works. A corners size saved in rem is read as the px set saves it as.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` offers lines that run and do what they say:
  - A setting and value in the other order beside a mistyped option (`set t red --color-accent --mdoe dark`), or with a spaced name beside a part typo, get one line with both repairs.
  - A `var()` naming a token one letter off gets the line with the token repaired, typed and as the repair of a saved entry beside its undo.
  - `undo` naming two settings of different scopes (`undo t spacing background-color --on card`) offers one undo for each, never one that drops the other.
  - After a plain part fill, the "to fill only one of them" and "to change only its fill at rest" lines start with the undo of that fill.
  - `new --base` offers the `--like` line as `new` checks it (an install first, other flags repaired). `new --font Open Sans` with no name reads Sans as part of the font, and offers a free name. `--mode light --mode dark` together read as both modes.
  - The editor's own lines pasted back keep their repairs in the arrow form (`accent tomato -> tomatoe`), read a mode label in any case or with `mode`/`only` (`(Dark)`, `[dark only]`), refuse a mode typo with its line, and keep a printed scope in another case (`on Card`, `:Hover`).
  - A pasted entry's field keys are read in any case (`{"Thing": …, "Value": …}`, `"On"`).
  - The line that drops `--only` keeps every other scope flag.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: lines offered work as the person will run them. A `new` refused for its name keeps each misspelled value as new repairs it for a free name. A word after `--like <base>` is read into the name, never glued onto the base. A damaged saved entry's set line is offered on its own only when it replaces that entry; otherwise it is labelled as the step after the undo. A typo of a built-in base reads as that base, installed or not, with its install first (set, `new --like` and a saved base alike), and an unknown base gets `how base`, never `base none` for a theme on a base. A thousands comma reads as such on a property that takes only whole numbers (`z-index '-1,000'`), and a comma in a ratio is a pair only between whole numbers of 1 or more (`0,75` is 0.75). An undo naming several settings offers one undo each; an undo with only a scope offers a step back only when there is one. A setting pasted in the saved form, or beside its scope keys, is one setting with its scope as flags. A word after a mistyped yes/no option is left out of the line and named. The settings reader reads a saved `only` of 1 or 0, refuses a vibrancy with no color as set does, and a saved step word steps from what applies without it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a repair's offered value reads the whole typed value, never a subset of its words. A line may carry part of the value only when the refusal's other lines carry the rest (`Inter 600` gives the family and the weight, `italic bold` on a part gives the style and the weight); a part alone (`all` for `all 200`, `bold` for `extra bold`, `5` for `0,5`) is not offered.
  - A comma between digits is a decimal point (`1,5rem` is 1.5rem, `0,5` is 0.5), or before three digits after a whole number a thousands mark (`1,000` on a weight is 1000), never a split into layers.
  - Several values of one kind for a property that takes one offer the first as typed, with px only when the property takes no bare number (`line-height 1.5 2` is 1.5), and never one value of a shorthand of several kinds (`transition all 200` gets `how`).
  - `headings extra bold` offers heavy (800), and `text-size x-large` offers 24, the size CSS gives it.
  - `more` or `less` authorizes a computed value only on a dial with a scale: a token, a part property or a dial's other name given a step gets `how`, never a stock color, weight or size.
  - A saved value authorizes only a keep line for its own setting, never the setting being typed, so `base buter` no longer offers the base the theme already has.
  - A light and dark pair on a part's color in a one-mode theme gives the half that theme shows, as a token does.
  - The note about a second pasted declaration names its line only when `set` takes it, or the line `set` offers for it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: every value a refusal or a saved-settings repair offers now passes one gate, and each offered line is checked as `set` checks it before it is shown. A value may come only from these sources:
  - What was typed, under exact readings: quotes, labels and copy debris (a trailing `;`, `!important`, a comment) taken off; the same number written another way (full-width digits, a comma decimal, an exponent, rem or pt as px, a percent); CSS color names written as words (`dark red` is `darkred`).
  - A documented table: Tailwind's radius classes (`rounded-lg` is 8px), a dial's own words, a weight word, a number read as a dial's nearest rung.
  - The theme's own saved values, for a keep or unlock line.
  - The setting's documented fallback or other-direction step.
  - The correction of a typo of what was typed: one letter off for a word of five letters or fewer, two for a longer one.

  Anything else, such as a stock color, a stock shadow or easing, a reset, a default token or a nearest guess, gives `how <thing>`. A scale step (`red-500`) is no bare color.

  Also:

  - `font 'Inter 600'` offers the family and the weight separately.
  - A Google Fonts spec (`Inter:wght@400;600`) offers its family.
  - Another property's label on a part property (`padding 'margin: 8px'`) offers that property.
  - `--color-danger` offers the error token, and `--color-primary` or `--color-brand` the accent token.
  - A CSS property typed for the whole theme leads with its dial or token (`border-radius 8px` → `corners 8px`), never a part that was not named.
  - A pasted object's nested values are read, and each of its lines is checked.
  - A bare fraction on a size token gets no px guessed.
  - A very long input is near nothing.
  - `--state 'hover,focus-visible'` gives one line per state.
  - A saved light-dark pair for one mode is refused with the half for that mode.
  - A CSS-wide keyword on a token offers the undo only when the theme sets the token.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: repairs follow the readers `set` already uses.
  - A saved property name with a space or capitals (`"background color"`) is repaired by `set` in place: the line replaces the broken entry, and the theme loads again.
  - A unit typed after a space joins its number for every CSS unit (`50 %`, `50 vw`, `200 ms`, `1,5 rem`), not only px, rem and em.
  - A typo in `--when` (`variant:primray`, `siez:lg`) offers the same command with `--when` corrected. A saved one gets the undo, then that line, so the setting is kept.
  - `undo <thing> <value>` with no `--mode` is refused when the setting is saved for one mode with another value, and names the saved value and its mode.
  - `new --font 'Inter 600'` offers `--font Inter --headings semibold`, as `set` reads the same value.
  - A saved entry that names its thing under `setting`, a saved entry with the setting and value the other way round, and a saved mode of `"both"` or `""` are read as `set` reads them typed, with a note, so the theme loads.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: repairs work when followed. A damaged mode or base with a second bad value in the list leads with the fix for that value, which also saves the mode or base as meant, and no repair offers a bare `undo` that would throw away the last change. A stored vibrancy is offered as a set only when a color dial is set, and the no-effect refusal names a token color as one vibrancy does not change. `undo` with a theme name typed in another form (`tTheme`, `T`, `brand_dark`) suggests the same undo with the theme's name. A missing name with a doubled or trailing dash suggests the cleaned name that `new` takes. The tracking half of headings listed twice is undone with `undo <theme> headings tracking`, the form that works. A trailing comma or a typographic dash in `--on` (`text-input,`, `text–input`) names that part, never its whole group. A light and dark color pair on `new` offers the user's own colors per mode, never a stock color. In a one-mode theme, a doubled entry for its own mode is kept with that `--mode`, which now replaces both entries.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a reset value typed with a typo on a part property (`display nnone`, `font-weight normall`) offers that value again (`none`, `normal`), since it is what was typed, corrected.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a resting shadow on a part that draws rings in its box-shadow (an input's hover and focus rings, a status's ring) is written, and in each state Core rings it the theme's shadow comes with that ring after it, so the rings keep working; a shadow the theme sets for a state keeps its own. `how "sunken bevel on inputs"` answers with an inset bevel lit from the bottom right.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` results say what the theme does: a mode's own setting under one for every mode names the one still drawing the other modes, with its undo; an inverted surface left as the base's is given the theme's own other-mode surface (a warm dark tooltip on a cream theme), or its surface in a one-mode theme; a token set on the top bar reaches the text over its ground, and a fix for that text stays in the top bar; a container's faint border, or a hairline where the base draws one too, is a choice, and a border or secondary text that needs a fix gets the nearest color that reads, not black or white; pills are listed as missed only when the corners go square; the open problems header and the missed count say which lines exist and where each miss is listed.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` lists under missed a part where the base theme takes a role color away on its own, once the theme moves that role: the base pointing the role tokens at others there (an info banner drawn in the base's categorical blue), or a variant named for the role drawn in a color of the base's palette written out (an accent progress fill in a pale blue). Each line gives the part the theme's role color there.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: what is pasted is read as meant, and a repair carries the value given.
  - A repair never offers a stock value the input did not hold (a gray, a violet, `inter`, `system`, `1px`): a line that sets the same setting again carries the value typed or saved, cleaned, else `how` for the setting.
  - A value labeled with a word that is not the setting's own name is refused with what the word means, never set with it dropped: a mode (`accent 'dark: #2563eb'` offers `--color-accent '#2563eb' --mode dark`), a state (set on a part with `--state`), a kind of screen (not set per screen), a part (`--on <part>`), a heading level (`headings 'h1: bold'` offers `font-weight 700 --on heading --when level:1`), or a word it does not read. The setting's own name before the value is the value (`font 'fontFamily: Inter, serif'`); a camelCase or quoted label of another setting names it.
  - A size multiplied by a variable with a number fallback (`calc(0.75rem * var(--x, 1))`) is taken.
  - CSS function names in any case are read (`LIGHT-DARK(…)`); a `light-dark()` with another separator offers the comma; a font list missing the comma before its generic family (`Georgia serif`) or with a spaced generic (`sans serif`) offers the list meant.
  - A backslash before `#`, a quote or a space is taken off; a JavaScript escape in a `content` string is written as CSS writes it (`\u2022` is `\2022`); JSON arrays and design-token objects (`{"$value": …}`, `{"value": 18, "unit": "px"}`) are read as their value.
  - `headings lighter` is the weight light; two headings words give one line each.
  - The change receipt names a quote or space mark as its CSS escape, so text and JSON name the same value; a saved value in corner brackets is named as quoted, not as spaces.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: several values of one kind on a property that takes one (`margin-top '-4px -8px'`, `padding-top '1pt 2pt'`) are offered the first again, with its sign and any unit: the repair and the repair gate read "several values of one kind" through one shared reading.
- `astryx experimental theme editor …`: a saved setting that writes one field two ways (`value` and `Value`, `on` and `--on`) is read the editor's way with a note naming both, and the next change writes the field once. A pasted declaration whose unquoted value went on past a space (`set t font=Inter, Arial`) is read whole, so the line offered with the theme left out works too.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a saved font family in French quotes (`« Inter »`, with plain, no-break or narrow no-break spaces) is offered as `"Inter"`, the value set saves, not `" Inter "`.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: names saved in a spelling `--state` or `set` reads typed are read the same way, with a note naming the spelling saved. Before, every command refused the theme. This covers:
  - a part's own state in other letters or with a space, an underscore or a colon (toggle-button's `IsPressed`, `is pressed`, `is_pressed`, `:isPressed` for isPressed);
  - a CSS property in other letters (`Background-Color` for background-color).

  A state's prop name typed or saved in one case (`--state ispressed` or `ISPRESSED` on button, `isselected` on tab) is that state, as `isPressed` and `aria-pressed` already were.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: `--only` now means one thing to `set` and to the settings reader. A saved `only` on a part that is styled on its own (as another editor version saved it) no longer stops the theme from opening. It is read and built as without it, which is what it means there, and one note says so; the next change saves it so. Where that puts it at the same place as a later entry of the same setting, the later one, the one the build shows, is kept, and the earlier one is named and left out. `set --only` reads it by the same rule.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a state saved in a spelling the editor reads (`aria-pressed` on toggle-button) is named by the part's own state (`--state isPressed`) in every line the editor offers, even before a change rewrites the saved entry.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "lighter" or "darker" on a part's fill starts from the fill it shows at rest (its own setting first; never a pressed overlay), uses the amount asked and keeps a see-through color see-through. "except" keeps every excepted part or variant at the value it has now (its own shadow, its own weight) in one answer, says when a part reads none of what changes, and says when an excepted place is not a part. Sub-parts and catalog parts named in words go to that part ("dialog header", "dialog title", "code block header", "text inputs", "date pickers", "toggle buttons", "select boxes", "switches"); a sub-part Core lacks ("card header") is answered for the whole part, and the answer says so. "As round as", "the same padding as" and "match" copy the other part's value onto the first part only (an amount of it with "twice as round as"). Each clause keeps its own variant; a bare size in a list of text changes is the font size; "headings 20% bigger" scales every heading level from its own size; a font stack stays whole on the part; side words write only those padding sides; a part whose name has a state word ("hover card") is the part; "card text lighter" and "dialog text twice as big" get commands; a second part with an ask of its own keeps it; and a theme name near the one typed with `--theme` suggests the same question.
- `astryx experimental theme editor` contrast-checks a change limited to one state or condition (a selected row's fill, an info banner's fill) like any other: the part's text is measured on its fill there in each mode, and a problem comes with the nearest readable color, set on what draws the text in that state or condition, instead of a "not checked" note.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a part kept to its container ("buttons inside cards", "headings in cards", "the card title", "the button groups' dividers") is answered only with a token the part reads, set on the container, which keeps it there ("headings in cards bigger" and "the card title bigger" set the heading sizes on the card); a part's own setting would reach every one, so then nothing is written, and the answer says why.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set` and `new`:
  - A new part setting that writes the same token reference Core already uses there, at rest and in every state, such as `border-radius var(--radius-full) --on badge`, is no longer written, and the result says "[no change]". A setting whose value only matches what the part draws today, such as `corners pill --on badge` on a round badge, is written as the person's own choice, and the result says it matches and holds if that token changes.
  - The "missed" line that `new` and `set` print near the top now says what it means: each part it names, with the variant and state (or at rest), still shows the base theme's own look where your changes did not reach. Keep each one, or bring it in line with the line `show` lists for it. The JSON lists the same places as `missedWhere`.
- `astryx experimental theme`: the settings a theme's source extends are the settings module's own export, by identity anywhere up its `extends` chain, so a theme merely named like the settings is refused and one that reaches them through another theme is accepted. A source that stops loading is refused by `show` and never recorded as built. `compile` builds a family in a `font` shorthand like any font, leaves a family the app copy loads out of the full font help family by family, names a theme folder it cannot write with its fix, says in its JSON result the `--out` warnings text prints, and says that an editor theme's next set or show builds it without `--icons-specifier`. `set` and `show` give the install line for every built family nothing loads, a font token's included. A theme or an `extends` written as a helper's call or a conditional is named as what the build cannot follow, not as an inline icon registry.
- `astryx experimental theme editor show --png` cuts a family's picture taller than 1600px into pictures of at most that height, in order (`sheet-inputs-1.png`, `-2` …), each cut between parts, so a reader takes each in whole. The pictures show a looping animation (a skeleton, a pulsing dot) at a frame a person sees, a status dot in its color, a vertical divider at a height, each table, code and app shell variant on a row of its own, and a section's sample text; a deprecated part, and a closed overlay the open states draw open (the mobile navigation drawer), are no longer drawn as empty cells.
- `astryx experimental theme editor show` draws every part of the sheet and its pictures whole: a cell grows to what it holds instead of cutting variants at its bottom; a table, a code block and an app shell take the whole row; a looping animation (a skeleton, a pulsing dot) is drawn at rest; and a section or a form layout holds sample text instead of nothing.
- `astryx experimental theme editor show` shows a look's overlays open and names the parts the look leaves unchanged:
  - The sheet's overlays section draws each tooltip, popover and hover card open beside its trigger, each drawer, bottom sheet and lightbox at its cell's size, and, open, each part another section holds whose control opens a menu or list (a dropdown menu, a selector, a tab menu), in light and dark, so its pictures show how a look styles them.
  - `show` names, as `unreached`, the parts with a fill of their own the theme leaves on its base's look: no setting is on them, and their fill or text color is still the base's (for example toast, banner, badge).
  - The author-a-theme guide opens with the theme editor, and a search for brand colors finds the theme topic.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a shorthand set for one mode points to commands that change that mode only.
  - A shorthand with a color longhand (`border`, `border-top`, `outline`, `text-decoration`, `background`) set with `--mode` points to its color longhand for that mode and its other words (width, style) for both modes, so following it never repaints the other mode; a named color counts as a color.
  - A shadow's color for one mode is offered in the value as `light-dark()`: on a part with no shadow of its own, the other half `transparent`; on a shadow token, each layer's other half kept from what that mode shows, or a true reason when the layers differ.
  - `set --help` and `undo --help` say a light-only or dark-only theme takes `--mode` for the other mode, which applies where Core draws that mode.
  - A light-only or dark-only theme lists the other mode's token changes it writes.

Before, those starters were made and the new app's type check stopped at the import. A refusal that comes after the theme's stale build was made again puts that build back, so the refused command changes nothing, as it says.
- `astryx experimental theme preview app --theme` refuses a theme that imports a file only a bundler loads by a name the new app's type check has no declaration for: a CSS file with a query or a hash (`./brand.css?inline`), an upper-case extension (`./brand.CSS`), or a font file (`./brand.woff2`). Before, the new app was made and its type check stopped at that import. The declarations it reads are the new app's own (`*.css`) and the pictures Next declares. A refused command that put back a build it made first now puts back each file's and folder's times too, so a dev server or watcher sees no change.

Typography is judged by the values the build was given: a scale base with a unit (which builds `NaNrem`) is refused with the number of pixels it means, a scale with a ratio and no base is named, a family written in quotes or holding `; { } < >` is refused with the working form, and `fallbacks` is checked as part of the family list it builds. - `astryx experimental theme editor`: a `var()` is read as CSS reads it. Glued after a letter or a digit (`padding '2var(--spacing-4)'`), CSS reads no reference there, so the value is refused instead of written as a value the browser drops. Text glued after it (`'var(--spacing-4)px'`, `'8pxvar(--spacing-4)'`) is refused for the value's grammar, not as the token being the wrong kind, and the refusal no longer offers the same input again.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a `var()` with spaces inside its brackets (`background-color 'var( --color-accent )'`) is read as CSS reads it, the same as `var(--color-accent)`. Before, every color refused it as no color.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how` reads three more kinds of words as what they say: a weight word before the text it describes, however many words about the text sit between ("thin elegant headings" is the weight, never a border around every heading); "reader" and "readers", which are no longer corrected to "header", so a book-reader ask changes the theme and not the app shell header; and a CSS custom property pasted from a stylesheet, whose last words name what it sets (`--brand-bg` is a background, `--brand-text` the text color), never the prefix a codebase repeats on every one of them.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: one reading for each kind of word. A mode is read one way everywhere (the `--mode` flag, a mode label in a value, a saved entry's mode and the settings file's mode): light or dark in its written forms, or day, daytime, night or nighttime; black, white, dim and bright are no longer read as modes. A base is read one way by `new`, set and the settings file. A `new` on a base that is not installed leads with the install, then the same `new` on that base, as set does. `how` reads state words from one table. A font file in a family list is found with the one family-list reader.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "table headers" (plural) are the table's header cells, never its rows; "menus" said plainly is every menu (the menus group); a tab's underline asked for a color or a thickness ("a 2px black underline when selected") is its indicator's fill and height, never a text decoration it has no text for.
- `astryx experimental export`: the file drops the web font faces that no character in the page, its stylesheet or its script reaches, so a page with a web font is smaller.
  - A font package ships one face per script (Latin, Latin Extended, Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese) for each weight. A browser loads only the faces its text needs, but the file used to carry all of them. A page that imports a font package and never uses its family now carries none of its faces. An English page that uses two weights of a font package is 10% smaller.
  - A face stays when its font family is named outside the faces (in a rule, a token, the markup or the script) and its `unicode-range` covers a character the page can draw: one in the markup, the script or the stylesheet (a `content` string). A character written as an escape (`\u039a` in the script, `\41f` in a stylesheet) counts too, so text that a later view, a menu or a hover shows keeps its face. A family name counts as CSS reads it (`Gill\ Sans` is `'Gill Sans'`), also when the script holds it as escapes. A list or counter style with other letters (`lower-greek`, a `@counter-style`), or a `text-transform` that changes the characters (`full-width`), keeps every face of a named family, whether the stylesheet (directly or in a custom property), the markup or the script sets it. Each character's other cases count too, for `uppercase`.
  - The cut runs before the font files are read, so a dropped face is not counted in `images` and gives no missing-file or network warning.
  - Some text is not in the file, so no face is kept for it: text a reader types, text the script builds from character codes, and text the browser writes in the reader's or the page's locale (a date field's placeholder, Intl-formatted dates and numbers). Such text in a script that no kept face covers is drawn with the next font in the family list.
  - Only the exported file is cut. The theme editor's previews keep every face, so text typed into them draws in its font.
- `astryx experimental export`: a page whose root theme draws in one mode stays readable in a viewer of the other scheme. Before, the file declared both color schemes, so a dark viewer showed its dark canvas behind a light-only theme's dark text. The export reads the theme module's `colorModes` export when it has one, without running the module. Otherwise it reads the page or text colors the theme's compiled stylesheet, which the page imports (directly or through an `@import` in its own CSS), sets on its root: a light page with dark text draws in light only, and a dark page with light text in dark only. Any color the theme editor reads counts (hex, a named color, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()` and the other CSS color forms). A theme that sets neither (a fonts-only or accent-only theme), sets a `light-dark()` color (a value for each mode), sets one the export cannot fix (such as a `var()`), or sets any page or text color under a light or dark condition keeps both modes, as before. A one-mode page declares only that scheme and paints the theme's own page color on the document. For a theme passed to `Theme` unbuilt, whose CSS is injected only at run time, only what the page's own stylesheets set on that theme's root counts. A page whose theme draws in both modes, or that has no theme, is written as before.
- `astryx experimental export` treats a package that `node_modules` links to a folder inside the project (`npm link`, a `file:` dependency, a workspace package) as a package: the file no longer carries its modules as page files, so `--reverse` gives the page back exactly instead of refusing it. The page looks and runs the same.
- `astryx experimental export` reads the page's packages faster. Node looks up the package scope of every module it loads and parses a package's exports map again for each one, so a page that loads hundreds of Core's modules parsed Core's exports map hundreds of times. The export now resolves an import between two files of one installed package by its path, and reads each folder's package.json at most once. Every other import, and every import of the page's own files, resolves as before. Exported files do not change.
- `astryx experimental export` compiles the StyleX in a package that ships StyleX source, as an app's build does. A component from such a package, installed or linked in from a workspace, that uses `stylex.keyframes`, `stylex.defineVars`, `stylex.createTheme` or `stylex.firstThatWorks` used to fail with "Unexpected 'stylex.keyframes' call at runtime". Its styles now compile with the page's own class-name prefix, so they never share a class with Core's, and its animations run in the exported file. A file of the package that the page loads lazily carries its styles too. A package that ships compiled StyleX stays as it ships.
- `astryx experimental export` loads a page whose modules import a `.tsx` file by its `.js` name (`./parts/Kpi.js` for `Kpi.tsx`), which used to fail with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. `--reverse` gives back a page whose modules import any TypeScript file by its JavaScript name (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`), which it used to refuse as damaged. A file in which such an import is relative says render format 3, so an earlier CLI names the CLI that reads it instead of calling it damaged; one through a path alias (`@/lib/rows.js`) keeps format 1.
- `astryx experimental export` refuses a page that uses no Astryx components or styles, with `ERR_RENDER_NOT_ASTRYX`, exit 1 and nothing written: "page.tsx uses no Astryx components or styles; `astryx experimental export` only writes pages built with Astryx. Don't add Astryx to this app to export it: share the page with the app's own build instead (for a Vite app, a single-file build); nothing was written." The page's own script decides: a page counts as Astryx when any module its script holds belongs to an Astryx package (imported directly, through a local component or a re-export, or lazily), or when it imports an Astryx stylesheet. The theme editor's previews are unchanged.
- `astryx experimental export --reverse`: an image a carried module names with percent-escapes (`/pics/a%20b.png`, `./c%20d.png`) is expected back as the file those escapes name ("a b.png"), the file the export read and carried. Before, `--reverse` restored the file but listed the escaped name as missing and reported the restore as not exact. The export also carries such an image when the page draws it only later (after a click), so it shows from the file. An image the page imports, or loads with `import()` or `require()`, by such a name is carried and followed as written, as before.
- Outside a project, `astryx experimental export` loads a subpath that a package from its package set exports only under the `import` condition, as a theme package's `./themes/<name>` often is. Such a page used to fail as if the package were not installed. A subpath the package does not export keeps the answer it had.
- `astryx experimental export`: the warning for something the page loads from outside the file says so in the words the Checks section uses, which fit a file beside the page as well as a remote address. The share-a-page guide points to the Checks section the export prints instead of a separate reverse run.
- `astryx experimental export` warns when text inside an SVG drawing that scales to its box would show under 10 px on a 375 px phone, because the text shrinks with the drawing. The share-a-page guide says how to keep chart labels readable.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> surfaces flat`: in a mode where the theme gives a panel a fill of its own (white cards in light mode), the panel shows that fill, so its pieces (a gray badge's pill, the muted fill) stay as they are there instead of being drawn in the card's color and vanishing on it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> surfaces flat` keeps its tinted panels, and the gray pieces inside a panel drawn in the tint's color (a neutral badge, a progress or switch track) are drawn in the panel's own surface there instead, so they stay visible; colored fills keep their hue, and the emphasized border is stepped inside the panel where it would stand out less from the tint than from the panel's surface.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: under `surfaces flat`, menus, popovers, select lists, hover cards, dialogs and drawers, which float over the page, keep their own fill and get a hairline `--color-border` edge instead of the page's tint with no edge (cards and the banner keep flat's tinted look). A floating panel a theme leaves within 1.1:1 of the page with no border or shadow is now a problem, with a line that adds a 1px border.
- An `astryx experimental icon` subcommand typed alone, such as `astryx experimental icon add`, now finds icons for its name when an icon (or, with no icon set installed, an icon definition) matches the whole name, as `astryx experimental icon <words>` does, and names the subcommand's usage on one more line. Otherwise the subcommand keeps its error and names the search. Outside a project, a subcommand that needs one still refuses. A subcommand given an argument or an option runs as before.
- Icon definitions: five descriptions now name only the job the icon does. `scale` no longer describes its drawing; `wrench` no longer reads as a second `settings` (it means tools for a technical fix or setup); `cloud` drops weather; `globe` drops language, which has its own definition; and `mail` is about email rather than a message inbox.
- Icon definitions: a definition can name its `group`, the family of related meanings it belongs to (for example `notification`, `notificationActive`, and `notificationOff`), and Astryx's definitions now name theirs. A set's own definition may join an Astryx group or name its own. `experimental icon --definitions` shows each definition's group; each finder match gains `relatives`, the other definitions in its group with what each means (the text answer names a few under the first match only); with no set installed, each matching definition gains `group` and `relatives`; and a definition's docs page names its group's other members. Groups are information only: ranking does not change, and stable commands print what they printed before.
- Icon definitions can declare `replaces`: the name of an older definition they take the place of. The old name keeps answering, through every later replacement: an icon set's `map` key that uses it maps the new definition, a template's `icons` value and a definition named to `experimental icon map` or `add` mean the new one, and `astryx experimental icon <old name>` finds the icon drawn for the new one. `integration check` warns with each `map` key to rename (`icon_definition_replaced`), the next `experimental icon map` writes the new name, and `astryx doctor` warns when an installed set still uses an old key. `experimental icon --definitions` and the definition's docs page show what it replaces.
- Icon definitions: `message` no longer lists `conversation` and `textCase` no longer lists `uppercase` or `lowercase` among its words. Each of those words is another definition's name, so a search for it now lists only that definition.
- Where icon features are on (an icon-set package is installed or `experimental.iconSet` is set), the agent block that `astryx init` and `astryx upgrade` write adds one line under the runner line: "Need an icon? Run `astryx experimental icon <what it means>` and paste the import it prints, instead of copying one from a template or other code." Where they are off, the block does not change.
- `astryx experimental icon <words>` in a project with no icon set installed says so, lists the icon definitions that match (built-in names first, which Core draws with no set), and says how to get a set, in text and in `--json` (`reason`, `definitions`, `next`). `--list` gives the same next step instead of pointing back at the search, and `experimental icon use <set>` or `--set <set>` with no set installed says how to get one. After `experimental icon use <set> --variant <look>`, the search prints each match's import in that look where the icon has it, and names both looks (`look`) where it does not.
- `astryx experimental icon` ranks faster: each search works out every icon set's searchable words once and each query's forms once per pass, so its passes read every icon without rebuilding its words. Answers are unchanged.
- Experimental `exportIconIndex()` and `rankIconIndex()` in `@astryxdesign/cli/api`, the icon counterpart of `exportSearchIndex()` and `rankSearchIndex()`. `exportIconIndex({cwd, package?})` returns the icon sets `icon()` searches in a folder as plain JSON, and `rankIconIndex(query, indexes, {set?, limit?})` ranks stored indexes with `icon()`'s own ranking, so a catalog that must not load package code can store each package's index once and answer icon searches exactly as `astryx experimental icon` does. `icon()` ranks through the same function, so its answers are unchanged. An index is ranked only by the CLI version that made it.
- `astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-sets` explains icon meaning groups and `replaces` in its overview: a match lists the other meanings of its group as `relatives` without changing which icon comes first, and a replaced meaning's old name keeps answering while `integration check` names the `map` key to rename. The search example now says the set's icon for a meaning answers where the set maps one.
- `astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-sets` opens with the icon model in one place: Astryx owns generic meanings (a description and a few words each), a library maps its icons onto them inside its own package or the integration that already ships for it, with no separate add-on, a missing meaning is added in that package with `experimental icon new-definition`, and `astryx experimental icon <words>` puts the set's icon for the matching meaning first while related icons stay findable by their own words.
- With no icon set installed, `astryx experimental icon` and `astryx experimental icon --list` now name the discover search that lists icon packs when discover lists one the project could add: Find an icon pack with `astryx discover "icon set"`, install it, then run `astryx experimental icon use <set>`. To make your own set, read `astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-sets`. The finder reads the catalog copies discover saved and calls no discover source, so before the first discover run, and where no catalog lists an icon pack, the step reads as before. The JSON `next` field carries the same sentence; its shape does not change.
- Installing an icon-set package turns icon features on, with or without `experimental.iconSet` in astryx.config. A project that installs no icon-set package and sets no `experimental.iconSet` sees no change in any command, apart from the search change for experimental docs below. In a project that installs one, these stable commands now read the installed sets, so their output changes there:
  - `astryx discover`: lists each package's sets, and `--type icon-set` works.
  - `astryx doctor`: runs the `icon-sets` check and reports an invalid installed set. It runs the `icon-placeholders` check when a main set is decided: the one `experimental.iconSet` names, or the only installed set. `doctor integration validate <package>` checks an installed package's sets.
  - `astryx docs icons`: one section, added in the name of the package that ships your set, says how to find its icons (`astryx experimental icon <words>`). `astryx search` does not return it, and search output does not change.

  Copied templates still follow a set only once `experimental.iconSet` names it.

  For integration authors: `astryx search` now leaves out the sections that a doc marked `stability: 'experimental'` adds to another topic with `extends`, as it already leaves out an experimental topic. `astryx docs` still shows those sections.

  Compatibility: in a project that installs an icon-set package, `astryx discover --type icon-set --json` now lists that package instead of failing as an unknown type, so its answer no longer carries the error fields `discover-type-icon-set.json.code`, `discover-type-icon-set.json.error`, `discover-type-icon-set.json.suggestions`, `discover-type-icon-set.json.suggestions[].name` and `discover-type-icon-set.json.suggestions[].reason`. A script built on 0.7.16 keeps working: a type discover does not know still fails with the same fields, and a project with no icon-set package gets the same error as before.

- `astryx experimental icon` and the icons block of `astryx search` leave out the words that only join others (`with`, `and`) when they look for icons that carry a query's words, so `card with an icon of a star` no longer lists an icon only because its name holds `with`. A query that no whole word answers as typed is now read without them, so `user with plus` finds `user-plus` directly.
- `astryx experimental icon` names each match's meaning import when its icon set maps the icon for a definition: `meaningImport` imports the icon under the meaning name, such as `import {TrashIcon as DeleteIcon} from '…'`, so app code keeps the name `DeleteIcon` when another icon set draws `delete`.
- `astryx experimental icon` answers a query of several words that no icon matches as a whole, such as a glyph named in a phrase with the control around it. Icons that carry some of its words come back as word matches (score 20), the project's set first and, within a set, the icon carrying the rarest words first; a word that names a definition the set maps an icon for counts twice for that icon, and a word no icon carries counts for nothing. Word matches appear only in the search's own answer, and only where nothing answered before. A word written as an export name (`SearchIcon`, `ChevronDownIcon`) is also read as its words; the reading with the better-scoring match answers, so an answered query changes only when the split reading finds a better match.
- The icon-sets guide shows how to make a set inside your own app, with no other package to make, install, or publish. When the package's own package.json sets `"private": true`, the `experimental icon new-set` receipt leaves out the publishing steps (peers, the `typecheck` script, the strict check's TypeScript, the placeholder description) and its notes end with the `experimental icon use <set>` step that turns the set on. Every other package gets the notes as before.
- Icon sets: the generated icons module marks each adapter call and each theme-map element `/* @__PURE__ */`, so a bundler drops the icons an app does not use. Before, importing one icon from a set also bundled its whole theme map (and, for a set built with an adapter, every adapted icon). Modules written without the marks, or with `/*#__PURE__*/`, read the same; the next `experimental icon add`, `map`, or refresh adds the marks, keeps any mark a statement written by hand already carries, and changes nothing else. Set authors: author and check a set with this release or later. An earlier CLI misreads a module written with the marks: its `experimental icon add` and `map` drop the adapter import, its `new-set --from` refuses, and its `integration check` and `doctor integration validate <set package>` report `icon_generated_types_mismatch`. In an app on an earlier CLI, template copies, icon search and the default `doctor` run read a marked set as before; validating the set package itself fails until the app moves to this release.
- Icon definitions: two new definitions, `fullScreen` (show something full screen) and `exitFullScreen` (leave full screen), so an icon set can map its full-screen icons apart from the icons it maps to `expand` and `collapse`. `expand` and `collapse` are unchanged for now, so every set keeps answering full-screen asks with the icons it maps today; sets that map neither new definition keep working, and `experimental icon --definitions` and `integration check` list them as optional.
- `astryx experimental icon` breaks a tie between equally scored icons in favor of one whose name the query names in full, so a request for a plus icon to add a row gets `plus` before `folder-plus`. Remaining ties keep id order.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> accent <color>`: when the accent is a color far from the hue of the base theme's info, and the theme leaves info unset (a pink theme over a bright blue info), the result says info's banners and badges keep the base's color and offers an info between the two hues, so it sits with the palette and stays apart from the accent.
- `astryx` discovery lists the lab's new media players: `VideoPlayer`, `AudioPlayer`, and the `MediaPlayer` root and parts for custom layouts.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> neutral <color>`: a neutral color whose shades are the base theme's own grays (black, white, or a pure gray) now says the page, surfaces, text and borders keep their colors, and how to get dark surfaces, instead of a bare `[ok]`: a gray sets the tint of the grays, not how light or dark the surfaces are.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: text on a role fill (accent, success, warning, danger, info) where neither the theme's white nor its near-black reads at 4.5:1 now uses the end of the gray ramp on the better side (black, or white) when that reads better, so the editor's own pick no longer makes a contrast problem that a darker gray would have solved; an exact fill that then reads keeps its color in dark mode too.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> neutral <color>` says the page background follows the gray too (or keeps a page color the theme sets), as it does, and so does the neutral dial's help; a moved accent text color's note names only the grounds it fails on, with the ratio on each.
- `astryx experimental render`: a page whose script holds a long run of letters and digits, such as a large string, renders in its usual time again. The pass that finds the script's reads of images from the embedded source started a match at every character of such a run, so a page with a 1 MB string took minutes.
- `astryx experimental render` carries the page's own modules and JSON data whose names only look like configuration: `config.ts`, `lib/arc.ts`, `data/chart-config.json`, `data/config.json`. They were left out as tool configuration, so the page came back from `--reverse` with `exact: false` and without them. These names stay refused: `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.*.json`, `jsconfig.json`, any `*.config.json` or `*.config.{js,ts,…}` module, manifests and lockfiles, and dotfiles such as `.eslintrc.js`. A file that carries one says render format 2, so a CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it; 0.7.16 and earlier refuse it as damaged.
- `astryx experimental render` draws a recharts chart sized by its `ResponsiveContainer` at a set of widths, from a narrow table cell to a wide screen, and the file's CSS shows the drawing nearest the width the reader's browser gives the chart, with no script. Before, such a chart was drawn once at a guessed size and stretched to the page's width: its text was about one and a half times its size on a desktop and half its size on a phone, and a chart that filled a box of fixed height ran out of the box. The widths run from 60 to 1920 pixels, each the square root of two times the one before, so the drawing shown scales by at most the fourth root of two either way. The chart now keeps the height the page gives it (a number, the width over `aspect`, or its share of the height that the box it fills states in its own style) and fits that box whole, so its text stays within a fifth of its own size. A box whose height comes from a stylesheet gives no height to read: the chart is drawn 300 pixels high and fits inside the box, scaled down in a shorter box and with empty space above and below in a taller one. Its legend sits inside its picture, where recharts places it, and keeps the rest of its style. Each such chart carries eleven drawings, whose coordinates keep two decimal places, so it takes several times the room in the file that one drawing takes. A chart of fixed size is drawn as before.
- `astryx experimental export` checks the file it wrote and says so: whether the file's markup and stylesheets load anything from outside the file (the page's own script is not read), and whether `--reverse` gives back every carried file exactly, naming any that differ (`data.checks` in JSON). When the file stands alone, it names it as the one file to share, with its size.
- `astryx experimental export`: a large exported page that repeats an element names each repeated list of the StyleX classes Astryx's packages write (the `x…` classes) by one short class in its first paint, when those repeated lists add up to at least 16 KB; the page's own StyleX classes keep their names, so a large table or list writes a much smaller file: a 10,000-row grid goes from 52 MB to 18 MB. The page looks the same, also where scripts are blocked; its script draws with StyleX's own classes, and `--reverse` gives the page back exactly. The experimental `render()` takes `keepClassNames: true` for a caller that styles the file's markup with its own copy of the StyleX styles.
- When a page does not compile, `astryx experimental render` names the file and the line the error points at, also for a module the page imports. When StyleX cannot read a value a style imports, the message names the value and the import, and says what StyleX needs: the value written in the style, or a `.stylex.ts` or `.stylex.js` file that defines it; for a `.stylex` file it cannot find, it says to check that the file or its package is there.
- `astryx experimental export` checks its `dropped-children` warning against Core's component docs. A Core component whose docs list no `children` prop is named as the one that dropped the text, even when the text sits inside another component (`<Badge><Text>New</Text></Badge>` names Badge), and the warning points to `astryx component <Name>`. Text that the first paint does not show yet (a collapsed Banner, an inactive tab or route) stops warning only when every component around it is a Core component whose docs list `children`. A text inside a page's own component, or another package's, keeps today's warning. A warning for a text in another of the page's files names that file (`on line 12 of components/Card.tsx`). The warning's code does not change.
- `astryx experimental render` names every package the page and its own modules import that is not installed, in one refusal, before it runs the page, with one install line for all of them. An Astryx package (a theme, say) counts as installed outside a project only when the CLI's package set holds it; otherwise it is named with the rest. Before, it named only the first, so a page that needed three packages took three failed renders. The message and the install suggestion name every package. In a TypeScript module, a static import the module uses only as a type, or not at all, does not count, as TypeScript drops it; a re-export, `import()` or `require()` of the same package still counts. A JavaScript module loads every import, so each one counts. A package stylesheet that is missing is still a warning, as before.
- `astryx experimental render`: a rendered file now explains itself to whoever opens it next. A note at its top names the CLI version and render format that made it, the page's path, the files it carries and the packages it rendered with, and gives the exact commands that get the source back and render it again; a short note after the embedded source repeats the way back. `--reverse` reports the render format, the CLI version (`renderedBy`), the packages and an explicit `--title` (`title`), and, for files this version renders, whether someone changed the markup after the render (`edited`, read as a browser reads the file, so a copy whose line ends changed on the way is not edited) with each text change (`edits`: what it was, what it is now, and the restored file and line that hold the old text, in a module or the JSON data it imports, also where it wraps across lines). A file in a newer render format than the CLI reads is refused with the new `ERR_RENDER_NEWER_FORMAT`, which names the CLI version that wrote it; a file that names a CLI version that is not a semantic version is refused as damaged, so no printed command carries it, and every path a printed command takes from a received file is quoted. The render format stays 1, so earlier CLIs keep reading the files this version writes, except for a file that carries an `.mts`, `.cts` or `.cjs` module, which says format 2 so that a CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it; 0.7.16 and earlier refuse it as damaged.
- `astryx --json experimental export`: the `data.files` description also names the images a page names by a path from the site's root, which the export reads from `public/`.
- `astryx experimental render --reverse` finds a rendered file's title, styles and body as a browser does, outside comments and outside the text of the style element, so an untouched file whose stylesheet text looks like HTML, or whose page path looks like a tag, no longer reads as edited.
- `astryx experimental render` says why when no answer from the page's process reaches the CLI: the answer was sent but not received, the process ended while it sent it, or the stage it ended in, after how many seconds and with how much memory free. When the page's process cannot send its answer, the error now says so.
- `astryx experimental export`: an exported page's script reads from the first paint an image the first paint shows through `src`, `srcset` or `poster` when the page's code names it as a whole string by that exact path or https address. The file holds each such image one time fewer: a page with one 450 KB local photo goes from about 2.05 MB to 1.45 MB, and an https image the page shows through `src`, `srcset` or `poster` is held once (the same photo by an https address: about 1.46 MB to 0.86 MB). The first paint is the same, also where scripts are blocked.
- A page rendered with `astryx experimental render` carries one copy fewer of each image a page module imports (`import photo from './photo.png'`) when the file's embedded source carries it. The page's script reads such an image from the embedded source, so the script holds no copy of its own. An image the embedded source leaves out (under a dot-folder or in `node_modules`) keeps its own copy in the script, and an image the page names by a string path keeps its copy too.
- New `astryx experimental import <file.html>` turns a file `astryx experimental export` wrote back into its page, the same as `export --reverse`, which keeps working. Help, the share and export guides, the file's own note and the render's suggestions now give the way back as `experimental import`. The JSON answer is unchanged (`render.reverse`). An old `experimental render --reverse` line now points straight to `experimental import`, and an unknown top-level `import`, `back`, `restore`, `unrender` or `reverse` suggests it without running it.
- `astryx experimental export`: a link to a place in the page (`<a href="#section">`) keeps working in a viewer that shows the file in a frame given its document inline (`srcdoc`), as many artifact viewers do. There the address resolves against the viewer's own page, so the click navigated the frame away and the page vanished. Now the file moves to that place, as a browser tab does: it scrolls there, sets `:target` for the page's CSS and fires `hashchange` for a page that routes by hash. `#` goes back to the top. This also holds in a viewer that cancels such a link itself on its way down and only scrolls to the place, from a listener its own script adds on the frame's window before the file's script runs, or on the frame's document from a DOMContentLoaded listener its script adds on the frame's document before the file's script runs: tabs and navigation that route on the address switch there too, also for a link inside a card that stops the click. A link the page cancels or handles itself, from any of its own listeners (also one its modules add while they load), one with a target, and a click with a modifier key keep their own way.
- `astryx experimental render` now writes the page as a live app in one file: popovers, menus, dialogs, tabs, forms and every other control work as in the app. The file carries the page's own script, inline after the embedded source: the page's modules and the packages they use, bundled for the browser by esbuild. It paints the rendered markup first, then the script draws the live page over it. It is still one file, and the render adds no network request and no `eval`, so it works in a sandboxed frame that allows scripts, under a content security policy that allows inline scripts; a frame that blocks scripts shows the markup, and `--reverse` still gives the page back byte for byte. A link out of the file opens in a new tab, and a form submits even in a viewer frame that blocks form submission: the file fires the form's submit event itself. A page whose script cannot be built for the browser (a module it loads needs Node, say) is refused with the new `ERR_RENDER_SCRIPT`, which names the module. esbuild is a new dependency of the CLI, and only `experimental render` loads it, so no other command starts slower. The JSON adds `scriptBytes` and `scriptModules` to a render. When the page's script throws, in its render or in an effect (a frame that blocks storage, say), the file keeps showing its first paint. An image the page names by a path in a string, in `src` or `srcSet`, keeps showing once the script draws the page, and an image named in `srcSet` is carried too. A page file the page loads later (a dynamic import) that does not compile is refused as a static import is, with `ERR_RENDER_COMPILE` naming the file and line.
- The experimental command `astryx experimental render` is renamed to `astryx experimental export`. It still writes a page as one self-contained HTML file, and `--reverse` still turns that file back into its page; its options are the same, and its text output says "Export it again:" where it said "Render it again:". The old name is no alias: `astryx experimental render …` fails, exit 1, with `ERR_UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND`, and suggests the run with `export` in its place, keeping the options before it (also as a JSON error with `--json`). An unknown top-level `export`, `render`, `share`, `bundle`, `snapshot` or `standalone` suggests `astryx experimental export` and never runs it, unless the next word is a name another command reads (`astryx export Button` still suggests `astryx component Button`) or the active base does not serve the command. The guide `cli/experimental/render-pages` is now `cli/experimental/export-pages`, and the command's reference is `cli/commands/experimental-export`.
  JSON fields that carry the command name now say `experimental export`: the command's entry in `astryx manifest --json` and in `astryx --json experimental --help`, and every suggestion's `name` that names the command. The result types stay `render.page` and `render.reverse`, the error codes stay `ERR_RENDER_*`, and the `render()` function keeps its name. A file written before the rename names the old command in its note; `--reverse` reads it as before.
