- `astryx experimental render` refuses a page that imports a name its module does not export, as a build refuses it, with `ERR_RENDER_COMPILE`: "The page does not compile (src/page.tsx, line 3): @astryxdesign/core has no export Chart". It checks named imports in the page's own modules from those modules (not from a CommonJS one, which a bundler reads by interop), from Astryx packages and from StyleX variables modules (`.stylex`), and an element drawn as `<Name.Member>` whose export has no such member. It counts only names the page uses as values, so a type imported without `type` is fine, and a file the page reads as text (`?raw`) is not checked. The script's build names the file and the module the same way. An import of a package subpath the package does not export (`@astryxdesign/core/Chart`) is refused the same way: "@astryxdesign/core has no export ./Chart". Before, the render named what the missing import broke, not the import: `ERR_RENDER_FAILED` with "Element type is invalid" for a missing component, `ERR_RENDER_FAILED` with "… is not a function" for a missing function the page calls as it loads, `ERR_RENDER_SCRIPT` for a name only the script uses, and a missing `.stylex` value rendered without its style and with no error.
- `astryx experimental render`: when a page imports packages that are not installed, the suggested install line now follows the page's own package, and no line is offered where running it would install in the wrong place. The page's package decides the package manager. When its lockfiles disagree, the message names them and suggests no install, where it suggested `npm install`. For a page in another package than the folder you run from, the message names that package and the line to run there, since the line run here would add the packages to this folder's package. In a folder that no `package.json` holds, the message says to install them in the project that uses the page, and suggests no install, since an install there would make the folder a project.
- `astryx experimental export`: an exported page's script is a module script when it runs the same in strict mode, so it runs once the file is parsed: a browser paints the page before the script draws it, and on the pages measured a small page shows its first paint about 200 ms sooner on a slow phone, with about the same time until it responds. A page whose script bundles a file that is not an ES module and does not ask for strict mode (CommonJS code, or a side-effect file with no `import` or `export`), or code that reads `document.currentScript`, keeps a classic script.
- `astryx experimental export` leaves `autofocus` out of the file's first paint. The page's script owns focus once it draws the page, as the app does, so a field the page focuses still gets focus. A viewer that shows the file in a cross-origin frame no longer logs a blocked-autofocus error.
- `astryx experimental export` draws some large chart pages faster: React no longer logs each render's timing while the export draws them. A page of four charts of 50,000 points each took 42 s to render and now takes 29 s; most pages take the same time as before. The file it writes is the same.
- `astryx experimental render` names every file the page uses that the rendered file does not carry. A file left out because its name reads as a tool's configuration now gets the warning code `not-carried` instead of `not-embedded`. It says what carries the file: rename a `*.config.json`, such as `chart.config.json` to `chart-data.json`, or move the values the page reads from a tool's own file, such as `package.json`, into a file of its own. The note at the top of the file lists every left-out file on a "Not carried" line, and then no longer says the page comes back exactly. The JSON adds `notCarried`, and the text output shows it, both only when a file is left out.
- `astryx experimental render --out` accepts an absolute path in any folder, such as a folder of files to upload as an artifact. The render still never replaces a file it did not write. A relative `--out` still stays inside the current folder, and its refusal now says that an absolute path works.
- render: a page's own styles compile with their own class-name prefix, so they never share a class with Core's stylesheet. Core's rules keep their layer on Core's elements (a Table's first and last cells keep their edge padding), and a page's override of a component still wins, as in the app.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the overlays a page opens are drawn one part at a time, so a part's document listeners (a typeahead's or a menu's outside press) hear only presses on its own controls. Every editor command that reads the part data, and every sheet picture, no longer pays for each press on every other part. The part data is the same as before.
- `astryx experimental export`: more images named by a path from the site's root (`/pics/shoe.png`) show in the file and come back with `--reverse`.
  - When the project has no `public/` folder, export reads such a path from the nearest `public/` above the page, inside the project. This covers a site folder below a shared package.json. Outside a project, it reads it from the nearest `public/` above the page, inside the folder you run the command from.
  - The file now carries each such image with the page's other files, so `--reverse` puts it back in the `public/` folder export read, at the same path.
  - An image the page names this way but draws only later (after a click, in the next view) is carried too, and the file's script shows it from the carried data.
  - Export reads such a path only from `public/`. A file of that name at the project's or the page's root is no longer read, and a path that leaves `public/` (`/../x.png`) is not read. A path to a file that is not in `public/` gets the missing-image warning, which now names the `public/` folder export searched.
  - The experimental theme editor's image notes read a theme's `url(/…)` file the same way: a file at the project's root, not in `public/`, is now reported as missing.
- `astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` say that a file they cannot read cannot be read, with the reason (`EACCES: no permission`, a folder or a pipe given as the file), and the new error code `ERR_READ_FAILED`. They used to say the file does not exist, with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, which a file that is not there keeps.
- `astryx experimental export` now fetches each image a page names by an `https` address, once while the page renders, and the file carries it, so the image shows in a viewer that blocks the network. The render sends no cookies or credentials, takes only an image (by its type and its bytes) up to 8 MB, and gives each image 2 seconds to answer and 5 to arrive, and all of them 15, and asks for no more when the network answers none of the first ones. Any failure (no network, no answer in time, not an image, too large, or an address that is not `https`) leaves the address as the page wrote it and warns, naming why; an address the page's code holds that counts as an image only by a name (an object's `src`, `imageUploadUrl`) is listed, and its fetch adds no warning, when its answer is another type. The JSON result lists every address fetched and every one that was not (`remoteImages`); the text names the first ten of each and counts the rest. `--reverse` gives back the page with its addresses. A fetched image travels with the file, so anyone who has the file can see it.
- `astryx experimental export`: an https image the page shows only later (after a click, in the next view) is carried too, when the page's own code writes its address whole. That means an address an element shows as an image (an `<img>`'s or an `<input>`'s `src`, an `<img>`'s or a `<source>`'s `srcSet`, a `<video>`'s `poster`), written there or in a variable the same file reads there (`const logoUrl = '…'` with `<img src={logoUrl}>`); an address whose path ends in an image extension; or one a name says is an image: a component's or an object's `src`, `srcSet` or `poster`, or a property or attribute one of whose words names an image (`avatarUrl`, `cover_image`; not `logoutUrl`). An address written only where an element takes it for something else, such as an `<iframe>`'s or a `<video>`'s `src`, is not fetched, even when its path names an image, and the file puts no carried data there; nor is one whose path names a type that is never an image (`clip.mp4`). It is fetched with the same rules and limits as an image in the first paint, and listed in `remoteImages`. The page's script keeps every address as the page wrote it, so a link, a text, a comparison and the URL API read the page's own address. Where the browser takes an image's address (the same attributes, or a CSS `url()` in a style the script sets), the file gives it the carried data instead, so the image shows offline. An address the code gives a fragment gets the carried image too; one it gives another query (`${hero}?w=640`, or the URL API's `searchParams`) can name another image, so the file asks the network for it. A link's address written in `href`, directly or through a variable that only links read, is never fetched, even when it names an image file. An address that counts only by a name (`imageUploadUrl`, an object's `src`) can be an API's or a player's: when its answer is another type (an API's JSON, a page), `remoteImages.failed` lists it with why, and the fetch adds no warning. Any other address the script draws later warns when its fetch fails, as in the first paint. No other address is fetched. An image address the code builds from parts where a whole one would count (a template or `+` chain that starts with `https://`) cannot be carried: a `remote-asset` warning names it, its file and its line. An address built any other way is neither carried nor warned.
- `astryx experimental export --reverse` gives back a page that imports through a path alias in a project whose alias leads outside the new folder, instead of refusing it. When the file the alias reaches, and every carried file it imports where the project has it, is byte for byte the page's copy, the page uses the project's files and their copies are not written (`aliased.sameAsProject`), so export, reverse, edit and export again work in the page's own project, again and again. When that file differs or is not there, the page's copy comes back in its own layout inside the new folder, never into a folder that exists, and the answer names the file the alias reaches today and any file it imports that differs (`aliased.differs`), with the `paths` entry that leads the import to the copy. It says that entry applies to the whole project (`projectWide`) and gives the narrower fix: the relative import of the copy for each restored file that makes the import (`instead`). A file from a CLI that recorded no alias imports gets the same `paths` entry, found from the carried file the import's path ends with. `aliased.config` and `aliased.paths` now appear only when `aliased.imports` is not empty.
- `astryx experimental render --reverse` gives back a page that imports files through a path alias (`@/components/Header`) in a folder whose project has no alias for those imports, such as an empty folder holding only the HTML file. A render records which carried file each alias import named; where no alias of the receiving project names the import, the file comes back in the page's own layout inside the new folder, byte for byte. The result's `aliased` names each such import with its file, the whole `paths` the page needs to build (the entries the config has now, own or inherited, with every target the imports need), and the tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json it belongs in (the one TypeScript reads for the page, else a new one), and the text prints them. Only an import that cannot be a package name or a package's own subpath import is followed this way (`@/…`, `~/…`), so a received file can never remap a package or the reader's own imports. Such a page used to be refused as carrying "files the page does not import". Where the project's alias points outside the new folder, the restore is still refused; an import that looks like a package name (`@components/Header`), or a file from an older CLI, which records no alias imports, is still refused unless the receiving project has the alias, and the refusal now says so.
- `astryx experimental render` names at most 10 files in its text answer, then counts the rest and names the folder they share, such as "... and 190 more in page-restored/images/". A page with many images no longer prints a long line an agent must read. The JSON answer still lists every file.
- `astryx experimental export --reverse` names every file the render records as not carried as missing, so `exact` is false whenever one is. A rendered file now records the files the render left out, and the reverse adds them to `missing`. This covers a module the page imports through a path alias from outside the carried folder, which the reverse cannot resolve and used to report as exact.
- `astryx experimental render --reverse` refuses two kinds of damaged Astryx page with `ERR_RENDER_SOURCE_DAMAGED` and writes nothing, instead of answering with a page that looks fine. A rendered file cut short before its embedded source used to come back rebuilt from the part of the markup that was left; it is now refused as cut short. An Astryx page a merge left with conflict markers used to give back one side's source without a word; it is now refused, naming the conflict, so you keep the whole file from one side or render the merged page again. A file that is not an Astryx page is still refused with `ERR_RENDER_NOT_ASTRYX`, markers or not.
- `astryx experimental export` says what the file's size is made of, one line per part (`scriptBytes`, `cssBytes`, `markupBytes`, `sourceBytes`, with a note when the script is most of it), and adds `markupBytes` and `sourceBytes` to its JSON.
- `astryx experimental export` keeps a theme's rules for the parts a component draws only after the first paint, such as a Banner's icon, a tab's indicator or a dialog. Core builds those parts' class names while the page runs, so the cut now also keeps, for each name in the page's script, the class Core's naming module makes from it. Before, those parts lost their theme styles in the rendered file.
- `astryx experimental export` warns when a page gives a Core component's prop a value it does not have: `unknown-prop-value`, "page.tsx:12: Button has no variant "danger"; its variants are primary, secondary, ghost, destructive." Such a component draws no variant's look and nothing else says why. The check reads Core's own docs for the component in the page's Core (the props `astryx component <Name> --package @astryxdesign/core` shows), so an integration that replaces the component does not change it. Where a theme can add values to a prop (Button's `variant`, Banner's `status`, Link's and Heading's `color`, which take Text's colors), the values the project's themes add count too: the check reads the module augmentations in the project's own TypeScript files (a theme build's `.variants.d.ts` included) and in the declaration files of the theme and integration packages it installs. It checks only string values written in the page, for props whose type is a closed set of strings, on components imported from Core by name or through a namespace import (`<Core.Button>`). A value the page computes, a component that is not Core's, and a prop with no doc entry are not checked.
- `astryx experimental render`: a page that saves to storage or copies text keeps working in a viewer's frame that allows scripts but blocks storage or the clipboard (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`).
  - **Storage:** there, touching `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` throws, and the page went dead after its first paint. Now the file gives the page an in-memory storage that acts as the browser's does, methods and properties alike (`localStorage.theme`, `Object.keys(localStorage)`). What it saves lasts until the page closes. A file opened from disk or on a real site keeps its real storage.
  - **Clipboard:** a frame can leave `navigator.clipboard` out, refuse it by permissions policy, or refuse the write, so a page's own Copy button failed. Now the write falls back to the browser's copy command where Core's clipboard hook does. It resolves when the text was copied and rejects with `NotAllowedError` when it was not, so the page's own success and error paths run. `readText` rejects with `NotAllowedError`, as a browser does.

  The share guide now says what such a frame allows: forms, storage in memory and copying work; a cookie write throws, fullscreen and printing do not work, and a link opens only when the viewer allows pop-ups.

- `astryx experimental export` follows an import written the TypeScript way, such as `./helper.js` for `helper.ts`, to its source when it looks for the files a page uses. A module from outside the carried folder that imports one now gets that file named in `notCarried` too.
- `astryx experimental render` warns when the page asks a media query in JavaScript, with Core's `useMediaQuery` (from `@astryxdesign/core` or `@astryxdesign/core/hooks`) or with `matchMedia`. The rendered file runs no script, so readers on every screen got the layout of the answer the page had on the server, with no word why. The new `screen-query` warning names each query and says to fold the layout with CSS: `Grid` with `columns={{minWidth}}`, or a StyleX `@media` or `@container` style.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a role color the theme sets (accent, success, warning, danger, info) now reaches the parts where the base theme draws that role on its own: a variant named for the role in a color of the base's palette written out (a success badge or progress fill), a role token the base points at another color on a part (a success banner), and a color the base gives a part as its own accent written as the color itself (nav links, outline buttons). Those parts take the theme's color, the missed list no longer lists them, and a color the theme sets on the part itself stays.
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a role's text and icons (warning, danger, success, info, accent) now start from the fill the theme really shows in a mode where it sets the fill token exactly, and the note names that color and calls the text by its role (warning text and icons) instead of the dial's color and "links and accent text".
- `astryx search` no longer lists icons for an `icon` or `icons` right after `with` (only `a`, `an` or `the` between) when its results hold a component or template: `card with an icon` answers the card alone. An icon described after `of` or `for` (`card with an icon of a star`), or named before the word (`button with plus icon`), still lists the icons that answer it.
- With an icon set installed, `astryx search` answers a query that asks for an icon (`trash icon`, `SearchIcon`, or a set's name) with up to three of the installed icons that answer it, after the results: `icons` in the JSON, one line each in the text. The results and their count do not change, a search with `--type` lists no icons, and with no icon set installed every search answers as before.
- `astryx search`'s icons block names a set two installed packages ship with its package (`trash (@acme/glyphs/glyphs): …`), as the JSON `name` does, so the two lines no longer read the same. A set no other package ships prints as before.
- When an unknown top-level word such as `share` or `export` suggests `astryx experimental export`, the reason now says what the command is for, as its help line does: one self-contained HTML file from a page built with Astryx components. It used to say "a page as one shareable HTML file", which also read as an offer for pages that do not use Astryx. The command's summary in `astryx experimental --help` and `astryx experimental export --help` says the same ("Export a page built with Astryx components as one self-contained HTML file, or turn one back into a page"), and the group's example is "Export an Astryx page as one HTML file".
- `astryx experimental theme editor`: the fills that follow a surface the theme sets (cards, popovers, the muted fill) keep their place between the page and the surface, as the base theme keeps them: a dark card that is the base page's shade never turns darker than the page the theme sets.
- Twenty-one new icon meanings let templates that drew their own icon for a meaning keep it when they import icons by meaning: `copyText`, `paste`, `block`, `verified`, `alert`, `create`, `media`, `listView`, `currency`, `checklist`, `channel`, `team`, `schedule`, `help`, `signal`, `house`, `moveToFolder`, `columnSettings`, `halftone`, `groupRows` and `review`. Each falls back to the meaning the template used before, so an icon set that does not map or declare the new meaning draws the same icon as before, and the set's unmapped template meanings leave it out when the set maps its fallback. The template icon table draws `info` as the information circle; the form wizard's review banner keeps its badge through `review`, which icon sets draw as `info`.
- `astryx template` writes each icon placeholder a template imports (`DeleteIcon` from `@astryxdesign/template-icons`) as the import of the icon the template icon table names for its variant (a Heroicon, or a Lucide icon for `/lucide`), under the same name. A project with an icon set then maps it like any declared template icon. The component showcase source and build's setup notes do the same.
- The CLI ships the template icon table: for each icon meaning a bundled template draws, the Heroicon (or, for the lucide variant, the Lucide icon) that draws it. A private workspace package, `@astryxdesign/template-icons`, is generated from it, so template sources can import icons by meaning (`DeleteIcon`) and previews draw the same icons.
- Bundled templates pick each icon by meaning: the template icon test fails on an icon imported straight from an icon library, with the command that moves it. Copies are unchanged.
- Twenty-five page templates (ai-chat through kanban-board) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders. Copies draw the same icons as before: the same Heroicons and Lucide icons with no icon set, and the set's icon for each meaning with one. Icon sets' template meaning counts read placeholder imports. The docs site's code view, playground, MCP source and ShadCN registry, and the theme editor's preview sheet, use the same filled source a copy writes.
- Twenty-five more page templates (library through work-item-detail) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders. `astryx template` copies draw the same icons as before, with and without an icon set. The template icon table gains a Heroicons drawing for `wallet`, so every variant of the table draws it.
- Fifty-one block templates (AlertDialog through MultiSelector) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders. Copies draw the same icons as before, with and without an icon set. The ChatSendButton custom-icon block's send arrow mirrors in right-to-left pages, as other send icons do.
- The last forty block templates (NavHeadingMenu through VStack) import their icons by meaning from the template icon placeholders, so every bundled template now does. Copies draw the same icons as before, with and without an icon set.
- When `astryx template` keeps an icon imported from a subpath of the library an icon set wraps, its reason names that library too: `it already comes from @heroicons/react/24/solid, part of @heroicons/react, which <set> wraps`, not the subpath alone as if the set wrapped it.
- The theme editor no longer loads all of Core when it checks a theme against its base. The check copied the build's module stand-ins with an object spread, and the spread read the lazy `@astryxdesign/core` entry, so each first `new`, `set` or `how` in a process imported Core's whole root entry and React for a theme that imports only `@astryxdesign/core/theme`. The stand-ins are now copied with their getters, so the root loads only for a theme that imports it. Results do not change.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a focus-ring change that keeps a status ("make the focus ring on inputs red but keep the invalid ones") keeps that status's ring as Core draws it while focused, on every input the new ring reaches, instead of writing the status's resting shadow.
- `astryx experimental theme` reads its cached part data once per change of the cache file instead of parsing it again for every command in a process. The per-user cache of transpiled TypeScript is not read again when it has grown until its oldest copy could be removed, so a large cache no longer slows every theme command's first load.
- The theme editor (`astryx experimental theme editor`) reads the families and weights a base theme loads from its font stylesheet's own `@font-face` rules, as the built-in themes now ship them, so it keeps the base's weight notes and does not suggest installing fonts the base already loads.
- `astryx experimental theme editor set <theme> font <family>` says when the theme file covers the setting. A `typography` family or a `--font-family-*` token in the theme's own file wins over its settings, so set now names the roles that keep the file's family, the line that gives it, and how to change it, in text output as well as `--json`.
- The theme editor reads a pagination's current page as its own cell. "Make the current page in pagination blue" writes `--on pagination-item --state selected`, kept apart from every other button, instead of a `current` state on every button, and `button` no longer lists `current` as a state.
- `astryx experimental theme editor show`: a theme image named by a path from the site's root (`url(/pics/paper.png)`) that is not there now says it was looked for in `public/`, the only folder such a path is read from. Before, the note said the image was not found beside the theme.
- The theme editor knows Core's calendar range band and keyboard key badge parts. "The calendar range band" is `calendar-range`, and "range" is no longer corrected to "orange". "The key badges" are `kbd-key`; "keyboard keys", "the keyboard shortcut" and "the kbd" still read Kbd. A part that draws none of what is asked hands it to the one piece of its own inside it that draws it at rest, and names it: "make the keyboard keys gray" writes the fill on `kbd-key`. With several such parts, nothing is written and the answer names them. Spacing asked between the parts a holder lays out side by side ("more space between the keys in the keyboard shortcut", "between the tokens in the tokenizer") is that holder's gap. A fill set on `kbd` or on `calendar` was refused, because the key badges and the range band painted over it from a token; they are parts of their own now, so that fill is taken and paints the group's own box.
- `astryx experimental theme editor undo` refuses a `themes` that is a file, not a folder, by name on Node 22.13 too ("themes in this app is a file, not a folder …", with `ls -la themes` to see what is there). Before, on the CLI's oldest supported Node, it stopped with a raw "ENOTDIR: not a directory" error instead.
- `astryx experimental theme preview add <description>` adds a page only when build is sure of its start. When build starts from the app shell, or from a page its page pick gives less than a clear fit (`start.fit` under build's `CLEAR_FIT`), it refuses, says why, and offers the nearest pages this app can show by name (`--template <id>`), then the list of every page. A description that names a page by its id or display name, names an app the preview has pages for, or names a page build's ranking matches by its name or a keyword, still adds it.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how`:
  - A value no page could show, such as a line height of 0 or 99999px of padding, is not written. The answer gives the range that works instead.
  - "List items more spacing between them" points to the list's gap, not each item's padding. A visited link gets the "no visited state" answer.
  - "selected tab with a 2px underline" gives the tab underline. "the selected date in the date picker" names the calendar day.
  - When the page background is part of a longer request, the combined line also paints the frame and main panel, as the page's own answer does.
  - White text asked for the header goes to the mode where it can be read, and the answer says how to have it in both modes. Readable-text lines no longer print an empty "()".
  - "buttons font weight medium" sets a weight, not the medium size. "semibold instead of bold" is one request.

  - `astryx experimental theme editor how` writes nothing for more kinds of messages that don't ask for a change:

  - **Tag questions:** "spacing is compact, isn't that so".
  - **A question about how the theme looks now, beside a look it names:** "cards no border. is the shadow still there?".
  - **A question about what a dial does:** "what does spacing less do". The answer lists the examples in its text instead of offering them to run.
  - **Sarcasm shown by emphasis or a "yes because" reply:** "yes because neon green links are SO professional".
  - **A past hypothetical:** "had we gone with serif headings".
  - **A change timed to a later event:** "after the review, square the buttons".
  - **An ask that takes back a setting the theme doesn't have:** "accent red; also undo the corners" with no corners set. The answer says so, and asks for the rest on its own.

  Other fixes:

  - In a sequence ("make it compact, then make it roomy"), the later step now decides where it ends, instead of the two being offered as a contradiction.
  - "badges: no fill" now makes the badge see-through, including every variant the theme fills itself. It no longer takes back those fills, which brought back the base theme's solid fill.
  - A screen named by what it shows ("a records table view") no longer counts as that part.
  - A real word is no longer read as a typo of another word that differs at its first letter ("stable" is not "table").
  - "no shadows" after a part that draws no shadow ("visible focus ring, no shadows") now applies to the whole theme.
  - `set … buttons outline` (or `soft`) no longer claims that an exact text color on the button's plain rule wins on the primary button. The primary label is now measured on the fill an exact property gives that variant.

  The answer to a list of looks for a part now reads each item as part of that list:

  - A subject how doesn't know ("flurbles: subtle gray background") writes nothing and names the word. It never falls back to changing the whole theme.
  - Other design systems' names for a part now resolve to that part: a snackbar is a toast, a lozenge is a badge, and form controls are the inputs.
  - A length and a color after the part's line ("inputs: 1px border #79747e, 2px #6750a4 when focused") are that line in that state, not a fill.
  - A color word with its value after a text ask ("uppercase 12px text, gray #6b7280") is the text color.
  - A day in the date picker ("date picker: today's date circled") is the calendar's day, and gets the calendar answer instead of filling the field.
  - A state at the end of a with-item ("red background with white text on hover") applies to the whole look, so it no longer contradicts the resting fill.
  - A text color for every button keeps per-variant lines when only a hover fill comes with it.
  - A part label with padding ("dialogs: no border, 16px padding") writes the padding on that part.
  - Corners on some sides ("4px top corners and square bottom corners", "4px corners on top only") change only those corners. A step on some sides asks for a size.
  - A color said with a shape ("a #e8def8 pill") is that shape's fill.
  - "divided by 1px lines" is no longer read as a change by 1px, and "shadow-sm" is the small shadow.

  Real asks said next to a question ("set font to Inter; does that need an import?") still write.

  - `astryx experimental theme editor how`:

  - Two-word color names ("off-white", "ink blue", "grass green", "safety orange", "slate blue-gray"), tan and paper now resolve through the color table. Off-white is a warm off-white. "pure white" means exactly white. "amber for warnings" sets the warning color. A typed value said with a named color, as in "bold safety orange #ea580c accent", wins.
  - "make it calmer" and "a calm dark mode" lower vibrancy. "more cheerful" means more colorful.
  - When no command can do the whole request, the text output now says each result explains why, instead of pointing to lines "above" that appear below.
  - Tailwind shadow sizes ("shadow-sm") map to the editor's shadow sizes.
  - "dividers between list rows" and "table rows divided by 1px lines" give a bottom border. "32px rows in the menu" sets the menu item height.
  - "should be a #e8def8 pill" gives that fill with pill corners. "dialogs with a dark overlay behind them" darkens the overlay. "big touch targets" makes buttons and inputs bigger. "a 2px dark border" uses the theme's stronger border color.

  - `astryx experimental theme editor set`: a step past a dial's last rung names an exact line only where one setting does it. On a part, spacing goes on in the control height the part reads ("bigger buttons" at the top rung offers `--size-element-md 46px --on button`); the text size offers a size it takes; the whole theme's spacing, which no one setting carries, claims no exact line. A one-mode theme reads its own mode named with `--mode` (`--mode dark` on a dark-only theme) as the same as no `--mode`, in `set` as in `undo`, and says so. A control height offered past the top rung is measured from the base theme's own height, so a base with taller controls offers a taller line.

  - `astryx experimental theme editor`: a role color the theme sets now reaches a badge or other part the base theme draws for that role in a color of another family (stone's info badge in its categorical blue): the part takes the role token the base gives that same color, so its look stays and it follows the role.

  - `astryx experimental theme editor`: the fix line for a loading placeholder that does not show now offers the theme's own gray nearest the placeholder's color (else a darker or lighter shade of that color), not a plain gray.

- `astryx experimental theme editor`: a value drawn on a track (a progress bar's fill) that a theme makes vanish on it, below 3:1 at rest, is now a problem with the nearest track color that reads, set on the track alone; a slider's thumb, larger than its track, counts only where it reads neither on the track nor on the page. Before, a black border the track follows and a near-black accent left a progress bar as one black bar with nothing reported.
- `astryx experimental theme editor how <part>` names what a token shows where the base theme points it at another one on the part or a part around it (neutral's progress track reads the muted fill, which it points at the emphasized border: `shows: --color-border-emphasized`), and a border the emphasized border follows names the parts the base theme draws from it (the progress bar and switch tracks).

#### New Features

- The agent block that `astryx init` writes ends with one line on how to remove it: run `astryx init --remove-agents`, which removes it from the agent files at the project root and in the folder you run it in, and delete any other copy between its markers. Asked to take Astryx's text out of a project, agents deleted whole agent files or cut one copy by hand and left the others; with the line, they run the command and remove what it leaves.
- `astryx upgrade` keeps each theme's chat corners now that `--radius-chat` follows the container radius: it adds `--radius-chat` to the tokens of each `defineTheme()` theme (28px, or the page step of its radius scale) and the page step to each adaptation rule with a radius scale. A theme that extends an Astryx theme, or a theme this project defines (a relative or aliased import is trusted to be one), and has no radius scale of its own inherits its base's value; one that extends another theme, such as one from another package, gets a TODO that also covers that theme's adaptation rules. It leaves a TODO where it cannot read the theme, and reports a default-exported object shaped like a theme for manual migration. The token it writes is declared at the theme root, so a value a project sets on an ancestor such as `:root` no longer reaches the theme's chat surfaces: set the token in the theme instead.
- The Best Practices section of `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx hook <name>` and an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` puts a `Do:` or `Don't:` label line before each run of items with the same guidance, instead of repeating a bold badge on every item; a blank line separates runs, so each run stays its own Markdown list. Every item keeps its place and its guidance; `--json` is unchanged.
- `astryx build` lists blocks as examples to read, not sections to insert. The kit starts from the template, builds its parts with components, and shows up to three BLOCK EXAMPLES for reference. The JSON `blocks` field keeps its shape and still holds the same blocks, now shown as examples.
- `astryx build` picks which page template to start from with a second word model, once the existing model has called a page. The page-or-shell and page-or-block calls are unchanged; only the choice among page templates changes.
- `astryx build` reports `start.fit` on a page-template start: the page-pick model's probability for that template among the ready page templates, from 0 to 1. At 0.4 or more the choice is clear; below it, several templates fit about as well. It is absent for a template the word tables do not list. `--verbose` text shows it too.
- Bases, first step: a run resolves one base. The new global `--base <package>` picks it; otherwise, in an integration package, the base it is or builds on; else the project's Core; else its one installed base; else Core. A package becomes a base by declaring `base` in its integration manifest. Commands and options that need a platform step the base does not serve (theme build, add, use, remove, targets, and template; `template --skeleton` and `--cdn`; `integration add theme`; `experimental render`) are hidden from help and refused with `ERR_BASE_CAPABILITY`. Commands do not call base adapters yet, so a base other than Core serves no platform step. In a run on another base, component, hook, swizzle, template, docs, search, and codemod reads leave out Core's items and answer from the integrations that build on the base (an empty list or an unknown name). There, `build` names no Core frame or foundation components; the `hook --list` and `swizzle --list` envelopes name the active base as their package; `upgrade --from` targets the active base's installed version, runs only the codemods of integrations that build on that base (even when `astryx.config` does not list the base), checks no copied ShadCN composition (with `--registry` too), and keeps the agent-docs version `init` writes; and `doctor` checks that the active base is installed instead of reporting Core and Core's theme packages as missing. `component --list --detail compact|full` lists no integration's components, so on another base that view is empty (the base's own components appear in the default list). A project with no base-declaring integration gets the same command output as before, except that root help gains the `--base` option; the "Component style overrides" lines of theme help, and the `--json` unknown-subcommand suggestions of `theme` and `experimental`, start with an integration's `cliCommand` when one is declared, as every other printed command does; and `astryx manifest --json` gains `base`, `available` on each command and each command option, and `requires` where a command, option, or argument declares steps.
  `--base` is a global option, so `experimental theme editor new <name> --base <theme>` reads it as the base library and refuses with `ERR_BASE_NOT_FOUND`; the refusal suggests the same run with `--like <theme>`, which stays the editor's base-theme option.
- The bundled official themes export `colorModes`, the modes each draws: gothic `['dark']`, the others `['light', 'dark']`.
- `astryx docs --list` lists every docs topic: the same list that `astryx docs` prints with no topic, in text and as `docs.list` with `--json`. It used to fail with `unknown option '--list'`, while `component --list`, `template --list` and `hook --list` each list their catalog. Every other docs flag reads with `--list` as it reads with no topic; a topic or section beside `--list` is refused with `ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `docs()` takes the same `list` option.
- `astryx docs <name>` points to the right command when the name is a component, hook or template rather than a docs topic. The read still fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC`, and its first suggestion is now the command that reads that entry, such as `astryx component Button`, `astryx hook useHotkeys` or `astryx template ai-chat`. Only an exact name counts, in any case and with or without spaces and hyphens (`docs text-input` points to `astryx component TextInput`); a hook also answers to its name without `use`. The suggestion keeps the usual `{name, reason}` shape and takes the last suggestion's place, so the list does not grow. When no docs topic shares a word with the name, it is the only suggestion, instead of the whole topic list. The check reads file names first and loads no docs for other names, so a docs miss stays fast. Docs routes and docs typos get the same suggestions as before. `doctor`'s cache row names the docs not-found hint's name summaries.
- `astryx doctor` text used to print each check as a block of `id:`, `status:`, `label:`, `message:` and `fix:` lines, with the summary counts on four lines. It now prints each check as one record: its status (`[ok]`, `[warn]`, `[fail]`, `[info]`) in a column, then its id, label, message and `fix`. A legend under the heading names each field by its `--json` key, and the summary prints its counts on one line. Every field still prints, so the answer reads the same in less space: about 10% less on a small app checked with `--built`. The JSON output does not change.
- `astryx doctor integration validate` (and so `integration check`) lists each component example that is not `kind: 'setup'` but cannot run on its own, the way a docs page or catalog card runs it as a live preview: code that does not compile, such as a top-level `return` or code that stops partway (`example_does_not_compile`); code that renders nothing (`example_renders_nothing`); a name the example never defines or imports (`example_undefined_name`); an import of code that runs only on a server, an async server component it renders, or a read of `process.env` (`example_server_only`); and an import of a relative path or of a package the package does not declare (`example_import_unresolvable`). Each is a note with its fix that fails `integration check --strict --next` now and `--strict` from the next minor release, so no build that passed before fails. An example may use without importing the components its package documents, the components and hooks Core documents, React's exports, and browser globals. `previewableExample(example, scope)` from `@astryxdesign/cli/authoring` is the same rule for a tool that shows examples as live previews: it returns the module to bundle, or why the example cannot run. `integrationExampleScope(pkg)` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api` returns the scope Doctor reads a package's examples with, as JSON, so a catalog can store it and a preview tool read each example exactly as Doctor does. `showcase_not_standalone` now reads the same packages: a Node built-in name such as `events` that only `devDependencies` installs counts as server-only, because an app that installs the package does not get it.
- `astryx component`, `astryx hook` and `astryx template` now point to the right command when a name they do not find is an entry another lookup command reads, as `astryx docs` already did. One rule serves all four commands. An entry's name is its full id: a component, hook or template id, or a docs route. A name matches the typed name at one of four tiers, best first: exact (the whole name, in any case); folded (the whole name without spaces and hyphens, and a hook with or without `use`); last segment (only the last segment of a path id or docs route, exact or folded); words (the name carries every typed word). When the typed name matches another command's entry at one of the first three tiers, that command joins the suggestions by the entry's full id, such as `astryx hook useHotkeys` for `component use-hotkeys`, `astryx component Button` for `template Button`, or `astryx docs typography/font-setup` for `hook font-setup`. A better tier wins; inside a tier, a component comes before a hook, a hook before a template, and a template before a docs route; among docs routes, the route with the fewest segments comes first, then the first in tree order. The hint goes right after the command's own suggestions that match at its tier or a better one, so it is first only when none does. The list never grows: the last suggestion drops, and a hint that would come last is left out; when a command had no suggestion, the hint is the only one. Every hint names an entry the hinted command reads: a template only when `astryx template` lists it, and any route of the docs tree, namespaces included. The error code and the `{name, reason}` shape stay. Docs keeps its rule that the hint stands alone when no topic shares a word with the name, and `component` keeps its example-block message, which already names `astryx template`. Names that resolve still resolve as before, and a miss stays fast: file names and doc text say first which components, hooks, templates and docs routes can match, so only those are read.
- For AI tools that cannot run commands, `astryx mcp` serves every astryx command as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool, over standard input and output; agents that can run commands keep using the CLI. Each command that answers with `--json` is one tool, named by its words (`theme build` is `theme_build`), with the command's arguments and options as its inputs under their CLI names, and every root option except `--json` and `--version`; an input a tool does not list is refused. A tool call runs that command with `--json` in the project folder, or in a folder inside it that the call names, and answers with the command's output unchanged; a command that exits non-zero answers as an error. The tools come from the same command definitions as `--help` and the manifest, so a new command or option is a tool input at once. When the project has no agent docs yet, the server gives the agent the text `astryx init` writes. `astryx mcp --docs-only` serves only the commands that read the docs (`search`, `build`, `component`, `hook`, `docs`, `template`, `discover`, `theme list` and `theme targets`), one message at a time, without the inputs that name a folder, a file to write or a package to read (`cwd`, `path`, `cdn`, `overwrite`, `package` and `base`); the docs site's MCP server is this command. `astryx mcp --json` exits 1 with `ERR_INVALID_OPTION`, because standard output carries the protocol. `astryx docs working-with-ai` shows the client entries.
- Component docs: `playground.mobile` holds the props of a second render at a phone viewport, merged over `defaults`, for a component whose layout changes at phone width; the theme editor's part census renders it too. AppShell declares its mobile layout there (the menu button in the top bar, the open drawer); its playground defaults are unchanged.
- A command doc's option can declare `pointers`: parts of its description that help leaves out when the run's base does not serve what they name. On a base other than Core, `astryx template --help` no longer names `--skeleton` in the `--list` text or suggests `--package @astryxdesign/core`, and `astryx mcp --help` no longer names `theme targets` in the `--docs-only` text.
- `astryx component <Name>` prints a short answer by default: what the component is, its import, a usage line, every prop as one line (name, type, default, required, and its description's first sentence), its accessibility requirements, its pieces with one command that reads them all, and the commands that print the rest (`--props` for each prop's whole description, `--detail full` for anatomy, best practices, examples and theming). The same answer is `--detail compact`; `--detail full` prints the whole doc as before, and `--json` is unchanged. Every part comes from fields each component doc already has, so an integration's component gets the same answer.
- The computer-level agent text says that inside a project with its own Astryx text (an `astryx-project` skill, or an Astryx block in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md), an agent follows that text, which knows the project's version and setup. Asked a vague question about a project, agents loaded the generic computer text and missed the project's own facts.
- `astryx discover` names the sections an installed integration adds to a doc another package owns, so a reader can open its own section straight away: the list prints the read beside the doc, `docs: theme (read: astryx docs theme install-and-apply)`, the JSON entry gains `docSections` (each name's section keys, each opening with `astryx docs <name> <key>`), and the doc's item page gains `sections` and prints the same reads.
- `astryx discover` shows an installed integration's package.json `description`, as it already did for a package a source lists: on the list's Installed side and on the package page (`discover <package>`). Text shows its first sentence; `--json` carries the whole description as the entry's `description`. Terminal escape codes and control characters are removed, and a blank description is left out. Search (`discover <words>`), which already matches package descriptions, now also finds an installed package by a word in its description.
- `astryx discover <words>` matches word by word, as `astryx search` does: every word is part of the query, and an item matches by the words of its name (camelCase split), title, summary, and keywords, with its package's description adding words. So `discover chart categories` finds a `BarChart` whose summary says "Compare values across categories", which the old whole-phrase match missed. When an item matches every word, only such items are listed; matches rank by how many words they match. When nothing matches, the error suggests the Core component or hook `astryx search` gives first for the query, such as `astryx component AlertDialog` for `discover modal`, when search matches it by name or keyword. `astryx search` now prints its "More in packages you could add" line only when the `discover` command it names would list a match: discover's own search, run over the saved copy of a discover catalog, decides. With `--type <kind>`, the line names `discover <query> --type <kind>`. With no saved copy, the line prints as before. Search reads only the saved copy and never calls a discover source.
- `astryx docs <topic>` prints the topic whole, as `--json` already did, so a guide's first read carries its rules and examples. A topic whose own text is over 16 KB still lists its sections, and a whole read ends with the commands that open one section or the section list. `--index` lists the sections of any topic, and `--full` prints any topic whole.
- `astryx doctor` warns about a Core button that does nothing when pressed (`button-actions`): a `Button` or `IconButton` from `@astryxdesign/core` with no `onClick`, `clickAction`, `href`, or `submit` or `reset` type, or with an empty handler or a link that goes nowhere (`#`, unless the app routes by the URL hash), where nothing around it acts on a press. The warning names each button's file, line and label. Doctor reads the app's own source as syntax trees and leaves out test, story and fixture files. It does not report a button it cannot judge: one with props spread in, a ref, a tooltip, or a disabled or loading state, or one inside a link, a trigger prop, a custom element, a `Provider` read off a namespace import of the app's own module, or a component it does not know, or one that holds an HTML control, a custom element, another package's component other than an icon, or content doctor cannot read (`{children}` a wrapper passes in). It does not judge a workspace member's buttons when the app imports the member by its package name. When doctor cannot follow a linked folder, it treats no component as a page. When the app's own code listens for a press through the DOM (`addEventListener('click', …)`, an `addEventListener` whose event a variable names, a library's `.on('click', …)`, or an `onclick` property), doctor judges no button and reports the check as not run. Nor does it judge a component that a module may load by a path doctor cannot read (a computed `import()` or `require()`, `import.meta.glob` or `require.context`, in a module, an MDX or Astro page, or a module that does not parse), or that an MDX or Astro page names. The check never fails `doctor`.
- `astryx doctor` warns about a prop the app gives a Core component that the component does not take (`core-props`), such as `selectedID` on `TabList` or `labelHidden` on `CheckboxInput`. Such a prop does nothing, and unless the build type-checks, no build step reports it. The warning names up to eight props, each with its file, line and component and a documented prop with the same words when there is one, and counts the rest: "src/App.tsx:6 CheckboxInput has no `labelHidden` (did you mean `isLabelHidden`?)". A prop is reported only when Core's docs for the component leave it out and Core's own types, read with the project's TypeScript as its pages see them, do not take it either. The name of an HTML, SVG, DOM or ARIA attribute, which a component can pass on to what it renders, is never reported, and neither is a name with a hyphen (such as `data-` or `hx-` attributes), which JSX never checks against a props type, a prop that JSX gives every component (such as a `css` prop the project's own types declare), a prop of a component from outside Core or of a generic component, or a prop in a module compiled with another JSX runtime. Doctor reads the app's own source as syntax trees and leaves out test, story and fixture files. Without TypeScript, or in a project whose TypeScript or build config compiles JSX with another runtime, the check says it did not run. The check never fails `doctor`.
- `astryx doctor` prints a short kept-cache row. Before, the `gather-cache` row printed a paragraph of about 2 KB: every kind of kept result, when each is used, the size limit, the transpile cache, and "deleting the folder clears it". Now the row prints only the folder, its entry count and size, the command that lists every kept item and the size limits (`astryx doctor --json`), and the exact command that clears the caches, such as `rm -rf ~/.cache/astryx/catalogs`. That command also names the transpile cache folder when it exists. The JSON check keeps its whole `message` and adds an optional `brief` field with the short form, which text prints in the message's place; the legend then reads `message (or brief)`. Ids, statuses and exit codes do not change.
- With no update check recorded, `astryx doctor`'s `newest-release` row reads "Newest release unknown: no update check recorded here. Only a copy installed for the computer checks, daily in the background after a command; a project's copy changes only when the project upgrades it; a tool running its own copy picks its release." The `gather-cache` row keeps its list of what is kept, and states the CLI's build id, the lookup commands' not-found path and the size limit in short clauses. Check ids, statuses, fields, the JSON shape and exit codes do not change.
- `astryx doctor` warns when a setting of an added local theme does not show as written (a later shorthand resets it, a more specific rule of the theme it extends wins, or cascade order decides), naming the theme, the setting with its line, and the fix, from the same check `astryx theme build` runs. It is a warning, never a failure: the theme builds as before.
- `astryx init --to <places> --once` writes a copy that is saved nowhere, so no later `init`, `upgrade`, or background refresh touches it (a bundle, or a skill to upload elsewhere). `astryx init --remove` removes the Astryx skill from every place the project saved, and with `--to` from the places it names, in the project, a folder outside it, or the computer (`--remove --to user`), and drops each from what is saved; an edited skill file is kept and named. `--remove-agents` is now the same option as `--remove`; in a project that saves nothing it removes the block as before, adding one note when a folder is saved for this computer (kept, with the command that removes it), and its `init.remove` result gains `from`, `skills`, and `user`. `--once` is refused for the AGENTS.md block and for a place already saved, and a skill file Astryx did not write is kept, a linked skill folder's included, while an unedited Astryx file is the place's own through a link too (a folder saved for this computer where every file was kept is not saved; in the project, linked copy folders share one file, written and removed once); the computer-level skill and its links and copies, reached through a saved folder such as `~/.agents/skills` or `~/.claude/skills`, are kept (`astryx init --remove --to user` removes them).
- `astryx init` says what it did to each agent-doc file: `[ok] AI agent docs: AGENTS.md updated (Astryx 0.7.15 -> 0.7.16)`, `... created`, `... already current, nothing changed`, or `...: Astryx block removed, another agent file holds it`. The `init.run` receipt adds `docsChanges` (`{path, change, from, to}` per file, in `docsWritten` order); every earlier field keeps its name and value.
- `astryx init` in a project whose Astryx agent-docs blocks are all current prints the `build` and `search` commands (and where the setup guide is) instead of the five install steps, since the app is already set up. It judges the files the run writes: the `--agent-docs-path` files, the `--agent` preset's file, or every agent file at the root. A first run, or a run that refreshes an outdated block, still prints the install steps. The `init.run` receipt adds `agentDocsStatus` (`missing` | `stale` | `current`, the agent docs before the run; null when agent docs were not installed or the write failed); `nextSteps` is false when the steps are left out.
- `astryx init --to <places>` puts the Astryx skill where your agents read it: `agents-md` (the AGENTS.md block, still the default), `skills` (the `astryx-project` skill in `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` in the project, named apart from the computer's `astryx` skill so neither hides the other), `user` (this computer, the same as `--user`), or a folder written as a path. The choice is saved: in astryx.config `skills.to` for the project, so a later `astryx init` writes the same places, and in the settings file for a folder outside it, whose copy the CLI installed for the computer refreshes after each of its upgrades while it is there (delete the copy to stop it). Moving a project to another place removes the skill from the old one. `astryx init` with no `--to` and nothing saved writes exactly what it wrote before.
- An integration can say how its apps add a dependency: `installGuidance` in its manifest, one line where `{packages}` stands for the packages to add. Where the CLI prints a step that adds packages the app lacks (template readiness, `init`'s theme step, `doctor`'s fixes, theme hints and errors, `theme eject`, the theme editor's notes, and `discover`'s add commands), it prints that line instead of the package manager's command; the `template` and `theme eject` receipts carry it as `installGuidance` beside `installCommand`. Steps that move Astryx's own packages to another release, or add `@astryxdesign/cli` at the project's Core release, keep the package manager's command. Without guidance, doctor's Core and peer-dependency fixes, `theme build`'s no-Core message and `render`'s missing-package suggestion now print the project's package manager in place of a fixed `npm install`. Two different lines cancel out, and a new `install-guidance` doctor check warns. An invalid line is ignored with an `invalid_install_guidance` warning.
- An integration can ship a skill: a doc that sets `skill: {name, description}` becomes a skill of its own in every app that keeps the Astryx skill in a skills folder (`astryx init --to skills`), and the AGENTS.md block gets one line that names it and points to `astryx docs skills/<name>`. `astryx docs skills` lists every skill a folder has (the project skill, the computer skill, and each integration skill), and `astryx docs skills/<name>` reads one. `astryx upgrade --apply` refreshes integration skills and removes one an integration no longer declares, `astryx doctor` checks them, and `astryx discover` lists them. A skill that breaks a rule (its name, a repeated name, its description) is left out with a note, and its doc still loads. `agentDocs.append` keeps working as before, and a project whose integrations declare no skill gets exactly the block it got before.
- `astryx theme add`, on the first add, when an installed package names the provider that wires its themes, says so: "This app may already get its theme from <Provider> (from <module>, declared by <package>)", with the props it takes the theme and mode through. When that one provider takes the theme (its manifest's `themeProvider` names `themeProp`), every receipt that shows wiring shows that provider in place of a Theme wrap: the first add passes the generated module's theme to it (`<Provider theme={themes[defaultThemeSlug]}>`, plus `<modeProp>={themeModes[defaultThemeSlug]}` for a theme with one color mode when it names `modeProp`), a later add that first lists `themeModes` passes the mode to it when the manifest names `modeProp`, and `theme remove` of the last theme undoes those props and keeps the provider. With no `themeProp`, or two such providers, the first add names each provider and its trade-off ("Replacing <Provider> applies this theme everywhere but also drops anything else it sets up; a Theme inside it themes only what it wraps.") above the Theme wiring. No receipt reads app source. The JSON carries it as `appProvider`: each provider as `{export, from}` (with `themeProp` and `modeProp`), `wire`, and `themeProp` and `line` when the provider form applies. An integration manifest's `themeProvider` takes an optional `themeProp` and, beside it, an optional `modeProp`. `themeProvider` is a hint and never stops a manifest loading: a part this CLI cannot use (an export that is no component name, a prop that names no prop, a `modeProp` with no `themeProp`) is dropped with an `ignored_manifest_field` warning.
- For an app whose theme its integration's provider wires, `astryx doctor` names the theme a stylesheet of the package belongs to: one in that theme's own folder, or one its stylesheet imports. `astryx theme list` says on each such theme's `wiredBy` line that the provider applies when the app renders it, and that `astryx doctor` checks where.
- An integration that wires its themes with its own provider component can name it once in its manifest: `themeProvider: {export, from}`. `astryx doctor` then counts the package's theme as wired when the app renders that component (the theme whose stylesheet the app imports, or the package's only theme), instead of warning that no theme is wired, and its CLI-managed-themes check names the theme and its provider instead of offering `theme add`. An import of the provider that is never rendered still does not count. A stylesheet the app imports from the package counts as the theme it is, wherever the package keeps it; doctor names it, and never calls it missing when it cannot match it to one theme. `astryx theme list` shows `wiredBy` beside each of the package's themes, in text and JSON; its added and default marks stay as they are. A CLI that does not know the key, or a key inside it, ignores it with a warning and keeps the rest of the manifest.
- When `astryx component` or `astryx template` finds no entry, the not-found error also points to a hook the name nearly spells or names by meaning. A `use…` name one or two slips from a hook's name, or one whose every word that hook's name carries (`useTableExpansion` for `useTableRowExpansion`), suggests that hook (`astryx hook <name>`). For `astryx component`, a name of two or more words that are exactly a keyword one hook's doc declares (`CopyButton` for a hook whose doc lists `copy button`) suggests that hook. The hint goes first only when no own suggestion matches as well: a suggestion whose name nearly spells the typed name or carries every typed word, or a component whose doc keywords or search-card synonyms hold the same phrase, stays ahead of it. The list never grows, the lookup still fails, and a name that already matches another command's entry by name keeps that hint.
- Palette generation has a second recipe, `astryx-oklch-v2`, beside `astryx-oklch-v1`: its pale stops, where a vivid seed asks more than the sRGB gamut holds, follow the vibrancy and each seed's own chroma instead of all landing on the gamut's edge, and a dusty seed stays dusty there; the dark side of a ramp, and every pale stop whose gamut holds the most vivid seed at the default vibrancy, are drawn exactly as v1 draws them, so role text and dark fills keep their strength. New palettes name v2: `astryx experimental theme editor` records `"recipe": "astryx-oklch-v2"` in each palette config it makes, and the palette guide's example config names it. A request or config that names no recipe still runs v1, from `generateTonalPalette()` and `astryx theme palette generate` alike, so existing callers, the shipped themes' palettes and any existing config keep their colors; a config keeps the recipe it records, and naming one pins it. A theme the editor saved before keeps the recipe it was made with, and a color change on it says how to move it.
- `astryx component <Name>` (and its `--props` view) lists props one per line, ``- `name`: `type` = `default` - description``, with the required and experimental markers after the type, instead of a four-column table. Union types keep their pipes as written, and no field is dropped; `--json` is unchanged.
- `astryx component <Name>` prints the first sentence of each prop's description, under one line naming the command that prints them whole: the read's own selector and `--package` scope with `--props`, so it resolves to the same component. A read prints its descriptions whole when that line would cost more than the cut saves. The `--props` view, `--json` and `astryx discover` keep every description whole.
- `astryx search` prints the first sentence of each result's description instead of the whole description, so a list of 20 results stays short. Component, hook and doc results' commands print the full doc; `--verbose` and `--json` keep descriptions whole.
- Every `--json` result that lists or returns a template gives it `isReady`: false for a template whose doc sets `isReady: false`, else true. `discover`, which names a package's templates only by id, carries neither. That covers `search` results, `build`'s start, alternatives, pages and blocks, `template <id>` (shown, `--skeleton`, and copied), and `component <Name> --blocks`; `template --list` already had it. In text, those commands mark an unready template `(not ready)`, and `template --list` says `(not ready)` instead of `(WIP)`. Search still lists an unready template in the same place.
- In an Astryx project, and outside any package, `astryx search` finds the experimental guides for sharing a page as one HTML file. A search for words like "share", "single file", "static html", "snapshot" or "artifact" now returns them, one entry per guide, and each says it is experimental; every other experimental doc still stays out of search, and in a package without Astryx search answers as before. A reference doc gains the optional field `searchable: true`, which only these CLI guides may set.
- Outside a project, when a tool runs the CLI for you from its own package set, a page can use the other packages that set's `package.json` lists, such as an icon library, as it already uses Astryx, React and StyleX. `render` renders a scaffolded template page with nothing to install, and `template` no longer asks you to install those packages there. Before, `template` printed an `npm install` step for the template's icon library, and `render` stopped until you ran it. In a folder with no `package.json`, `template`, `build` and `theme eject` now name a package that nothing provides as missing, for the project that uses the page, instead of printing an install step that would turn the folder into a project.
- `astryx upgrade` rewrites the deprecated `swipeActions` and `swipeBehavior` props of `Item` and `ListItem` to `swipe={…}` where each entry is an object literal. It defines each swipe once with `createSwipe`. The definition goes to module scope when every value outside a handler is fixed at import: a literal, a JSX element, an import or a module `const`. It goes into `useMemo` in the enclosing component or hook when the options read its props or state. A function counts as one when it is declared or assigned under a capitalized or `use…` name, directly or through `memo` or `forwardRef`. Each entry with no `id` takes one named after its label or handler, else its side and place, with a TODO. On a `ListItem`, a handler that compares the row's `itemKey` value with `===` or `!==` takes it from `onActivate` instead. Where it cannot define a swipe once, it keeps `createSwipe` on the row and leaves a TODO. That covers options that read a map callback's value, a ref's `current` or a local assigned after its declaration. It covers a local they read at render when code sets, updates or deletes a property read from it. A method called on such a local counts too, and so does passing it to a call, naming it again, storing it or returning it. It also covers options that call or read at render something that is neither fixed nor one of the component's own props, state or locals. The codemod assumes that props, state and hook results are not changed in place, as React's rules and the React Compiler assume. Only an entry's `onActivate` runs when the action fires; any other callback in the options runs at render. On an `Item`, that TODO says an `Item` passes no `itemKey`. It reports, and leaves unchanged, a value whose entries it cannot see and a JSX spread that may carry the props. It migrates a condition only when it can read every id and prove both swipes key alike exactly where the deprecated props did. Otherwise it leaves the condition unchanged, with a TODO.
- The `table` and `incident-console` page templates are ready, so build can start from them.
- The markdown tables in `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx hook <name>` and an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` use a three-dash rule under each header cell (`|---|---|`) instead of a rule as wide as the header text. Tables render the same in markdown.
- The `table` page template now builds what its description promises: sortable columns, row selection into a bulk-action toolbar, and a per-row overflow menu, with a confirm step before removing members. It stays unlisted (`isReady: false`) for now.
- `astryx template <name> <path>` names the components the written file uses in one line right after `Copied template to ...`: `Read the components it uses in one call: astryx component A B C`, so an agent reads them all in one call instead of one at a time. `astryx template <name>` prints the same line to stderr, so stdout stays the source. The names are the ones `astryx component` answers in the project (Core's and each configured integration's), in the order the file first renders them, each once, and in a project with an integration each is written as `<package>/<Name>` for the package its import names, so the read never opens another package's component; a chart library's parts and the file's own helpers are left out, and nothing prints when none are left. `--json` carries them as `components` on the `template.copy` receipt and as `componentsToRead` on `template.show`; every existing field is unchanged.
- `astryx template --list` prints the first sentence of each template's description, so the catalog is about a quarter shorter. `--json` keeps descriptions whole, and `astryx template <id> --skeleton` prints a template's whole description above its layout. The first-sentence rule that `astryx build` shares no longer ends a sentence at a period inside quotes, so a description quoting a date such as "2. Nov. 2026" reads whole there too.
- When `astryx template <name> <path>` refuses the destination of a Core template that no integration replaces, outside the project (an absolute path, or one that leaves it through `..`), it also names the command that writes that same destination: a change to the nearest folder of it that exists, then the template command with the path from there, printed with the CLI invocation for that folder. When `--overwrite` was given, that command and the scratch-copy command keep it, so they do not refuse a second time; the suggested place inside the project is another file and never gets it. A `..` path used to get the refusal with no command to run; it now gets the same commands as an absolute one. A `..` path that lands in the system temp folder is still not a scratch copy; the refusal names its absolute path, which takes one.
- `astryx template <name> <path>` writes a scratch copy to an absolute path in the system temp folder (`os.tmpdir()`, or `/tmp` on a POSIX system), such as `/tmp/dashboard`, instead of refusing it. The receipt names the folder by its whole path (`data.outputDir` in `--json`), and the checks of a write in the project apply: no link carries the copy out of the temp folder, and an existing file is replaced only with `--overwrite`. A temp folder that is a disk's root or holds the home folder is not used. Any other path outside the project is still refused with `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`.
- `theme add` and `theme use` wire a theme with one color mode in that mode. When a theme's built module exports `colorModes` (`["light"]` or `["dark"]`; `theme build` writes it when the theme source exports it), the `theme.app` receipt gives that theme a `mode` field and the generated theme module lists it in a `themeModes` export. The first import's wiring passes `mode={themeModes[defaultThemeSlug] ?? 'system'}` to `Theme`, so the selected theme shows its own mode and a theme with both modes follows the system. When a later `theme add` or `theme use` first adds `themeModes` to an app that is already wired, the receipt marks `change.wireModes` and prints the wiring line to use. Once the module has exported `themeModes`, it keeps the export (empty when no theme has one mode), so the wiring keeps compiling after `theme remove`. The mode is read from the file that declares the theme, so a theme module that re-exports the built module (whole or by name) carries it. A project whose themes all have both modes gets the same receipt, module and wiring as before.
- `astryx theme add` with a shared theme follows an integration's install guidance: in a project whose integration says how it adds packages, the command installs nothing with the package manager and names that line for the Astryx base packages and any others the theme imports (`data.copy.installGuidance`).
- `astryx theme add` installs a theme someone shared in one command: give it the theme's folder, a `.tgz` archive of it, or an https URL to a `.tgz` instead of a slug. It checks that the one theme folder it finds is a complete, built theme, copies it into the app's local themes root (`src/themes/<name>`), installs the Astryx packages the theme imports that the app lacks (its base theme package) with the app's package manager and install scripts off, and records the theme as the app's default, so an app wired to the generated module shows it at once. Nothing of the theme runs during the add. Any other package the theme imports is named with its install command, never installed. The result lists every file written and the record and dependency changed. It never replaces a file it did not write, and adding the same shared theme again replaces its own unchanged copy. `theme remove` undoes the add: it deletes the files the add wrote (keeping any you changed) and uninstalls the packages it installed. `theme add <slug>` is unchanged; the JSON gains `data.copy`, and a remove's gains `data.undo`.
- `astryx theme build --family`: the family's root may extend a theme the family does not select, such as an installed theme package. Its CSS and export carry that base as the root's standalone build does, and the module imports the package for the icons it inherits. That package is a requirement: the family's receipt names it (`base`) and its text output says which package it requires, and a build fails naming the package and the theme when it is not installed or does not export the base, never building the root without it. A member whose own base is not selected is refused naming that base, and a local base the family does not select that supplies icons is refused naming the base to select.
- `astryx theme build` warns about a component setting of a theme's page rules that the browser does not show as written, for each setting a key of the theme's own file (or a local theme it extends) writes, also through a call, a const or a spread; settings a helper function builds or a module the theme imports writes, its onDark and onLight surfaces and its adaptation rules are not read. It names one a later shorthand resets (a `border` after the block's own `borderTopColor`, or a second key that builds the same rule), one a more specific rule of the theme it extends beats on a variant, and one whose order against such a rule (or the theme's own variant of it) decides what shows where both hold. A rule for a runtime state alone (`:hover`, `selected`) is the look of that state and never counts. Each warning names the setting's line, the rule that wins and the change that makes it show, and the receipt lists them in `settingIssues`. The output is the same as before.
- `astryx theme list` names, for each theme, the owner the app imports it from and whether that owner is installed (`owner`, `installed`). The CLI ships a bundled theme's descriptor and source (for `theme eject`), not the built output the app imports: `theme add` records and the app imports that from the theme's own package (such as `@astryxdesign/theme-neutral`), and refuses to add it until that package is installed; the list now says so instead of naming only the CLI. Existing fields are unchanged.
- The Theming section of `astryx component <Name>` (and of an integration component read through `astryx discover <package>/<Component>`) prints its `defineTheme` override example, and its standard-CSS example, on one line each instead of a multi-line code block. The same keys and comments appear; `--json` is unchanged.
- `astryx theme remove` can remove the only added theme. Before, it refused and said to add another theme and make it the default first, so removing a theme left the app on a theme nobody chose.
