Now it deletes the generated theme module when the module is exactly what the CLI wrote, and prints the module import and the `Theme` wrapper the app root must drop. A module with changes the CLI did not write stays, and the command says how to finish by hand. Removing the default while other themes are added still asks for `theme use` first. In `--json`, the `theme.app` result of that removal has no themes, an empty `default`, and `change.moduleRemoved: true` (and `change.themeModes: true` when the deleted module exported `themeModes`).
- `astryx theme template` lists the `'@light'` and `'@dark'` block form among a component's style keys, with a commented example: a block that applies only in that color mode.
- `astryx upgrade --apply` refreshes the Astryx skill in every place `astryx init --to` saved (astryx.config `skills.to`), under init's rules: the two copies of the project skills folders are written together or not at all, an edited file is kept, and nothing is written through a folder linked out of the project. The dry run names each file it would write. An Astryx block is still refreshed wherever it is, and a project that keeps its Astryx guidance only as a skill is no longer told to add it. `astryx doctor` adds a `skill-places` check: it passes when each saved skill file matches this release, and warns when one is missing or stale, when the two copies of a place differ, when the block and a project skill copy (in the project skills folders or a saved project folder) are both there without both being saved, or when a project skill is named `astryx`. Doctor's `computer-agent-text` check names the folders outside a project that `init --to` saved. Inside a project, `astryx init --to` naming only places outside it (`user`, or folders outside the project) with no feature beyond the agent docs is answered by the copy that started the run, as `--user` is.
- `astryx upgrade --list` prints each codemod on one line, its name and title, under its version, with `(optional)` on the codemods that run only on request and the package named once when every codemod shares it, instead of a five-line record per codemod. The list now grows by one line per new codemod, plus a heading when a codemod starts a new version. `--json` is unchanged.

#### Fixes

- `astryx add` refuses a named pipe or a device where it writes a file, never opening it.
- The note for an Apple interface face offers its generic once (`system-ui, sans-serif`), and a font name such as `constructor` is no Apple face. `astryx doctor` names the package that loads a family a theme's font stylesheet lacks when it is an open font it knows (`npm install @fontsource/inter`), then the command that writes the stylesheet again; for a self-hosted family (such as `Acme Sans`) it gives the step to add the font stylesheet export or a local `<slug>.fonts.css`.
- `astryx theme build` warns, and `astryx experimental theme` refuses, a radius scale with no `base` or `multiplier`, or one Core cannot read as a number (a boolean is read as 1 or 0, so it builds). Core builds every scaled corner from it as NaNpx, which the browser drops. A radius of `0` or `''` is said too: Core skips it and builds no corner token, so the base theme's corners stay (`radius: {base: 0, multiplier: 1}` squares them).
  In the editor:

  - A family typed alone that the base theme already uses keeps the base's own fallbacks (Fraunces keeps Georgia and serif).
  - Any other family typed alone gets fallbacks of the kind its name says (a Serif name serif ones, a Mono or Code name monospace ones), as the open fonts do.
  - A family the base's font stylesheet loads is no longer also named as a font no package loads.

- `astryx theme build` and `astryx experimental theme` judge the shape of a typography block by what Core reads:
  - a type scale with no base or ratio, or one that is no block, which builds every size as NaNrem;
  - a role or a typography given as a plain value, which builds nothing;
  - a heading `weights` that is no block of levels, which Core reads letter by letter;
  - one heading level written twice (`'01'` and `1`), where Core keeps one.

  Without a type scale, any role weight gets the no-scale reason, and an empty weight is named as skipped. A boxed value is judged as its primitive, a signed number weight (`-100`) is read as written, and a plain-object theme is judged on the values it loads.

- `astryx theme build` warns, at its line, a typography value Core builds into something no browser uses, as `astryx experimental theme` refuses it: a font stack with a space in one `family` (Core quotes it whole), a quoted family name with a space, a role weight with no type scale, and a `weights` entry that is no heading level. Both judge a family by what Core writes, so a quoted name without a space (`'"Lato"'`) and a list without one (`'Lato,serif'`), which build as written, are taken. On the font dial, a weight number in any form CSS reads (`Inter +500`, `Inter 1e3`) after a known family, or a weight or style word before it (`700 Inter`, `bold Inter`), is that weight or style, never saved as a family of that name.
- `astryx theme build` warns a typography value wherever the theme writes it (a const, a role const, a spread, an import, a value computed at run time), at the line that writes it when one does; a role weight that is no font weight (`'semi-bold'`, `'1200'`), which the browser drops; and a heading weight under a number key that is no level (`{7: '800'}`). Both the build and `astryx experimental theme` read a heading level as Core does, so `'01'` and `'1.0'` are level 1. On the font dial, a weight or style word after a name that starts with a family the editor knows (`Inter Tight Bold`) is read as a number there is: a weight where a family goes.
- `astryx theme build` and `astryx experimental theme` name a typography weight given as a number (`weight: 600`) as a type mismatch: the field takes the text `'600'`. The message says Core still writes a weight from 1 to 1000, and offers the text form.
- Two example blocks no longer cause a hydration mismatch: `TimestampAutoFormat` and `TimestampRelativeFormat` read the clock once per mount after hydration instead of during render; the server markup shows a fixed placeholder date until hydration. Six example blocks that show several breadcrumbs, outlines, paginations or side navigations side by side now give each one its own accessible name, so screen readers can tell the landmarks apart. No visual change after hydration.
- Six chat example blocks (the full-featured composer, the composer drawer with progress, the message bubble with custom content and with metadata, and the message metadata footer and showcase): Copy now copies the message and says so; Retry, the thumbs, Mention, Attach and the report card show a short demo note instead of doing nothing. Other chat examples are unchanged.
- Layout header and footer, card and empty state example blocks: their action buttons show a short demo note instead of doing nothing. The general Layout example blocks are not part of this change.
- The CommandPaletteGroup basic block, both CommandPaletteList blocks and the DropdownMenuGroup showcase: picking an item shows a short demo note instead of doing nothing. Other command palette and dropdown menu examples are unchanged.
- Five nav example blocks (TopNav showcase, centered navigation, enterprise dashboard and mega menu; SideNav with a header menu): Search, Notifications and Profile show a short demo note, and Sign in, Get started, Upgrade and the header-menu side nav's items are links. Other top and side nav examples are unchanged.
- Nine example blocks (Toolbar card header, sizes and three slots; Selector and MultiSelector ghost toolbars; Selector option descriptions; Table bulk actions; TabList tabs with actions; Popover hook usage): their action buttons show a short demo note instead of doing nothing, and the three-slot toolbar's Back arrow mirrors in right-to-left. The three-slot toolbar's Back still does nothing on press; the bulk-actions Delete and Archive, and controls in other blocks (such as the toolbar-with-tabs New item), are unchanged.
- `astryx build`'s block picker counts every block its doc-side word weights were fitted with as known, so those blocks no longer get the head start the picker gives blocks it has never seen.
- The heading truncation, bottom sheet menu, step content, step indicator, step states and grid focus examples lay out with HStack and VStack instead of hand-written flex wrappers, so their gaps follow the theme's spacing steps. They look the same in the default theme; themes with roomier spacing show wider gaps.
- `astryx build` ranks blocks also by single words a block's docs use that its fitted word weights do not know (such as a newer Core block's own terms), so a request that uses those words can tie to that block.
- `astryx build` calls page or app shell with a refit word table and new blend numbers. The weights file stores that table once: the pick model reads the call model's tables when it carries none of its own.
- `astryx build` starts from a family's frame template when the frame holds the page the idea names. "Notification settings in a modal" now starts from the settings dialog template instead of the plain settings page; a modal that holds only a part ("a toggle in a modal on the settings page") keeps the settings page.
- `astryx build` treats a frame as evidence for a page template only when the frame holds that template's kind of page. "Saved drafts in a modal with resume and delete row actions" asks for a list of drafts in a modal, not a settings page, so it no longer starts from the settings dialog; it starts from the app shell, with the parts listed in the kit.
- `astryx build` no longer starts a part, a change to an existing page, or a page it would put on the app shell from a template kept off the template gallery. The theme showcase, a page of sample product screens, was taken as the app shell; those requests now start from a real shell template.
- `astryx build` reads a request that opens with "add" and says where the piece goes ("add a filter row above the table") as a change to a page the builder already has, so it starts from the app shell. "Add a dashboard to the app" and "add a new dashboard" still start from a page template.
- `astryx build` keeps "a side panel with an owner, a status, and a history" as one part that starts from the app shell, and reads "a list of planning jobs" as a page. Component categories now declare the page-template family whose records their components hold.
- `astryx build` starts a part from a page family's base template only when that template leads the ranking and the family is where the part goes. A part request headed by a word that also names a component, such as "a table filter chip", asks for that piece and starts from the app shell.
- `astryx build` with no query now names the exact theme wiring `theme add` prints for your project: the imports and the value `<Theme>` takes (`themes[defaultThemeSlug]` from the generated `astryx-themes` module), the color mode for a theme with one, or the provider to pass it to when an installed package declares one. Before a theme is added, it reads the installed theme's built module the way `theme add` does, so the wiring it names is the one `theme add` then prints. When no theme is added yet, a last step gives the `theme add <slug>` command for your installed theme or the starter theme. The old rule left the value open (`theme={...}`), so pages often passed a theme name such as `"light"` and crashed once script ran.
- `astryx build` names a page template that is not ready only when the idea names it, as a reason ("`incident-console` isn't ready yet, so build started from `shell-top-nav`."); otherwise no not-ready template appears in its output, including `pages` and the "Keyword search matched" line.
- `astryx build` chooses its start from ready page templates only: a template that is not ready yet, however well its words match, is no longer search's direct match for build and no longer keeps an idea on the app shell.
- `astryx build` reads search as if every page template that is not ready yet were absent: search leaves such templates out of what it ranks for build, so the start, the page list, the block suggestions, the components and `matchCount` are exactly what they would be without them. A not-ready template's name typed as the idea no longer empties the kit. When the idea names a not-ready template that search matches directly, the reason still says it is not ready yet. `astryx search` still lists every template.
- `astryx build` names where its start and each alternative go in the project it runs in, so the scaffold command runs as printed: the path `astryx template` names for that template from the project's layout and the template's own id (not the Core id an integration replacement stands in for): in a Next app, its App Router folder (`app/<name>` or `src/app/<name>`) or, with only the Pages Router, the page file `pages/<name>.tsx` or `src/pages/<name>.tsx`; else `src/pages/<name>`. The path is quoted when a shell would read it otherwise. In a folder with no package.json, the command keeps the `<path>` placeholder.
- `astryx build` settles an exact ranker tie by whether a template is its family's base, instead of by how many hyphen-separated parts its id has: a family's base keeps its place ahead of a tied variant. Templates still tied, in the same family or not, are ordered by how strongly each one's own descriptor answers the idea, then by how typical of its family it is, then by name. A template the idea names by its whole name wins a tie. The page-pick model settles an exact tie of its final score the same way, and its rank features give equal values equal ranks, so the order of the weights file never decides.
- When page templates of one family tie exactly and the ranker's pick is one the word tables do not list (such as the collapsible and comparison tables, or an integration's template), `astryx build` starts from the tied template whose own description, keywords and page components best match the idea, then the one most typical of its family, instead of the alphabetically first.
- When `astryx build`'s ranker picks a template the word tables don't list, it now weighs that template against the pick model's best listed page, the same model that chooses the page everywhere else, instead of against the call model's.
- A page template that is not ready yet no longer takes one of the places in the search results `astryx build` reads, so it no longer pushes a page, a block suggestion or a component out of build's kit; `matchCount` still counts it. When the idea names a not-ready template, the reason still says so even if another not-ready template ranks above it.
- `astryx build`: a page template named the way code writes it (`CheckoutWizard`, `kanbanBoard`) starts that template, as its plain words do, and so does a name with two neighbouring letters swapped in a word of six or more letters (`dashbaord`). Shorter words are read as written.
- A long-running CLI process reads a family doc or a theme or icon descriptor again when npm replaces it with a file of the same size and modification time, and reads the theme part data cache again when it is rewritten in place with the same size and modification time.
- The `canvas-editor` template draws the corner radius field with the one-rounded-corner icon and the per-corner button with the four-corner icon, and declares each icon with the meaning its picture shows, so a project whose icon set reaches these Lucide icons through reviewed matches also gets the right picture on each control.
- The canvas-editor page template fits a phone. When 40% is too wide for the canvas, the artboard opens at the largest zoom step that fits, the tab strip keeps the open tab's close reachable, and the save note leaves the screen when the header is too narrow for it (a screen reader still reads it).
- The `canvas-editor` template's flip buttons draw the mirror axis of their action: Flip horizontally shows the vertical axis and Flip vertically the horizontal one. Before, each button showed the other's picture. Each button keeps its meaning, so icon sets that map the flip meanings draw the same icons as before. A main icon set that wraps `lucide-react` and names no variant keeps the template's Lucide imports, so it now shows the corrected pictures too.
- The checkout wizard template fits a 320 px phone again: the order summary, the step strip, the promo code row and the Continue buttons stay inside the page's side padding instead of running about 18 px into it, and the promo code's Apply button keeps its full label while the field gives up the room. Wider screens look the same.
- The bundled chocolate theme's light category text reads at 4.5:1 on a card.
- The bundled gothic theme template matches the gothic error-toast fix.
- The bundled matcha theme's dark menus, popovers and muted fills take its near-black neutral like its cards.
- The official themes that `astryx theme eject` scaffolds carry the theme packages' text contrast fixes: text, links, category and status text, and code text meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) on the surfaces the theme packages now check.
- The neutral and y2k themes that `astryx theme eject` scaffolds show Skeleton placeholders on their light page: their `--color-skeleton` takes a darker neutral stop, as the theme packages do.
- When Node already uses a compile cache (`NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`), the CLI leaves it as it is and no longer makes an empty `node-compile-cache-<uid>` folder in the temp folder.
- The contact-form template no longer scrolls sideways on a phone. Its section takes the full width up to 800px instead of its content's width, so a long field placeholder no longer sets the page's minimum width. On its own, the page looks the same at 768px and wider. Inside a padded layout region narrower than 800px, the section now stays within the padding where it used to run into it.
- CLI errors name a run to try. An option a command does not take now names the options the command takes, and the command as meant when the option points at one of them: `component Table --format json` names `component Table --json`, `--full` names `--detail full`, `--props-only` names `--props`, and `theme --list` names `theme list`. A word the CLI has no command for names the command the words point at: a whole command passed as one word, a command's plural, an option some commands take (`list` names `component --list`), a command deeper in the tree (`verify` names `integration verify`; `eject` names `theme eject --help`, since it needs a theme), or a name another command reads (`info Text` names `component Text`); with no such command, it names near command names by Commander's own rule (at most three edits, and more than 40% of the name the same), so `info Text` names `component Text` where it used to name `init`. `doctor` given a path names `doctor --built <path>`, and several paths in the project name the folder that holds them. `upgrade --from <version> --list` names `upgrade --list` and the migration from that version, `template` with `--skeleton` or `--list` and other words names each run alone, and an option given without its value prints the command's usage with that option in it. Every named run parses, and a call that does not itself name the `experimental` group gets no experimental command in its answer. A word that names no command followed by an unknown option (`astryx describe Table --format json`) now reports `ERR_UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, as the same call without the option does, instead of `ERR_INVALID_OPTION`; every other error code, and every exit code, is unchanged.
- A theme module that throws from a microtask while it loads is a refused theme load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming the error) on every supported Node. Before, Node before 24 answered `ERR_UNKNOWN`, and a theme loaded through the CLI's own Core (no Core in its folder, and each member of a `--family` build) could build with the exception dropped. `astryx theme build` and the theme editor still need Node 22.15 or later, or 23.5 or later, to load a theme that imports a stylesheet or an asset, and so does a recorded theme that imports an asset, or a stylesheet that a module in another folder imports by a relative path. On an older Node those loads are now refused with a message that names the file and the Node versions that load it, and says that nothing was written, in place of Node's "Unknown file extension" or "Unexpected token" error. A recorded theme's other stylesheets still load there.
- `astryx theme palette generate` refuses a palette config made with a newer Astryx CLI, whose recipe this CLI does not know yet, with the recipe it uses, the recipes this CLI knows, and the update step that fits where the CLI runs. The refusal keeps its error code.
- The Order Detail template writes the discount with a true minus sign held to its amount (`− $15.00`), not an en dash and a space that a narrow row could break between.
- A long answer piped to a slow reader arrives whole. When a command ended in an error with an answer longer than 64 KiB, such as `astryx template <name> --json` with many suggestions, a reader like `$(…)` or `| (sleep 1; wc -c)` got only the first 64 KiB, so `--json` callers got invalid JSON. Every command now writes piped output in full before it exits; short answers are as fast as before.
- On a phone, the payment-form template's order summary keeps each price inside its card. An item's name and badge wrap onto two lines, and when even that does not fit beside the price, the price moves under them at the end of the line. Desktop is unchanged.
- The CLI orders names the same way on every machine. Build, search, discovery and the CLI's lists (such as `astryx component --list`) broke ties with the host's locale, so a machine set to another language could pick a different template or print lists in a different order. They now use one fixed text order, and a lint rule keeps locale-dependent comparisons out of the CLI.
- `astryx component` and `astryx discover <package>/<Component>` print the commands a component doc writes (with a `{@command …}` token, a `{@link …}`, or a bare `astryx …` code span) with the project's command, as `astryx docs` does, instead of a bare `astryx …` that may not run in the project. `--json` keeps the bare command.
- `astryx component VStack --detail full` and `astryx component HStack --detail full` print the props list once, under Props, instead of again under Components. The JSON is unchanged.
- `astryx component <hook>` prints the hook's parameters, which `astryx hook <hook>` also prints: one line each in the default answer (name, type, default, required, and the description's first sentence) and the whole table at `--detail full`. The JSON is unchanged.
- `astryx component <hook>` prints what the hook returns, as `astryx hook <hook>` does: a Returns section at the default and full detail, and the returned fields in the brief signature. The JSON is unchanged.
- `astryx component <name>` no longer opens a component through one of its keywords. A keyword is a word to find a component by, not another name for it. A name that is clearly one component's keyword now gives the usual not-found error, with that component as the first suggestion. Exact names, names in another case, and file names open as before. The component doc type and the single-component authoring guide now define keywords the same way, and the guide has a section on choosing them.
- `astryx component <Name>` names a family's sub-components that have their own doc on one line, with the command that reads each, instead of a heading and a "see" line per sub-component. A sub-component with its own description or props keeps its section.
- `astryx component <Name>` with a name that is not a component now suggests the components of your project's integrations, not only Core's. A typo of an integration component's name (`ZorbletCrd` for `ZorbletCard`), or its name without its package's prefix, gets that component as a suggestion, matched by the same rule as a Core component: name, keywords and description. Two adjacent letters swapped in a name (`Butotn`) now count as one slip, as a one-letter typo does, and so does one slip in a name typed as words (`hover crad` or `hover-crd` for `HoverCard`): that name comes before a component that only has the words as a keyword. A component whose name is part of the typed name now comes before a component that only has one of the typed words as a keyword, from any package (`MetricCard` suggests Card, not InfoTip). Among names that hold every typed word, the one with the fewest extra words comes first (`time` lists TimeInput before Timestamp). Only a Core component still resolves by a close match, and the suggestion count rules are unchanged. `astryx component tag-list` no longer opens OverflowList: the name is also one slip from TabList, so the lookup lists OverflowList first, then TabList.
- The computer-level agent text adds Astryx to a new project, or to an existing app only when the user asks for Astryx; an existing app that doesn't use Astryx keeps its current UI stack. Before, it told agents to add Astryx to any project without it, so an agent asked for one page in a plain React app could rewrite the app with Astryx.
- An option that answers a question in other tools (`--yes`, `-y`, `--assume-yes`, `--non-interactive`, `--no-interactive`, `--no-input`) now gets a direct answer: no Astryx command asks a question, so the error says the option is not needed and names the same command without it (`Run: npx astryx init`). On `upgrade`, which writes only with `--apply`, it names the `--apply` run first and the preview run second (a `--list` run keeps the plain answer). Before, `astryx init --yes` listed init's options and pointed at `init --help`, so an agent spent a step reading help before it ran plain `init`.
- Two content page templates now ask for confirmation before a destructive action: Refund on the detail page and Delete in each attachment's menu on the work item page. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.
- The order detail, work item detail and component documentation page templates read correctly when they are shared as a file that runs no script. Their first paint is the narrow layout at every width, instead of a desktop side rail that squeezed the page into a narrow column on a phone; once script runs, wide screens still get the side rail. On a narrow screen the order and work item details now follow the main column instead of opening in a full-screen dialog, and the component documentation's section links stay on top as links instead of a picker.
- `doctor`'s fix for a missing Core, and `theme build`'s hint to install Core, now name Core at the same release as the theme hints. That is the Core release the project already names, in its dependencies or peer dependencies, or, when it names no Core at all, the release of the CLI that answers. Before, they named the newest Core. A project that followed both hints could get a Core that its theme's exact Core peer does not accept.
- In dark mode, secondary text on a neutral fill (an unselected SegmentedControl label, AvatarGroup's "+N" count) now meets 4.5:1 contrast on the default surface and on a Card. The default dark `--color-text-secondary` is a little lighter: `#B0B5BB`, was `#AAAFB5`.
- The dashboard page templates give screen readers clearer structure: each page marks its content area (`LayoutContent`) as the main landmark, has exactly one level-1 heading, and has a heading outline with no skipped levels (set with `accessibilityLevel`, so the look is unchanged). `dashboard` gains a visually hidden "Dashboard" title, and `dashboard-comparison`'s decorative sparklines no longer take keyboard focus inside hidden content. No visual change.
- Controls that did nothing in six dashboard page templates now respond with a demo message that says what would happen: Reload and both View more buttons on the analytics dashboard, Export on the comparison, scorecard and funnel dashboards, Export status on the program dashboard, and View more on the portfolio dashboard.
- `astryx component <name>` keeps a suggested component whose keywords or synonyms are the typed name ahead of another command's hint for a near spelling, and leaves the hint out when such components fill the list (`astryx component Combobox` lists Typeahead, Selector and Tokenizer, not `astryx hook useCombobox`).
- The text wrapping, word break, truncation, heading truncation, overflow list, context menu, bottom sheet menu and direction hook examples draw their demo frames and targets with theme colors instead of fixed grays, so they follow the app's theme and dark mode.
- `astryx discover` names an installed integration's docs the way `astryx docs` opens them: a doc that adds sections to a topic by that topic's name, and a guide by its route. It listed each doc by the name on its file, so a doc such as a theme package's guide, which adds its sections to `theme`, printed a name `astryx docs` did not know.
- `astryx discover <package>/<set>` names an icon set's default look by its variant in text (`default: outline`) instead of printing `[object Object]`, and leaves the line out when the default names no variant. `astryx experimental icon --list` no longer prints an empty `default:` line for such a default. The JSON is unchanged.
- A section an integration adds to a topic, or to a guide by its route, now stays when another integration, configured later, replaces that topic or guide: whether it showed used to depend on configured order alone. A topic read also names, at its top, the sections other packages add to it, since an added section joins the end of a topic that can be long.
- `astryx docs` now names Core, the CLI, and the packages Astryx releases with Core such as themes, at the Core release your project uses, as `theme add` and `doctor` do. In a project that pins Core 0.7.10, the step to add a theme shows `npm install -E @astryxdesign/theme-neutral@0.7.10`. Before, it named no version, so npm picked the newest theme, which needs a newer Core than the project has, and the install failed. In a folder with no Core, on the docs site's pages, and in a step that first moves to another folder, the commands still name the packages with no version. The docs site's MCP endpoint names the Core release it documents.
- Two packages that add a section with one title to the same docs topic or guide both keep it. Across packages, a section replaces another only when one carries an authored `id` that is the other's key or a title query the other's title answers. When one package's section holds the key another package's later section derives from its title, the later one is read by a key that starts with its package's provider id (its package name unless it sets one), such as `acme-dune-theme-install`, so `astryx docs`, `--index`, namespace reads and search show both. This includes titles that differ only in letter case: the later of two packages' `Install` and `INSTALL` was read as `install-2` and is now read by its provider key. Every other key collision keeps its numeric suffix. Sections of the topic itself still take a replacement from any package, the last configured winning.
- The documentation page templates fit a phone: the overview page's hero gives its title the card's width, so in the default theme the title no longer breaks inside a word, and the design page's example actions and button previews wrap instead of running past their card. Wide screens look the same as before.
- The stored docs routes, and so the build id, are the same on every machine that packs the same files. How the machine's Node resolves module imports no longer changes which folders the stored routes list.
- The technical documentation page template's "Next steps" items wrap on a narrow screen instead of cutting off after one line, so a phone reader sees each item in full. Wide screens are unchanged.
- The technical documentation page template reads correctly when it is shared as a file that runs no script. Its first paint is one column with the section links on top at every width, instead of a desktop side rail that squeezed the article into a narrow column on a phone; once script runs, wide screens still get the side rail. Copy buttons appear only once the page runs, so a static copy shows no buttons that do nothing. On a phone the section links stay on top as links instead of a picker.
- `astryx docs <topic>` opens a page typed in another spelling of its route: spaces, hyphens, slashes, dots and underscores all separate words, and word order does not count (`docs tokens.tokens-color` opens `tokens/tokens-color`). When the typed words only name a page and no other command's entry matches, the miss suggests the pages whose title or declared keywords carry them, closest first (`docs theming` suggests the Theming topic first), keeps a route the typed words name first, and never lists more than before; a namespace's children are ordered the same way.
- `astryx docs` with a mistyped topic or namespace (`tokns`, `colr`) now lists the one a slip or two away first, ahead of the other topics and namespaces.
- `astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` no longer offer to install a package named after a project folder, such as `src`, for an import the project's `baseUrl` maps to a TypeScript file written with a `.js` extension (`src/rows.js` for `src/rows.ts`). They now read such an import as the project's own file, as TypeScript does.
- Outside a project, `astryx doctor` now warns about an integration installed for the computer that has issues in its own files, and names them. Before, commands such as `astryx search` and `astryx discover` warned about the integration and said to run `astryx doctor`, but `doctor` passed and named no issue. Issues that need a comparison with Core components are still not named there, because `doctor` reads no Core outside a project.
- `doctor` now says when an app does not load Core's component styles, `@astryxdesign/core/astryx.css`. In an app that uses Core's prebuilt styles, components render unstyled without them. Before, nothing caught it: the build, `doctor` and `doctor --built` all passed. Plain `doctor` warns when no project stylesheet or module imports them and no page links them. `doctor --built` warns when the output uses Astryx but no built stylesheet or page carries them. An app that compiles Core's styles from source with `@astryxdesign/build` is not checked.
- `astryx doctor` no longer reports a theme as wired because a theme source or a generated theme file imports it: the theme editor's settings module, a theme build's output, or a theme source that imports a package theme only to extend it. Before, an editor theme built on an installed theme package (`--like <theme>`) turned the "no theme appears wired" warning into a pass while the app rendered no theme; now only the app's own imports of a theme, or a theme it passes to `Theme`, count.
- `astryx doctor`'s theme font check now accepts a Google Fonts or Bunny Fonts stylesheet `<link>` in the app's page head as loading the families it names: in `index.html`, `public/index.html`, `src/index.html`, or a Next.js root layout or `_document` (`.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.js`, `.mjs` or `.ts`, under `app/`, `pages/` or `src/`). An app that loads a theme's fonts that way no longer gets the warning. A link inside a comment, one whose `rel` is not `stylesheet`, or one from another host does not count. When a package theme ships no font stylesheet, the fix names the page file whose `<head>` the link goes in.
- `doctor`'s theme font check now counts a family as loaded when a `family` parameter of a font service URL in the theme's font stylesheet names it. The Google Fonts import in every Astryx theme's font stylesheet does this. Before, an app set up correctly with the neutral theme got a warning it could not act on: "External font imports prevent proof for neutral: Figtree." A family that no `family` parameter names still gets that warning, as does a font service URL that names its families another way.
- `doctor`'s theme font check now counts a family as loaded when any font stylesheet that the generated theme module imports loads it. A local theme built on neutral, such as one whose source extends neutral or a copy that `theme eject` makes, names neutral's fonts but ships no font stylesheet of its own. Before, `doctor` warned "Added themes name font families but import no font stylesheet (<theme>: Figtree (font stylesheet is not imported))", even when the app also added neutral and the module imported neutral's font stylesheet. A family that no imported font stylesheet loads still gets that warning.
- With no update check recorded, `astryx doctor`'s `newest-release` check no longer says the check runs once a day after a command, which is true only for a copy installed for the computer. It now says that only that copy checks, that a project's own copy changes only when the project upgrades it, and that a tool that runs its own copy chooses its release.
- `astryx doctor integration <check> <package>` run in the folder of that package now says the package is the one in this folder, not one the project installs, and names `astryx integration check` for checking the package you are making. Before, it said only that the package was not installed and to install it first.
- `astryx doctor --built`'s purity check no longer flags the stylesheets the app's registered themes load. It reads them from the theme module the CLI writes (`theme add` and the theme editor), so an editor-made theme starts with no "imports the stylesheet" findings. Any other stylesheet import is still flagged.
- `astryx doctor --built` no longer flags the setup stylesheet as page styling. A stylesheet that only imports Astryx packages' CSS (`reset.css`, `astryx.css`, a theme's CSS), as the getting-started steps write it, is read as wiring. A stylesheet with rules of its own, or an import from another package, is still flagged.
- `astryx doctor` no longer fails its private theme variables check in a Yarn Plug'n'Play project. For a built-in theme that the app installs as a package, the check now reads that package's own theme source, which is the copy the app uses, instead of the CLI's copy, whose icon import Yarn refuses to resolve.
- `doctor`'s private theme variables check now loads each theme input with the Core the project installed when the CLI is installed for the computer. Before, in an app with Core and a theme package but no CLI in the project, the check failed for every theme input that imports `@astryxdesign/core`, as every Astryx theme package does. That CLI has no Core of its own: "Added theme inputs set private --_* variables directly (…: input could not be inspected …)". When the project's Core isn't installed yet, as in a fresh clone, the check now says that it did not inspect the theme inputs. Before, it failed for each input that imports `@astryxdesign/core`.
- The editor template's transactions table keeps names readable on a phone. Each column now has a floor (name 180px, date and amount 120px, actions 60px), and its share of the width matches that floor. The table needs at least 480px; in anything narrower, such as a phone, it scrolls sideways instead of squeezing names to a letter or two per line. Desktop windows that give the table 480px or more do not scroll; the name column takes a larger share and the actions column a smaller one.
- In a project that pins `@astryxdesign/core` to one version, as Astryx starters do, the commands the CLI prints to add or upgrade Astryx packages (the once-a-day hint, `doctor`'s fixes, the setup reminder, and the upgrade notice) save the new versions exactly too, such as `npm install -E @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.16`. Before, with npm, following them replaced the project's exact pins with ranges such as `^0.7.16`, so a later install could bring a CLI from another release than the project's Core.
- A run that prints its answer and then exits 1 records the code that answer carries in its debug event, as an error that `cliError` prints does. A component batch with a selector that does not resolve records the first unresolved row's code (such as `ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT`); `theme build --check` that finds stale outputs records `ERR_THEME_STALE`; `upgrade` records the code of an error it reports in text mode, and the `errorCode` of a run that stops incomplete (such as `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED`), in text and in `--json`; `init` that refuses its agent-docs path records `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`. Each code is recorded once the answer is printed, so an error that stops the answer first (a recorded theme that does not load) keeps its own code. A `debug` handler saw these runs as `ERR_UNCLASSIFIED_EXIT`. Output and exit codes are unchanged.
- `astryx theme use <theme>` opens its receipt with the default it set: "[ok] <theme> is now the app's default theme: themes[defaultThemeSlug] is <theme>.", or "[ok] <theme> was already the app's default theme; nothing changed." when it was the default already. The receipt's fields are unchanged, and the JSON is unchanged.
- The payment form template's Remove link on each cart line now asks for confirmation first. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.
- The `form-wizard-vertical` template declares its review banner icon as `review`, which icon sets draw as `info`, the meaning the banner shows, instead of `checkDouble`. A project whose icon set draws template icons by meaning now gets that set's info icon in the banner. A project whose main set wraps `@heroicons/react` keeps the check badge unless it picks a variant, and copies without an icon set are unchanged.
- The vertical form wizard's cover buttons keep their full labels on every phone width: the dropzone column moves under the cover before "Preview on device" would be cut.
- Buttons in form page templates that did nothing now show a demo message that says what would happen: Cancel in the workspace and audiobook wizards, Create workspace and Submit for review on a finished last step, Place Order on a complete payment form, and Save on the payment form's cart line.
- In a fresh clone (a project that lists `@astryxdesign/core` and a theme package, with nothing installed yet), `astryx doctor` now says to install the project's dependencies, such as `npm install`, for a missing Core and a missing theme package. Before, its fixes added Core with no version and the theme package at the latest release, so following them replaced the project's versions with others.
- In a fresh clone whose `package.json` lists `@astryxdesign/cli`, the once-a-day hint, `doctor`, and the setup reminder now say to install the project's dependencies (such as `npm install`), not to add the CLI again. Adding it again replaced the exact version the project lists with a range, such as `^0.7.10`.
- File protection now decodes consecutive octal escapes in quoted `.gitattributes` paths as UTF-8 bytes. Before, a rule such as `"caf\303\251.js" linguist-generated` was treated as separate code points and failed to protect the matching `café.js` file; quoted and literal UTF-8 spellings now classify consistently.
- In a Yarn Plug'n'Play project, the `astryx` command installed for the computer hands each run to the project's own CLI: it starts again with the project's runtime, as Yarn starts a command, instead of answering with its own release and telling you to install a CLI the project already has. Commands the CLI prints there start with `yarn astryx`, not with a `yarn dlx` download of the CLI.
- Palette recipe `astryx-oklch-v2`: a gray family's color now fades toward white the way a gray scale's does, so a colored gray (a slate `#64748b`, a warm `#78716c`) gives the page and the cards on it only a faint tint instead of a clearly blue or cream page; its darker shades keep their color. v1, and so every shipped palette and existing config, is unchanged. The neutral dial's help says so, and names `--color-background-body` for a clearly tinted page.
- Two page templates no longer leave an empty column on wide screens. The product gallery's header (a heading and its intro) now fills two columns instead of three, and the two-column form's contact strip fills three columns instead of four, so it sits centered. Narrower widths are unchanged.
- Grid: `columns={{minWidth}}` without `max` no longer overflows a container narrower than `minWidth`. A lone column now shrinks to the container width, as it already did with `max`, so a phone no longer scrolls sideways. In a container that takes its width from its content (an inline-block, or a flex item with no width), an uncapped Grid is now as wide as its content instead of `minWidth`, as a capped Grid already was.
- Page template headers on a phone: when a page title and its action do not fit one row, the action moves under the title instead of squeezing it, in the service-jobs table and the grouped issues table. Wide screens look the same as before.
- `astryx experimental icon new-set --from` run again on a set whose library dropped an icon now removes that icon in every look from the generated module and its declarations. Before, the filled (or other variant) export stayed behind and named a library export that no longer exists, so importing the integration package failed.
- In the Tool: IDE page template, the editor's and terminal's scrollbars no longer sit under the properties panel's resize handle. On desktop the editor and terminal keep a small gap before the handle, so the whole scrollbar scrolls; before, a press on the half of the scrollbar nearest the handle resized the panel. Mobile, where the panel is hidden, is unchanged.
- The incident console page template works on a phone and its buttons act. On a narrow screen its header controls wrap onto their own rows, and choosing an incident opens its details in a bottom sheet instead of doing nothing. The inspector's next-step button ("Mark mitigated", "Resolve", "Reopen") moves the incident to its next status, and "Escalate" and "Declare incident" confirm with a demo toast that marks where to connect the real action. Rows show each incident's start date and time instead of a relative time that grew stale. The template stays unready for now.
- `astryx init` next steps and the `doctor` theme hint name the project's own install command (`pnpm add`, `yarn add`, `bun add` or `npm install`) instead of `npm install` in every project. An install command the CLI prints no longer adds a `@"*"` range to a package name.
- `astryx init`'s theme step now names the theme at the project's Core release, as `theme add` and `doctor` already do. In a project that pins Core 0.7.10, it prints `npm install -E @astryxdesign/theme-neutral@0.7.10`. Before, it named no version, so npm picked the newest theme, which needs a newer Core than the project has, and the install failed. `doctor`'s hint for an app with no theme and `theme build`'s hint to install a missing theme follow the same rule.
- `astryx init --user` on a skills folder you cannot write (such as a read-only `~/.agents/skills`) now fails with `ERR_WRITE_FAILED` and a message that names the path, the reason, and what to change, instead of a bare `EACCES` line with `ERR_UNKNOWN`.
- Nine page templates fit a 320 px phone without their content scrolling sideways, and a tenth scrolls less. Their responsive grids now pair the minimum column width with a column cap, so a column narrower than the screen shrinks to fit instead of overflowing. The inline form wizard's checkbox descriptions now wrap instead of being cut to one line. Screens up to 1920 px wide look the same as before; above about 2,380 px the library's six category cards fill their row instead of leaving an empty column.
- `astryx docs global/problems` now also explains the "installing CLI release" line outside a project, where the astryx command you started downloads its own Core once. Before, the page said only that a project's own CLI could not start, and told you to install the project's dependencies.
- `astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor` name a theme module that `theme build` wrote (`.js`, `.mjs` or `.cjs`) and that imports TypeScript source, as built themes from a CLI before this one do (`built_module_imports_typescript`, a `next` note with the weight of `relative_import_not_shipped`), with the file, the line, and the fix.
- `astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` now resolve every relative import of the modules a package ships the way an app's bundler does, against the files npm packs (for an installed package, its files on disk). Run in the package's own folder, they used to pass an import such as `./icons` that the tarball leaves out, because the file was on disk there. Each import no shipped file answers is a `relative_import_not_shipped` note marked `next`, naming the importing file, the import, and that the file is not in the package. It fails `integration check --strict --next` now; the next minor release makes it a warning, which fails `--strict`. When npm cannot be asked, an import whose file no `files` entry can reach is still a note, and any other is listed as not checked. `astryx doctor`'s theme owners check now also reads a package theme's stylesheets, whose `@import` and `url()` references it never followed, and warns that the built module loads but names a file the package does not ship. Type-only imports are skipped; `./icons` resolving to `icons/index.js` is fine.
- The kanban-board page template stacks its lanes top to bottom at the full width below 768px, so a phone shows whole lanes instead of one lane and a cut edge of the next. A swipe that starts on a card now scrolls the board; a finger lifts a card with a long press and carries it to another lane. A mouse drags as before, and the layout at 768px and wider is unchanged.
- Keyboard users can reach two template controls. The kanban board's column info icons use InfoTip, so each is a named button that Tab reaches and Enter opens, where before Tab stopped on a hidden, unnamed icon. In the side-navigation shell, a conversation's options button sits in the row's actions slot and shows while focus is in the row, so Tab reaches it; focus returns to it after its menu or delete confirmation closes, and the conversation link keeps its status in its name.
- `astryx integration check` and `astryx integration verify` handle very large icon libraries (tens of thousands of exports). The check scans every file of the package for contribution metadata instead of stopping after 5,000 files with a warning that failed `--strict`. Verify reads npm's pack list from a file, so a package of any size no longer fails with `ENOBUFS`, and both commands keep a bounded number of parsed modules in memory, so they run in Node's default memory. An icon set that re-exports icons from its own package name (`export {X} from '<own package>'`) is now checked through the package's `exports`, as Node resolves it, instead of being listed as not checked.
- The messaging shell page template, still marked not ready, now works as an app. AppShell owns its side navigation of channels and direct messages, so on a phone the channels open from the navigation toggle. Picking a direct message shows that conversation, sending a message or a thread reply adds it to the page, a message's replies open its thread (in a drawer on narrow screens), and selecting a conversation clears its unread count. The page no longer uses raw elements or a local style object, and the actions without a real destination show a demo toast.
- Card, Center, Collapsible, Divider and Blockquote examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit. Wide columns look the same.
- TextArea, TextInput, Switch, SegmentedControl and TabList examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit (and the status-variant columns wrap). Wide columns look the same.
- Layout header, footer, content and panel examples and the chat layout examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit. Wide columns look the same.
- Toolbar, TopNav (and its item, menu and mega menu examples), Table, Step and Stepper examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit, and the custom-content stepper's two side-by-side fields wrap. Wide columns look the same.
- The AspectRatio examples other than its showcase, the Avatar, AvatarStatusDot, Grid, GridSpan, the clipboard, hotkeys, streaming text and container reveal hook examples, Markdown, OverflowList, Resizable and ScrollableArea examples no longer overflow a narrow column: each keeps its demo width but now shrinks to fit (and rows of avatars wrap); the Resizable showcase's sidebar can grow to two thirds of its card, so the handle stays inside a narrow card. Wide columns look the same.
- The payment form and checkout wizard page templates no longer squeeze their form beside the order summary on a narrow screen before script runs: the summary wraps below the form instead. Wide screens look the same.
- In a project, the update notice and `doctor`'s matching fixes now upgrade every Astryx package the project lists that is released with Core, such as its themes, beside Core and the CLI. Before, the command upgraded only Core and the CLI, so following it left a theme on the old release; its exact Core peer no longer matched, and `doctor` reported it.
- The npm commands that the CLI runs for itself now use npm's own `noproxy` setting. These commands install a release into the CLI's per-user cache and ask the registry for versions. Before, when the shell's `NO_PROXY` named the npm registry but npm's own settings sent the registry through a proxy, npm went straight to the registry. Then the first command that needed the cache, such as `astryx component` outside a project, waited until npm's time limit and failed.
- The payment form's promo code "Apply" button keeps its full label on a phone; the promo field gives way instead.
- Page templates keep their text on a 320 px phone. The filtered table no longer scrolls sideways on a phone, buttons in three templates (the vertical form wizard's cover, the editor and the composition dashboard) keep their full labels instead of cutting off, the work item's success criteria and the report wizard's option descriptions wrap instead of cutting off after one line, and the canvas editor's document tabs show their full name in a tooltip when a name is cut. Wide screens look the same as before.
- Theme editor pictures show responsive charts drawn: each page draws in a window of its own until it is quiet, and its script is held while the whole page is pictured, so a chart no longer starts over and is pictured empty. The page stays laid out for the 1280 × 900 window.
- The theme editor's pictures and the render stylesheet cut read a media query's condition the way the browser does: `not` before a condition in parentheses, `or`, and nesting. A rule under `(not ((min-width: 768px) and (min-height: 500px)))` no longer counts as matching in the 1280px picture window.
- The principles doc says settings groups use Section, not Card, matching the Card and Section docs.
- ProgressBar and CircularProgress fills reach 3:1 against their track (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11, non-text contrast). ProgressBar's status fills take the status text colors, and its neutral fill, like CircularProgress's, takes the secondary text color instead of the disabled one, which is the bar's track color in dark mode in Theme Neutral and Theme Stone and under 3:1 on the bar's track in every bundled theme in light mode. A disabled bar takes the same fill and dims its track and fill to half opacity, as a disabled Slider or Switch track does, and a disabled ring dims as a whole, center content included, so each reads quieter than a neutral one. A mark on any fill but accent takes the surface color; in Theme Butter and Theme Stone, a mark on a status fill takes that status's on-color. CircularProgress draws every variant on the muted background track, ProgressBar's base track, because some themes' status muted colors are the status color itself. In Theme Neutral, Theme Butter and Theme Stone a dark neutral or disabled fill takes a lighter neutral stop, Butter's and Stone's status fills take the theme's status colors, Stone's accent fill takes a blue stop that reaches 3:1, and the CLI's bundled theme templates match.
- `astryx doctor integration components` no longer reports a documented string union that leaves out a value the code marks `@deprecated` in every place the type takes it from.
- When two installed packages both declare the same provider ID in their manifests, the warning and `astryx doctor`'s fix now say that if they are one integration installed under two names, keep one of the two dependencies, and otherwise change one package's providerId. When a provider ID comes from a package name, the advice is unchanged.
- The not-found hint refreshes its name index after an imported doc dependency changes on the minimum supported Node version.
- A stop signal sent to the CLI's own process while it installs the release matching a project's Core, such as a time limit's SIGTERM, now stops the run. Before, the run went on once npm returned, answered, and exited 0 to a caller that had already given up: npm runs synchronously, so the signal waited for the install to end, and by then its handler was gone. The handler now stays until the signal is delivered, and the hand-off lets it stop the run before it answers.
- A release that failed to install is tried again at once when npm's registry changed since the failure, instead of waiting 2 or 10 minutes, and the reason names the registry npm tried.
- Remove six page templates that were never marked ready: not-found, access-denied, error-page, welcome-portal, run-console and review-workspace. Page templates will come from the design team instead. None of them was in a release, and no command offered them as a start.
- `astryx experimental render` carries the `.mts`, `.cts` and `.cjs` modules a page imports, and `--reverse` gives them back and follows their imports. The render loaded them but left them out of the file, so the page came back with `exact: false` and those modules missing. A file that carries one says render format 2, so an earlier CLI that reads render formats names the CLI that reads it instead of calling the file damaged; every other file stays format 1.
- `astryx experimental render` carries every image, font and media file a carried module's strings or a carried stylesheet name by a relative path inside the folder that holds the carried files, also when the page did not show it in this render: a branch the page did not take, or a stylesheet rule no element uses. Such files now ship in the rendered file, up to 8 MB each, as a shown image does; a larger one, one whose bytes are not an image, font or media file, or one it cannot read, is left out with a `not-embedded` warning that names the file that names it. A name that climbs above that folder is not the page's file and is not carried, as `--reverse` reads it too. `--reverse` reads the same names with the same scan, so such a page used to come back with `exact: false` and those files missing.
- A page render that draws overlays open waits for React's queued work before it reads them, and no longer compares the page's markup turn after turn: a page whose overlays have settled is read at once, so the theme editor's sample page and sheet render as fast as before while each render stays the same every time. The theme editor's contrast checks reuse each part's token reads within a command.
- A page render that draws overlays open (the theme editor's sample page and sheet) reads each overlay once its update has finished. Before, on a busy machine it could read an overlay between two renders, so the same theme could render to different pages: `undo` then left the sample page different from before the change.
- `astryx experimental render` outside a project carries the modules a page imports from above its own folder, and the files those modules import, as long as they are inside the current folder. A page restored with its neighbours (`report-restored/app/report/page.tsx` beside `report-restored/components/`) and rendered again by the command its file prints used to leave those modules out, so the new file came back with `exact: false`. Where the render reads the page's `tsconfig.json` and `public/` images does not change.
- `astryx experimental render` renders a page outside a project whose StyleX reads Astryx theme variables (`@astryxdesign/core/theme/tokens.stylex`), as many templates do. Such a page stopped with "The page does not compile: Could not resolve the path to the imported file", because the StyleX compiler looked for Core beside the page, where outside a project there is none. The compiler now gets the theme file the page loads from the CLI's own Core, and the page renders the same as it does inside a project.
- `astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` read a folder or file whose name begins with two dots (`..x`) as one inside the folder that holds it, where they took it for the folder above. A page in such a folder keeps its own folder as the root of the files it carries, so the file it writes reverses; a file above it stays out, named in a `not-embedded` warning. The note at the top of a page rendered outside a project names the page by its path among the files it lists (`app/x/page.tsx`), where it named only the file (`page.tsx`) and pointed at it as the file to edit.
- `astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` read path aliases from the config TypeScript reads for the page: the nearest `tsconfig.json` (else `jsconfig.json`) at or above it, through its `extends` (a path with or without `.json`, a package's config, or a list, the later one winning, with `${configDir}`), and, behind a solution-style `tsconfig.json` (`"files": []` with `references`, as Vite sets up), the referenced project that includes the page. A page whose aliases live in `tsconfig.app.json` or in an extended config used to fail, with `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, or with `ERR_RENDER_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` when the alias looks like a package name (`@data/rows`), although `tsc` and the app's build found its imports.
- `astryx experimental render --reverse` finds the embedded source in a file whose script tag a minifier or another tool rewrote: an unquoted `type` (`<script type=application/x-astryx-source>`), or an attribute before `type`. Such a file used to come back as a page rebuilt from its markup (text and layout only) instead of the exact source.
- `astryx experimental render` gives a relative or aliased import with `?raw` the file's text, and a `.css` file imported with `?inline` its text (not added to the page), as Vite does by itself, however the import names it. It used to give a JSON file's object for `?raw`, fail on a text file such as `notes.txt?raw`, and refuse a `.css` file with `?inline` as CSS Modules. A package import with `?raw`, and a Sass, Less or package stylesheet with `?inline`, stay as before. Any other query loads the file as it loads without one, as before: an image, font or media file as its address (`?url`, `?inline`, `?w=400`), a module as itself. `--reverse` gives back the files the render carries; a `?raw` file of a kind a render never carries, such as `notes.md`, is named in a `not-embedded` warning.
- On Windows, `astryx experimental render` and the experimental theme editor now transform the page's own files. The renderer read every file as outside the project, because the module loader named files with forward slashes while the project path used backslashes, so no file was transformed. A page or theme that imported a stylesheet then failed with `Unknown file extension ".css"`, and StyleX, image and JSON imports were not handled either.
- `astryx experimental render` and `--reverse` write in one step. A render writes the HTML file under a temporary name beside it, then gives it its name, so a reader or another run never finds half a file: two renders of one page to one file both succeed, where one could be refused because the file "already exists and was not written by a render". A restore writes its new folder the same way, so restores run at the same time each get a folder of their own, also when they restore with `--out` into folders under one new folder, where some were refused, and a restore stopped part-way leaves no folder behind, so the same command works again. A run stopped between its write and its rename leaves a hidden temporary file or folder, which the next run to the same place, on the same computer and in the same container or sandbox, removes once that run's process is gone. A render still never replaces an HTML file this user cannot write, and the file it replaces keeps its permission bits; it now needs to make a file in the HTML file's folder, so a folder this user cannot write is refused, and the refusal names it. Every copy a restore writes, except the page at its target, lands in the one new folder, including a copy of the page that a path alias places; such a copy outside it is refused with nothing written.
- In right-to-left pages, the settings dialog's Reset buttons, the inbox's Reply action and Send button, and the tree list settings example's Documentation chevron now point the right way: these icons mean back, reply, send or go into, so they mirror. Left-to-right pages look the same.
- In right-to-left pages, the canvas editor's artboard no longer goes blank and the progress dashboard's milestone timeline no longer draws its labels over the bars: both keep a left-to-right layout, as a design canvas and a chart should (the same page's scope burndown too). Left-to-right pages look the same.
- The dashboard scorecard template's trend charts keep their y-axis labels whole with a small font up to 16 px, wide fonts included: the labels are compact and in the series' own scale ("6M" and "1.4M" for values stored in thousands, matching the heading's "4,350k") instead of 6000 and 1400, and the axis gutter is 52 px instead of 40 px. The tooltip still shows exact values.
- The dashboard scorecard template fits a phone screen: its trend charts shrink to a narrow column instead of running past the screen edge, a chart's change line moves under its title when the card is narrow, the header's generated date moves to its own line instead of squeezing into a sliver, and on the narrowest phones Export moves under the period control instead of running past the edge. Tablet and desktop layouts look the same.
- Search: a family's root now comes before a part of its own family whenever the part adds nothing the query asked for, also when the part's name scores higher. `astryx search "code sample"` lists CodeBlock before Code. The part still comes first when the query is the part's exact name (`astryx search code`), holds a word only the part's name has, or writes the part's name of two or more words as one word, as is or misspelled (`astryx search "breadcrumbitm"` keeps BreadcrumbItem first). The new order changes no match, score or reason. The `search()` doc page now describes this order, so it also matches a few of those words (such as "family" and "root"), and such a query, in `search` or `build`, counts one more match.
- Search: a family's root now leads a part of its own family when the part adds nothing the query asked for: `astryx search tabs` lists TabList before Tab. A query that holds a word only the part's name has, in any plural form, such as "item" for ListItem or "statuses" for FieldStatus, keeps the part first. Scores, reasons and match counts are unchanged; only order inside a band moves.
- Search: a match whose name of two or more words the query writes as one word now comes first, also inside a longer query. `astryx search "TableSortableTable with pagination"`, `astryx search "table-sortable-table with pagination"` and `astryx search "tokens-color for dark mode"` list that block or doc first. Words written apart stay plain words (`astryx search "multiline text input"` keeps its order), and so does a one-word name such as `card`. A name inside a longer name the query holds, such as a block's display name or a doc's title, does not come first. Matches, scores, reasons and counts are unchanged; `build` is unchanged.
- `astryx search` reads another entry's name as that entry's evidence. A block no longer ranks above a component only because it uses components that match the query's words. A guide whose title sits in the query no longer takes the title's rank when the query also names a component the guide does not answer: it ranks by the words it matches, so a guide whose title is its only match yields to that component. Two cases keep the guide first: a component word that is also a doc's name (`link`, `icon`, `theme` or `calendar`), which may be asking for the docs, and a guide whose own name is a query word. `build` is unchanged.
- Search: when matches of one domain tie for first place on score and on the query words they matched, the one whose own name holds more of the query's words now comes first, instead of the first by name. `astryx search "side navigation sidebar"` lists SideNav first. A first result that matched the whole query, as a name, keyword or title, or whose title the query holds, keeps its place: `astryx search "date picker"` keeps Calendar first, and `astryx search "how do i generate a palette"` keeps the theme authoring guide first. A part of the first result never takes its place this way. Matches, scores, reasons and counts are unchanged; only the order inside one score band moves.
- `astryx search` reads a one-identifier query written as a component's, type's or icon's name (PascalCase, such as `ThemeProvider`) as its words also when all it matches is text that mentions it, including a code term or table cell a doc's keywords gather. The entry that mentions it stays in the answer, beside the entries its words find. In the lexical ranking, the entry that mentions it, and an entry one of its words names outright, come before every entry its words only match; search's learned order inside a score band still applies, so `astryx search` can list a words-only match above them. A prop's name (camelCase, such as `autoFocus`) keeps only the entries that mention it, as before, and other queries rank exactly as before.
- `astryx search` reads a docs namespace page at the reader's grain. A word the page's text shares with a doc beneath it, which that doc answers at least as strongly, is that doc's evidence, so a namespace page that sums up its guides no longer ranks above the components, templates, hooks and guides it summarizes. Words only the page carries, and its name, title, description and declared keywords, still match it. `build` is unchanged.
- Secondary text now reads on every palette tint. The default light `--color-text-secondary` is `#445564` (was `#4E606F`), so secondary text on a gray Card or any other `--color-background-<hue>` tint meets 4.5:1 over the surface and the page body. The dark value is unchanged. To keep the previous light colour, a theme can set `--color-text-secondary` to `light-dark(#4E606F, #B0B5BB)`.
- The settings dialog template's Delete my account button now asks for confirmation first. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.
- The settings and settings-sidebar page templates no longer offer nav items that lead nowhere. In settings, choosing an item other than Profile no longer moves the selection while the Profile form stays; in settings-sidebar, Notifications, Taxes, Payments and Travel for work no longer open an empty page. A nav item with a section works as before; an item without one shows a demo message and keeps the current item selected, and the current item is marked as the current page for screen readers. The first screen looks the same.
- Settings page template on a phone: the search moves under the title instead of squeezing it until "Settings" breaks mid-word.
- Controls that did nothing in two settings page templates now respond with a demo message that says what would happen: the three Save buttons on the settings page, and Professional hosting tools on the sidebar settings page. The sidebar settings page's back arrow and drill-in chevrons now point the right way in right-to-left languages.
- The setup reminder (`Next step: run … init …`, shown at most once a day in a project that has not run `init`) now prints on stderr before the command's own output instead of after it. Agents often keep only the start of a long answer (`2>&1 | head`), so a reminder at the end was cut and the day used up without anyone seeing it. It still never prints under CI, in `--json`, or once the project is set up; a command that fails now shows it too.
- The setup reminder now says why to run `init` now: "Astryx is not set up in this project yet. Next step: run `npx astryx init` now, before you write Astryx code. It asks no questions, prints the getting-started steps, and saves the Astryx guide to AGENTS.md." Before, it said `init` would "install the Astryx agent prompt", which agents read as a file change the user did not ask for, so they kept working without it. The command it names is unchanged, and so are the places it prints.
- Delete in two shell page templates now asks for confirmation first: a conversation's menu in the side-navigation shell and a row's menu in the theme showcase. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.
- When the docs catalog withdraws an integration's docs because one doc fails its checks (such as a flat topic that sets `aliases`), `init` and `upgrade --apply` keep that package's skill copies until the doc loads instead of removing them as leftovers, and when any of its docs does not load, its skills get one note saying so instead of a `replaces` fix.
- `astryx component Flex` names Stack first. Stack's search card now lists `Flex`, the name Chakra UI and Mantine use for the same row-or-column layout part, so the lookup that misses suggests Stack before Layout.
- A shipped doc's stored parse is used only when the installed zod release is the one that made it. With another zod release, the CLI parses the doc, so the answer is always what a fresh parse gives.
- `astryx swizzle` without Core says what to do. Outside a project, it says the folder is outside a project and that swizzle copies source into an app project that installs `@astryxdesign/core`; in a project that has not installed Core, it says to install it. It no longer tells you to work inside the design system's own repository. The error code stays `ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND`.
- The dashboard, dashboard-cohort-funnel, dashboard-composition, dashboard-progress and editor page templates, and the Table in Card block, keep their look with the Table bleed fix in Core: each Table is now the card's direct child, so it still reaches the card's top or bottom edge.
- Delete in two table page templates now asks for confirmation first: the support inbox's row, conversation and bulk Delete, and Delete issue in the grouped table's row menu. After you confirm, a demo message says what would happen; Cancel does nothing.
- The table page templates give screen readers more structure: seven pages that had no main landmark now mark their content as main, `table-tree`'s sidebar headings follow the page heading without skipping a level, and the icon-only status and actions columns in `table` and `table-grouped` get visually hidden header names. No visual change.
- `astryx template <name> <path>` and `astryx template --cdn <path>` accept an absolute path inside the project root, also through a symlinked project folder. It is written exactly as its relative path. An absolute path outside the project is still refused with `ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL`. For `astryx template <name> <path>`, the receipt says the path was written as its relative path (`data.givenPath` in `--json`), and the refusal names a command that writes inside the project and the command that prints the source without writing anything. In a Next app whose `pageExtensions` include `tsx` (the default), the named path is one Next builds and serves: a page goes to the App Router folder (`app/<name>`, or `src/app/<name>`, inside the route group with the root layout when that folder has none of its own), or, with only the Pages Router, to the page file `pages/<name>.tsx`; a block goes to `app/components/<name>` with a root `app/` folder, `components/<name>` with only a root `pages/` folder, else `src/components/<name>`. Every other project gets `src/pages/<name>` and `src/components/<name>`. When that path exists or another page already serves its URL, the name becomes `<name>-2`, `<name>-3` and so on. The path is quoted in the command when a shell would read it otherwise, as with a route group folder. Next refuses to build when its `app` and `pages` folders are in different folders, and when two pages serve one URL. For `--cdn`, the receipt is unchanged, and the refusal names `astryx template --cdn cdn.template.html`.
- Dashboard templates show every chart label whole: the progress timeline's "Today" label gets room above the plot, and Y axes wide enough for their widest tick no longer clip it.
- Outside a project, when a tool runs the CLI for you, `template`, `build` and `theme eject` no longer name an integration the tool approves and installs as a missing dependency. `render` already gives the page that integration, so the page renders without installing it. Also, `render` now takes an approved integration only from the tool's package set itself. Before, it also took one from a folder above that set.
- In a project with no Next route folder, the page path that `astryx build` and `astryx template` name is now the file the copy writes (`src/pages/<id>.tsx`), not a folder holding `page.tsx`; a block's path is now its file (`app/components/<id>.tsx`, `components/<id>.tsx` or `src/components/<id>.tsx`) in every project. An import of the named path, such as `import Page from './pages/settings'`, now resolves, and a name an import already resolves to (a folder's index or a file with another extension) moves to `<id>-2`. Next App Router pages keep their route folder, and Pages Router pages were already files.
- A `{@link …}` in a template's description no longer prints as written. `astryx template` (the list, `--skeleton`, and a template read), `astryx build`, `astryx search` and `astryx component <Name> --blocks` resolve it to the command that opens the doc it names, as `astryx docs` does: with the project's command in text, and as the bare `astryx …` command in `--json`. The JSON shape does not change.
- A template doc's `{@command …}` and `{@pm …}` tokens no longer print as written. `astryx template` (the list and `--skeleton`), `astryx build` and `astryx search` show the command with the project's command in text, as `astryx docs` does, and as the bare `astryx …` command in `--json`; the JSON shape does not change. `build` and `search` text show every description's commands with the project's command too. A template's source still prints byte for byte.
- `astryx template <name> ~/<path>` reads `~/` as the home folder, as a shell does.
