A caller that passed `~` through unexpanded no longer gets a folder named `~` in the project: a home path outside the project is refused with the commands that work, like any absolute path outside it, and one inside the project is written there. `template --cdn` reads it the same way. To write into a folder that is really named `~` in the project, write it as `./~/<path>`.
- A copy of the `canvas-editor` page template no longer carries two comments about its icon imports that no longer described them: one on aliasing `File`, one on which Lucide icon draws the rotation angle. The template now names its icons by meaning, and its copy draws the same icons as before.
- A page template's keyword now means one concept. When build chooses the start and its alternatives, a multi-word keyword counts only as the whole phrase (skipping stopwords and one-letter words inside it), so its single words no longer count for other templates. Core templates' keywords are migrated: lists of words are split into single keywords, terms that mean something different as a whole (such as "getting started" or "reading pane") stay phrases, and keywords that weren't true of their template are removed. The template-doc field reference says how to write keywords.
- Four Core page templates no longer list keywords for things their page does not render, so `astryx build` and `astryx search` stop offering them for those ideas. AI Chat Conversation drops "citations", "reasoning" and "playground"; Kanban Board drops "swimlane" and "backlog"; Page Editor drops "drag and drop"; Theme Showcase drops "tokens", "palette" and "typography". The Page Editor and Theme Showcase descriptions now say what the page renders: blocks reorder with move up and move down, and the showcase shows sample product screens in the active theme.
- `astryx doctor` warns on a `{@link}` in a template's description that names no doc, and `doctor integration validate` lists it as a `next` note, so `integration check --strict` fails on it only from the next minor release.
- 37 page templates (the tool templates other than `incident-console`, the content templates other than `work-item-detail`, the form, gallery and hero, login, settings and AI chat templates, plus `blank` and `theme-showcase`) give screen readers clearer structure: each marks its content area (`LayoutContent`, or the page's `Center` root where it has no content area) as the main landmark, has exactly one level-1 heading in each state it shows (a phone section view, a sign-in step, the signed-in state), and has a heading outline with no skipped levels. Titles keep their look (`accessibilityLevel`, or `Text` rendered as `h1`); pages without a visible title get a visually hidden one. Also: icon-only columns in `editor` and `theme-showcase` get visually hidden header names, and `documentation-design` names each example's tab list. No visual change.
- Action buttons that did nothing in four page templates now respond with a confirmation toast: Restock, Fulfill item, Create label, Refund and Send Invoice on the order detail page, the next-step action in the service-jobs detail panel, Dispute this line on the invoice line items page, and Format Document in the IDE workspace.
- Action buttons and menu items that did nothing in eleven more page templates now respond with a toast that names the demo action: Add to Cart and Buy it now on the product detail page, Publish in the page editor, the sign-in, plan, export and connected-app actions in the settings dialog, Sign In, Google Pay, PayPal and the promo code's Apply on the payment form, Save & exit, Crop image and Preview on device in the vertical form wizard, the social sign-in buttons on both login pages, Share in the file explorer, the AI chat landing page's settings menu and composer, and Pin, Rename and Archive in the side-nav shell's conversation menu. On the work item page, Add subtask and each attachment's Edit name their demo action, Cancel clears the comment, and Comment confirms it and clears the field. The settings dialog's search-result chevron mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
- 78 template buttons that did nothing when pressed now say what would happen, as the other template demo actions do: the example toolbar buttons of the `documentation-design` page template, and the buttons with no handler in the Button, ButtonGroup, Center, IconButton, Layout, MediaTheme, Section, Stack, Theme, Toolbar and VisuallyHidden example blocks, show a "Demo: …" toast. A destructive one (delete, archive, or a destructive-variant demo) first asks for confirmation; Cancel does nothing.
- More template buttons that did nothing when pressed now show a `Demo:` toast that says what would happen. Archive and Delete ask first with a confirm dialog, then show the toast. Overflow menu items run the same action as their buttons. Upgrade is a link. Fixed blocks: OverflowListShowcase, OverflowListOverflowDropdownActions, OverflowListCollapseFromStartList, OverflowListCappedToolbar, TooltipActionBarTooltips, BannerWithActionButton, BannerSectionVariant, BannerCollapsibleContent, useOverflowHookUsage, useContainerRevealHookUsage, useListFocusHookUsage, TopNavWithLogo, TopNavHoverMenu, TopNavMenuShowcase, TokenizerEndContent, StepContent, useOverlayHookUsage, OverlayShowcase, OverlayHoverReveal, ChatComposerFullFeatured, ChatComposerFooterActions and ChatComposerFlat. No pages change.
- The Table Filter template and the Avatar and LinkProvider example blocks show a "Demo: …" toast for their demo actions instead of calling `alert()`, so the click still responds when the page runs in a frame that blocks browser dialogs.
- The technical documentation page template now teaches the real setup. Its AI setup prompt no longer asks for a style compiler, which contradicted the article's own precompiled-CSS step, and its theming example uses the real `Theme` component from `@astryxdesign/core/theme` with a theme package instead of a `ThemeProvider` that Astryx does not export. Its prerequisites now name React 19 or later, which Core requires.
- Three menu items in two page templates now respond instead of doing nothing. In the grouped issues table, "Edit issue" and "Duplicate" confirm with a demo toast. On the kanban board, "Assign to me" confirms with a demo toast. Each toast handler carries a comment that marks where to connect the real action.
- Page templates now have no horizontal overflow on a 390 px phone, with touch or a mouse. In the service-health, data, funnel-and-cohort and program-status dashboards and the kanban board, the header controls now wrap onto a second row instead of widening the page past the screen edge, and on the data dashboard a section heading's hint is no longer squeezed into a narrow column beside the heading. Desktop layouts are unchanged. A check builds every ready page template into an app and runs it in a 390 px phone emulation, with touch and with a mouse, so a template that widens the page past a phone's screen fails before release.
- The `dashboard-scorecard` and `dashboard-progress` templates no longer wrap whole page sections in cards, as Card's own guidance says: the scorecard's goal list, and the progress page's summary panels and workstream table, sit in plain page sections under their headings. Repeated items keep their cards: the scorecard's metric tiles, trend charts and commentary notes.
- The `dashboard-scorecard` and `dashboard-progress` templates draw their trend lines as straight segments between the measured points, so a line no longer bends between measured points.
- With longer, translated labels at phone width, the form wizard, vertical form wizard, technical documentation and table templates keep their buttons in full: their header, footer and toolbar rows wrap instead of cutting labels or pushing controls off screen. The canvas editor's header keeps its save note and Export at full width, and the badge and stack direction examples wrap their rows. In English at 390 and 1280 px only the form wizard's last step changes: Back and "Create workspace", which were cut, now show in full. On narrower phones, English rows that were already tight wrap instead of cutting a label or running past the edge: the technical documentation's AI assistance row from about 375 px (its More options menu button moves to a second line), the vertical form wizard's header from about 330 px (Save & exit moves to a second line), and at 320 px the form wizard's Back and Next (its Cancel moves to a second line just below 320 px). The badge and stack direction examples wrap in columns narrower than about 295 and 335 px.
- `astryx theme build` names an import through a path alias (`@/lib/c`, `~/lib/c`) as one the theme loader does not map, never as a package to install; expands a quoted glob to the theme sources it matches in its suggestion; and counts the fonts macOS and Windows ship, from one table by platform, as system fonts in its note on fonts named but not loaded.
- `astryx theme build` refuses a blank or whitespace-only `--out` (it wrote files named by the spaces alone), and its note on fonts named but not loaded leaves out the families a local theme's own font stylesheet loads (`<slug>.fonts.css` beside the source, the stylesheet `theme add` imports). `astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` also treat Segoe UI Light, Semilight, Semibold and Black as system fonts, the faces Windows installs as families of their own, so neither reports them as not loaded.
- `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, custom properties that read each other (a token with a fallback reading itself, two tokens, a half of a [light, dark] pair, tokens and local tokens, a part's own custom property), a pseudo-element near a known one (as that one misspelled), a pseudo-element missing from the CLI's selector data (as possibly newer than the CLI), a pseudo-element inside `:is()`, `:where()`, `:not()` or `:has()`, a pseudo-class after `::highlight()`, `:window-inactive` after any highlight but `::selection`, a token name that does not start with exactly two dashes, and an empty token value. A pseudo-class after `::search-text` or `::scroll-marker-group` is no longer warned. A child theme's own build names the file and line of a value the theme it extends writes. A null value's warning says what it builds: a null property leaves the base theme's value, while a null token is kept by the browser as the token's value, so most properties that read it act as if they were not set (text keeps the surrounding color, a background goes transparent) and a font family reading it falls back to the browser's default font.
- `astryx theme build` counts the fonts macOS and Windows ship for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (such as PingFang SC, Hiragino Sans, Microsoft YaHei and 微软雅黑) as system fonts, so it no longer names them as fonts the theme does not load.
- `astryx theme build` warns a `[light, dark]` pair with any half that is no color (a size, a duration, a word that is no color name), not sizes only, since `light-dark()` takes colors only. A value the build cannot place on a line of the theme file is named as computed in it, and the theme it extends is named only when it holds that very value.
- `astryx theme build` reads a font family name as CSS reads it (`Gill\ Sans` is Gill Sans), names as not loaded a family the theme holds in its own property and reads with `var()`, and builds a theme bound with `let` or `var` that is never assigned again as it builds a `const` (one assigned again is refused naming that, not as an icon registry it sets).
- `astryx theme build`: a doc module given as the theme (`oceanTheme.doc.mjs`, or a file whose default export is a doc such as `{type: 'theme', name, description}`) is refused with `ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming it as a doc and the theme source beside it to build, and nothing is written.
- `theme build` of a missing file in a folder whose files another command generates (their first comment says which command writes them) says the file is generated and names that command, instead of offering a blank theme template. `doctor` still compares such a local theme's outputs with its source, and its fix for a stale or missing one runs the exact command that writes it, never a `theme build`. `doctor`'s fix when the themes folder cannot be read names the theme the message names (for a generated one, its command), never `<slug>`. A font stylesheet's local `@import` (a file beside it, `url(faces.css)`, or a package stylesheet such as `@fontsource/inter/index.css`, resolved from where the stylesheet really is) is followed and its fonts proven; a URL import is an external font service, and a local import doctor cannot follow, or one past the files it follows, is a warning, never a failure. The help and docs say `editor show <name> --png` takes pictures of real components.
- `astryx theme build`: building a theme the theme editor made now also says that the build does not write (or, with `--check`, does not check) the theme's app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/`, which the app imports, and names the `astryx experimental theme compile` command that builds the theme and writes the copy.
- `astryx theme build`: a plain-object theme with no `tokens`, a name alone (`export default {name: 'p'}`) or a name and component styles, builds as an empty theme over the base instead of ending with "Cannot convert undefined or null to object".
- `themeBuildFamily` (`astryx theme build --family`) builds each member as it is at that build. Before, a second family build in the same process, such as a tool or a test that builds in process, built a member file changed since the first build from the module the first build had loaded.
- `astryx theme build` names a misspelled field at the line that writes it when the theme object is a member of a const (`all.a`), an element of an array, a branch of a ternary, an object `Object.assign` merges, or a `defineTheme()` argument written any of those ways. `astryx doctor` names each cause when a theme package's built module both imports TypeScript source and has a stylesheet that names a file the package does not ship.
  Plain themes whose bases extend each other in a cycle are refused naming the cycle, instead of a stack overflow or a silent merge. `astryx experimental theme` removes a render folder a killed command left as soon as its maker is known gone (same machine, no such process), not only once it is ten minutes old.
- `astryx theme build` no longer sets the page root's color scheme. A built theme stylesheet used to declare `:root { color-scheme: light dark; }`, so a site that loads it without `reset.css`, and sets no scheme of its own, followed the reader's device: for a dark-mode reader its native controls, links and page canvas turned dark around its own light content. A theme now follows the page's scheme; it still pins it where the page or the Theme provider forces a mode (`html[data-theme="light"|"dark"]`), and a `--family` build drops the same rule from each theme's scope. Apps whose page scheme comes only from `reset.css` see no change, while an app that sets its own `color-scheme` on `html` (in its own CSS layer, as the Tailwind setup does) now keeps it. To follow the device with theme CSS alone, add reset.css or `html { color-scheme: light dark }`.
- `astryx theme build`: its font notices name the typography recipe, written with the project's own runner in text output, and it compares real paths in the disk's own case, so a theme reached through a differently cased path is not reported as missing or as another file.
- `astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` give each file that says a tool generates it (`@generated`, `@partially-generated` or `Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.` in its leading comments) one note with the count and that tool (`--family` and doctor give one per file, however many themes extend it), instead of a warning per setting it writes that does not show as written: that file is not where the fix goes. The build's note reaches text, `--json`, `--check` and `--family` output, and `settingIssues` still lists each setting; doctor's note names the `theme build --check --json` command that lists them. A hand-written theme that a generated one extends keeps its own warnings.
- `astryx theme build` no longer replaces a file it did not write at its default outputs beside the source. A file of your own named like an output (`brand.css` or `brand.js` beside `brand.ts`) used to be silently overwritten; now the build fails with `ERR_FILE_EXISTS`, names the file, and writes nothing. At the default outputs, a file an earlier build wrote is still replaced, an output of the CLI before it was named Astryx included. At a path `--out` names nothing changes: only a file with the current build header is replaced, as before. Beside the source, an output another theme source built there is replaced with a warning naming both sources, as at `--out`. To migrate a project that keeps its own file under an output's name, build to another place with `--out` (for example `--out dist/brand.css`), or move or rename your file. The `--out` refusal no longer suggests building beside the source, which could replace such a file.
- `astryx theme build` and `astryx doctor` no longer warn that a theme's font does not load for Noto Sans, Noto Serif and Noto Sans Mono (system fonts of Android, ChromeOS and Linux) or Cantarell, Ubuntu and Ubuntu Mono (system fonts of Linux). A system font stack that names them needs no font package.
- `astryx theme build`: the import hint is given only for a load failure that is an unresolved import, and `@fontsource-variable/<name>` is read as loading `<Name> Variable`, the family that package declares, not `<Name>`.
- `astryx theme build`: a theme module that throws from a microtask it queues while it loads is a refused load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`), not a crash; a listener a theme module adds to `process` (`process.on('exit', …)`, `beforeExit`) goes with its load, so it no longer sets the command's exit code, prints after the `--json` envelope, or keeps the command from ending. `--out` naming a stylesheet's source map (`p.css.map`) is refused, and a slip after `.css` (`p.css.bak`) is told the stylesheet name meant (`p.css`, not `p.css.css`).
  `astryx experimental theme compile` refuses a theme whose own values throw when read (a `tokens` getter or Proxy) as the build does, with no stack trace or `ERR_UNKNOWN`.
- `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the form that works, more part keys a browser drops or Core misreads: a vendor property written without its dash, a pseudo name in capitals, something after a pseudo-element, two pseudo-elements, an escaped pseudo name, the custom property `--`, an empty key, and a block under a key that nests none. The output is the same as before. A `--family` build with such a key in a member builds, with each warning naming the member's file, where it stopped on an unknown error before. A default export that is a Promise of a theme is named as one, instead of a theme without a name.
- `astryx theme build` (and `astryx experimental theme compile`, which builds the same way):
  - A theme that gives null for a part or a style key's block is refused at the line that gives it, never a crash. A null property or token value keeps its meaning (it is written as it is) and is warned at its line.
  - A style key no element carries is warned: a value a closed prop never takes (`size:xxl` on Button, which takes sm, md and lg) and a pseudo-class written as a style key (`':hover'`, which goes inside one: `base: {':hover': …}`).
  - A named pipe, a device or a socket where an output or `--out` goes is refused at once, never opened.
  - `--out out/.css` is told to give the stylesheet a name. An `--out` that starts with an unexpanded `~` is warned: the build writes in the project's `~` folder, as before, and the warning names that folder and the home folder path to give instead.
  - A theme with no name is refused as one, at its line.
  - Apple Color Emoji and Noto Color Emoji count as the systems' own fonts.
- `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, more values a browser drops: a part property that builds dash-first without a vendor prefix (`Color`), a token or part value that is no text (an object, a boolean, NaN, an array in a part), a [light, dark] pair with a missing half or another count, a token that reads itself, and a token's `var()` that no token sets. A pseudo-class after a pseudo-element that takes one (`::file-selector-button:hover`) is no longer warned, and only `:hover` and `:active` in capitals are. A warning about a value the theme takes from the theme it extends no longer gives a line of the file that extends it, and a `--family` build names it once, at the member that writes it. A tokens map spread from a defined theme's tokens no longer trips over Core's own private copies in it.
- `astryx theme build` reads a base theme that the same file defines as a const, and that the theme's `extends` names (directly, or through `defineTheme(...)` or a wrapper), as the theme it extends, not as the theme itself: a setting the base's variant beats is named, and the theme's own lookup never reads that base. A base that a call returns (`extends: makeBase()`) or that a helper's object names is still read as the theme's own.
- `theme build` through a CLI installed for the computer now writes the same files as a CLI installed beside Core. It reads the component docs and types of the Core it builds with, which is the project's. So a theme that gives a component a custom variant gets its `.variants.d.ts` type declarations. Before, that CLI read them only from a Core beside it, which it does not have. It wrote no variant declarations, and `doctor` and `theme build --check` reported a theme built by another CLI as stale. The built module's doc comment now names `astryx theme build` rather than the command that ran the build, so builds through different package managers or tools write the same module.
- `astryx theme build` now writes a built theme module that loads in any bundler and in plain Node. A local module the built module imports (an icon registry, a component icon slot value, or the helpers they import) that is TypeScript or JSX is compiled to JavaScript named after its source (`icons.tsx` → `icons.tsx.js`) in a folder beside the built module named for it (`w98.modules` beside `w98.js`, whatever `--out` names the stylesheet), at the place each source has under the folder that holds the theme and its compiled sources, so every compiled module has a path of its own: `import { icons } from './icons'` with `icons.tsx` beside the theme becomes `import { icons } from './w98.modules/icons.tsx.js'`, and a helper it imports becomes `w98.modules/helper.ts.js`. Each local import names its file with its extension. Before, the built module kept the TypeScript import, so an app whose bundler does not compile TypeScript from `node_modules` (a plain Next.js app) failed to build after it added the theme. The compiled modules carry the build header, `--check` compares them, and a file of your own at a compiled module's path is never replaced (that import stays as written, with a warning saying so). A theme with no local module writes the same outputs as before; package imports stay as they are. `--family` builds compile each member's TypeScript registry the same way, in a folder named for the family key.
- `astryx theme build`: a family build names a file it replaces, and builds that would not load say so.
  - A family build over a file with no build header at the `--family-key` name (an output of a CLI before 0.6.7, or a file of your own) still replaces it, now with a warning naming the file. Another theme's outputs there are replaced with a warning naming that theme.
  - A family member whose icon registry is imported without its extension (`import {icons} from './icons'`) builds, as it does on its own.
  - An icon registry that imports an asset (`import check from './check.svg'`, a `.png`, a font) builds; the asset loads as its URL, as a bundler gives it.
  - With `--out` in another folder, a relative icon registry import that nothing answers to from there is warned, with the `--icons-specifier` that names the registry from there.
  - A theme file that exports two named themes and no default warns which theme it builds and which it leaves out.
  - An empty or blank `--icons-specifier` is warned (the built module would import from `""`); `astryx experimental theme compile` refuses it, and an empty or blank `--out`, before building. `theme build --out ''` still writes beside the source.
- `astryx theme build`: what a theme module leaves running no longer decides the command, and three source layouts build.
  - A callback a theme module leaves running that calls `process.exit` after the module loaded is ignored with a warning; one that sets `process.exitCode` does not set the command's; one that throws is a warning, not a crash after the result.
  - A family root may import the family's own stylesheet (`import './k.css'` for `--family-key k`), and a source its own stylesheet with a query (`import './p.css?inline'`): a first build from a clean checkout writes it.
  - A project in a folder whose name holds `#`, `?` or `%20` builds a theme that imports a stylesheet.
  - What a theme module changes for the whole process while it loads (the working folder, a built-in object such as `JSON` or `Object.prototype`) is put back when the load ends.
  - `--out` naming a TypeScript declaration file (`p.css.d.ts`) is refused with the stylesheet name to give, instead of writing CSS into it.
- `astryx theme build`:
  - A plain-object theme (`export default {name, tokens}`) goes through `defineTheme` as a `defineTheme(…)` call does: a `[light, dark]` pair is written as `light-dark()`, and Core's media-surface rules are written. One with `extends` and no tokens builds as the empty theme over its base.
  - A spread of a package theme (`{...neutralTheme, name}`) is refused naming the spread and the form that builds (`extends: neutralTheme`), not an `icons` field the file does not set.
  - A stylesheet the theme source imports (`import './brand.css'`) is named in a warning: the built outputs do not carry it, so the app imports it.
  - What a theme module changes while it loads in `console`, a global (`Buffer`) or the file mode mask is put back when the load ends, so the command prints its result and writes readable files.
- `astryx theme build`: a theme file is read for its theme, and nothing it does while loading breaks the command.
  - A Sass, Less, Stylus or PostCSS stylesheet a theme module imports loads as an empty module, as a `.css` import does.
  - An import that the project's tsconfig `paths` or `baseUrl` maps (`@app/c`, `lib/c`) is named as a path alias, never offered as a package to install.
  - With `--out` naming another stylesheet, the built module's usage comment names the stylesheet written.
  - When a build of several files stops at a failure, the error says which outputs the files before it wrote, in text and `--json` alike.
  - A default export that holds themes (`export default {light, dark}`) is named as such.
  - A theme module that calls `process.exit` while loading is refused by name; `--check` never passes without its verdict.
  - A value a theme module throws that is not an Error is shown as it is.
  - What a theme module prints goes to stderr, so `--json` output stays valid.
  - A timer a theme module leaves running no longer keeps `theme build` or `--check` from exiting.
- `astryx theme build`:
  - A plain-object theme a theme extends (`const b = {name: 'b', extends: neutralTheme, …}; export default {name: 'p', extends: b}`) is made with `defineTheme` first, so its own base, typography and `[light, dark]` pairs are kept, and one with no tokens builds.
  - A misspelled field is named wherever the theme object comes from (a member, an array element, `Object.assign`), without a line where the source does not write it as one.
  - The warning for a stylesheet the theme source imports names a package stylesheet by the specifier the source wrote, and is given by the editor's compile too.
  - A plain-object theme whose getter throws is a failed load (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`) naming the file and the field, not `ERR_UNKNOWN`.
- `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the form that works, a part key it cannot write as intended: a pseudo key that leaves a parenthesis, bracket, quote or comment open (a browser then drops the rules after it), a pseudo key that is no selector, a selector list such as `':hover, :focus'` (only its first member is scoped to the part), and a custom property with capitals (written in kebab case, so `var()` of the name as written reads nothing). The output is the same as before. A missing input near a theme source in the same folder (a missing extension, a one-letter slip) is offered that source.
- An import written as a template literal with nothing put in it (``import(`./icons.ts`)``) is read as the string it holds by these commands: `astryx theme build --watch` follows it, the built theme module carries it, `astryx doctor`'s shipped-import check judges it, and `astryx template` lists a package imported that way in its install line when the project lacks it. Before, such an import was skipped.
- `astryx theme build` reads `var()` in any letter case when it warns about a token that reads itself, tokens that read each other, or a `var()` no token sets, and it follows a loop through the token definitions Core sets on the theme's root (`--font-size-2xl: var(--text-heading-1-size)`). A misspelled pseudo-class (`:hovr`) is warned with the one it is near. The output is the same as before.
- `astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field in a theme a `let` is reassigned to or a dynamic import loads, at its line; warns tokens given as a `Map` or `Set`, whose entries it does not read; and stops at the field, with a message, on a token object that has no text form (made with `Object.create(null)`), never with Node's own text. A BigInt in a plain theme's type scale no longer ends the build. `astryx experimental theme` reads a boxed token (`new String('red')`) as the text the build writes.
- `astryx theme build`: a theme file is read for its theme, and what its code leaves behind no longer decides the command.
  - A family build over a file at the `--family-key` name lists the replace warning in `--json` too, as the text does.
  - A `process.exitCode` a theme module sets is not the command's exit code.
  - A theme module importing a `.postcss`, `.stylus` or `.sss` stylesheet loads it as an empty module.
  - What a theme module prints after it loaded (a deferred log) goes to stderr, so `--json` stays valid.
  - A theme module whose top-level await never settles is refused (`ERR_THEME_LOAD`, naming the file), not ended by Node with exit 13.
  - A theme source may import the stylesheet its own build writes, which a first build from a clean checkout now writes; a missing stylesheet it does not write is refused by name.
  - Every handle a theme module opens (a timer from `node:timers`, a file watcher, a server, a message port) is let go once it is loaded, so the command exits.
  - A promise a theme module leaves rejecting is a warning on stderr, not a crash after the result.
  - `astryx experimental theme compile` names a value a theme two `extends` up refuses in the file and line that hold it.
- `astryx theme build` warns, at its line and with the same output as before, a field `defineTheme()` does not take (`component:`, `tokenz:`, `ondark:`, `onDark.localTokens`, `typography.body.fontFamily`), with the field it is near; and a BigInt, a function or a Date value, naming what it writes. A BigInt no longer ends the build with an unknown error. A surface token that loops through a token Core sets on that surface is warned once, at its line, and Core's own surface token is no longer named as one from the theme it extends.
- `astryx theme build` warns a `[light, dark]` pair of sizes (`['4px', '12px']`), which `light-dark()` does not take, and a pair half that reads a token nothing sets, as it warns the same CSS written as text. A var() name with a letter beyond ASCII (`var(--café)`) is read as CSS reads it: no false warning in the build, and no refusal in `astryx experimental theme`.
- `astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field that reaches the theme input through a spread (`{...shared}`, `onDark: {...dark}`, an imported object), or in a theme the file imports and then exports, at the line that writes it; a BigInt typography value held in a const is named too; and a `[light, dark]` pair whose half is empty or a number, which `light-dark()` does not take, so the browser drops the value. A boxed primitive in a part (`padding: new String('4px')`) is written as its text, as a token's is, instead of as JSON text with its quotes.
- `astryx theme build` warns a misspelled field wherever the theme's sources write its input: an input held in a const, `defineTheme` imported under another name, a theme a file re-exports from another module (named with that module's file and line), and an `onDark`, `onLight` or `typography` block held in a const; a method written as a field (`onLoad() {}`) is warned too, and so is a BigInt typography value. A TypeScript type assertion such as `<any>1` in a `.ts` theme no longer costs every warning its line. A BigInt inside a part's array or nested block no longer ends the build: it is warned by what is written, and a value that holds itself stops the build at its line. A symbol, or a tokens object that holds itself, stops the build at its line instead of with a raw error. A boxed string (`new String('4px')`) is judged by what is written: no warning as a token or a pair half.
- `astryx theme build --json` carries in its `warnings` the `--out` warnings the text run prints (a stylesheet name that is not .css, an output of another theme source it replaces, a folder the theme editor made), names a folder it cannot write with its fix instead of a temporary file's error, and names an `extends` written as a helper's call or a conditional as what it cannot follow instead of an inline icon registry. Its note on fonts named but not loaded also names the families of a component's `font` shorthand (`font: '600 14px Lora, serif'`).
  [fix] `astryx theme build`'s full font help leaves out, family by family, each family the theme's own `<slug>.fonts.css` loads; before, it printed the whole list unless every family was loaded.
- `astryx theme build --watch` rebuilds when a file a theme brings in with TypeScript's `import x = require('./file')` changes, as it does for any other import.
- `theme build --check` and `doctor` no longer call a local theme's outputs stale just because another CLI release built them, or the CLI ran under another command name. Each output's header still names the CLI release that built it, and a built module still names the build command, but those lines no longer have to match. Before, every update of the CLI that answers marked every local theme stale. So did building under one command name and checking under another, although a rebuild changed only those lines. That CLI can be a global install, or a tool that runs the CLI for you.
- A theme that gives a Card, a Dialog or a menu corners of different radii (`borderRadius: '12px 12px 0 0'` or a corner longhand such as `borderStartStartRadius`) now reaches what those components hand each corner to: a full-bleed Table or a bleeding List in a Card or a Dialog takes each corner as the container draws it, focus ring and row fills included, and the rows of a pointer menu (DropdownMenu's popover and sub-menu flyouts, and ContextMenu), sub-menu rows included, take the menu's shape less its padding; the touch sheet's list rows, and a drilled-in sub-menu view with its own header or footer, keep their own corners. An elliptical corner (`8px / 4px`) reaches a full-bleed Table; a List and menu rows subtract the padding from it, so they keep square corners there. A default Card, Dialog or menu inside a themed one keeps its own corners. Before, these children kept square corners, or took the first corner's radius at every corner when the CLI theme editor wrote the radius. The theme pipeline writes each corner to its own private variable for components whose derived `borderRadius` entry sets the new `corners` flag. A radius of one value draws as before.
- When an app adds a theme from a package it has not installed, `theme add` and `doctor` now name the install that works. They use the project's package manager. For a theme package that Astryx releases with Core, they name the project's Core release, saved exactly when the project pins Core. A project with no Core yet gets the release of the CLI that answers. Before, `doctor` named `npm install <theme>@latest`, and `theme add` named the package with no version. Each Astryx theme names Core's exact release as its peer, so in a project on an older release, npm refused the install. `doctor` also no longer adds `--package @astryxdesign/cli` to the theme add command, which named the CLI as the theme's package.
- `astryx theme build` gives one warning, at its line, for a part's variants written as a `variants` map of values to blocks (`variants: {variant: {secondary: {…}}}`), naming the style keys that write them (`'variant:secondary': {…}`), instead of three warnings that never showed the working form. The output is the same as before.
- The theme showcase template's inventory table keeps product names whole on phones: the Item column's floor grows from 80 px to 160 px, and in a narrow column the name moves under its thumbnail instead of breaking letter by letter. The table scrolls sideways in its own region as before. Wide screens look the same.
- `theme build` (with or without `--check` or `--family`), `integration verify` and `doctor` load a theme that extends a base theme whose module imports its own stylesheet, such as a package's `./themes/<slug>` entry that loads the theme's CSS. Node stopped on that import with `Unknown file extension ".css"`. On Node 22.15 and later, a stylesheet that any module of the theme imports now loads as an empty module. Node resolves each stylesheet import from the module that writes it, so a missing stylesheet still fails. On Node 22.13 and 22.14 nothing changes: a theme build (`theme build`, `integration verify`, `doctor`'s freshness check) still stops on any stylesheet import, and a read of a built theme module (`doctor`, `component`) still loads only a stylesheet whose import resolves from that module's folder.
- A plain table's rows keep the text colour around them in Butter, Y2K and Gothic; only a striped table's even rows take the stripe's text. Inside a coloured card in dark mode, every second row of a plain table read white on the pastel card, at 1.15:1 to 2.12:1. Those themes' striped-row rule now reads the row's `striped` state, in their packages and in the copies the CLI bundles.
- On a phone, TopNav's end content is never wider than the bar, so an end item that can narrow, like a search field, narrows and the menu button stays in view. The Shell Nav template's search now narrows on a phone instead of pushing the menu button off screen at 375 px.
- The per-user cache of transpiled TypeScript stays small and fast however many folders load the same files. Copies now live in `astryx/transpiled`, named for each file's text and settings, so the same file in many folders shares one copy, unless its text contains `meta`. Each new copy trims only its own subfolder, so no run reads the whole cache. Before, a machine that ran many projects or tests in fresh folders could fill the old single folder with hundreds of thousands of copies, and the next theme command spent minutes reading it. Project `doctor` now names that old folder and the command that removes it.
- An unknown command names the command meant when its words come from another command line. `astryx add theme matcha` names `theme add matcha`, not `integration add theme matcha`; `astryx eject button` names `swizzle Button`, not `theme eject button`; `astryx templates list` names `template --list`, not a template called `list`. A short table of other tools' words names the command that does their job: `migrate --from 0.6.0` names `upgrade --from 0.6.0`, `add button` names `swizzle Button` and `component Button`, `add settings --path <file>` names `template settings <file>`, `props Card` names `component Card --props`, and `browse integrations` names `discover`. A suggestion keeps the options in reach of the command it names, including the program's own (`--json`, `--base`), and names an input the run still needs as a placeholder (`upgrade --from <old-version>`). A suggestion is never run for you.
- A manifest key the running CLI does not know is no longer an integration issue. Everyday commands stop printing "has 1 integration issue(s)" for an integration published against a newer CLI, and project `doctor` no longer lists it. `doctor integration validate` and `integration check` list it as an `unknown_manifest_key` note, which fails nothing; a key one letter from a known one is a `next` note with its fix.
- Outside a project, `astryx upgrade` without `--from` now leads with the reason: the folder is outside a project. It says to run upgrade with `--from <old version>` in the app's folder. Before, it led with "Missing required --from", so adding `--from` in the same folder got a second refusal.
- `astryx upgrade` reads a `.ts` file as TypeScript without JSX and a declaration file as declarations, as TypeScript does. A type assertion (`<Item>value`) in a `.ts` file, or a declaration without a value (`export const limit: number;`) in a declaration file (`.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, `.d.cts`, or an arbitrary-extension declaration file such as `styles.d.css.ts`), no longer stops the run with a parse error, and a codemod changes such a file like any other. A `.tsx` file and JavaScript read as before.
- Outside a project, `astryx doctor integration validate <package>` now checks the copy of the package that the folder uses, an integration installed for the computer included. Before, it looked only in the `node_modules` at or above the folder and reported `package_not_found`, though `astryx doctor` names this command for an integration installed for the computer that it cannot load. A copy that the other commands skip for its peer ranges is checked too, with a note that says why: `cli_peer_version`, or the new `core_peer_version` when only its `@astryxdesign/core` range excludes this CLI's release.
- The StyleX setup docs name `@stylexjs/unplugin` (`stylex.vite()`) for Vite. Under Vite, `@stylexjs/rollup-plugin` fails on `astryx.css`, so a page template that uses StyleX stayed blank. The note on such a template now points to the setup section.
- The work item's subtasks wrap instead of cutting off after a few words on a phone, and each task's due date and assignee move under its title there.

#### Performance

- A mistyped `astryx component` name answers faster on repeat runs: the Core docs its suggestions read are kept between runs, so the answer no longer reads every Core doc again. (#12538)
- A run that loads no project, other than `hook`, and whose `--base` names no other package, such as `astryx --version`, `--help` or `manifest`, no longer loads the base resolver. Core's base declaration reads Core's package name from a small module of its own, so it loads no provider-identity code. Output is unchanged.
- A run that keeps many values trims the per-user catalogs folder once, when it ends (a command that fails trims it as it exits), instead of after each value. A first `theme build` on a fresh cache keeps about 270 values and is about 130 ms faster. Every answer is unchanged, and the folder keeps the same size limit.
- `upgrade` skips a codemod for a file that holds a backslash when the file's escapes spell none of the codemod's words, as it already did for files with no backslash. Before, any backslash anywhere in a file (a `\n` in a string, a `\d` in a regular expression) sent the file through every codemod's parse, so a scan of a typical app parsed about a quarter of its files several more times than needed. An upgrade from 0.6.8 answered 24% to 55% sooner across the apps measured; ranges that run mostly older codemods gain less, because those codemods still run on every file. Output and written files are unchanged.
- `upgrade` binds jscodeshift to each parser once per codemod instead of once per file, which built a new copy of jscodeshift's helpers for every file. An upgrade over a 240-file app runs about 150 ms faster. Output does not change.
- On Linux, in a project whose integration takes the CLI's debug record, every command finishes about 11 to 17 ms sooner. The record names the locale and time zone the process's Intl uses, and asking Intl for them first loads ICU's data at the end of the run. The answer is now kept beside the kept gathers while the environment values, the Node and ICU versions and the time zone files it comes from are unchanged. Elsewhere, and on other systems, it is asked as before. The record's values do not change.
- `astryx discover` with no query asks the project's discover sources for their catalogs while it reads the installed packages, instead of after. With a large integration whose source asks a remote catalog, the list came back about 0.4 seconds sooner. Output does not change.
- A command that keeps catalogs keeps the parse of each shipped doc it reads, by the doc's text, so a later read of that doc does not parse it again. The doc parsers build their schemas only when they first parse, not when the CLI loads them. Output is unchanged.
- `docs` keeps the CLI's own docs tree between runs, while every file it was read from is unchanged. In a project where an integration can load, `docs` and its topics start about 30 to 65 ms sooner. Where none can load, `docs` keeps nothing and nothing changes. `doctor` still checks the tree's files themselves. Output does not change, except that `doctor`'s row for the per-user cache now names the docs tree among the entries it holds.
- `doctor --built <path>` now reads doctor's kept checks back as `doctor` does, once the per-user cache folder exists: the CLI took the path after `--built` for a subcommand, so those runs checked the docs again every time. In a project whose integrations add docs, a warm `doctor --built` is about 200 ms faster; in a Core-only project the difference is within noise. The build itself is still checked on every run. Check results do not change; the cache row counts the kept checks.
- `doctor --built` reads source files faster: it parses each file without attaching comments to syntax nodes, blanks comments in one pass, and walks a file's syntax tree for `require()` and `import()` calls only when its text can hold one. On a 240-file app the source scan takes about a third less time. Output does not change.
- Once the per-user catalogs folder exists, `astryx doctor` keeps what its `button-actions` check finds while every folder the check listed, every file it read and every package it looked up are unchanged. A warm `doctor` in a project that has not changed then skips that check's scan: it no longer parses the project's pages for buttons again. Every answer is unchanged.
- Once the per-user catalogs folder exists, `astryx doctor` keeps what its `core-props` check finds while every folder the check listed, every file it read, and the TypeScript, Core and project config it used are unchanged. A warm `doctor` in a project that has not changed then skips that check's scan: the check no longer parses the project's pages or reads Core's types again. The check also loads its parts only when they are needed, so a project without TypeScript no longer loads the component reader. Every answer is unchanged.
- `astryx doctor` reads its kept docs checks back after an edit to the app's source. They run before the scans that read the app's source (its theme wiring and, in a project that names an icon set, its placeholder icons), so what they keep no longer depends on the app's files. Right after an edit, `doctor` in a project with an app finished about 230 ms sooner. Output does not change.
- A kept value from an exact codec is stored as the JSON text its exactness check already read, so storing it no longer writes, parses and compares the value a second time. A run that keeps template discovery stores it about 15 ms sooner. A value that does not read back exactly is still never kept. Output does not change.
- A machine's first `search` or `build` run, and its first `component`, `template`, `theme`, `discover` or `docs` run in a project where an integration can load, now keeps what it gathers, and Node's compile cache is written from the first run. With the CLI installed in the project, the second command on a new machine (most often the same session's next one) reads them instead of gathering again: about 1.7 s faster for `search` and 0.8 s for `component` in a project with an integration. A global copy with no Core beside it starts installing its Core after its first run, which changes what the next run reads, so it reads from its third run, as before. Answers do not change; `doctor`'s "Kept catalog cache" row counts the entries the first run now keeps.
- A run through `@astryxdesign/cli/host` now keeps what it gathers, as a run of the `astryx` bin does, so a tool that carries the CLI answers its second `search` from the kept catalog: about 0.47 s instead of 1.4 s. A kept entry names the package sets, integrations and command name the host passed, so a hosted run and a bin run in the same folder never read each other's answers. Answers do not change.
- `astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` in a package's own folder keep npm's list of the files the package packs. They read it back while the package's folders list the same entries (names, types and where each link points), and package.json, the ignore files npm applies in the package and in each folder above it, any package.json above it, and the npmrc files npm reads are all unchanged. Which files npm packs never depends on what they hold, so a run after an edit inside a file, saved in place or by renaming a new copy over it, skips npm. That took seconds for a large package: each check there finished about 2.6 seconds sooner. A package that bundles dependencies, or has a link in its folders, is asked every time. Output does not change.
- `integration check` and `doctor integration validate` ask npm once what a package's own folder packs, instead of once for each check that asks, and the authoring checks inside `integration check` no longer run the shipped-import check, whose notes they never read. In a large package with a `files` field, `integration check` finishes in about 10 seconds instead of 27, and `doctor integration validate` in about 9 instead of 12.5. Output does not change.
- `component --list` keeps its list between runs in a project where an integration can load, like template discovery's records, so a repeat list answers sooner there (about 220 ms with a large TypeScript integration). A new, removed or edited component, doc or integration lists again on the very next run.
- Which integration component answers to a Core component's name is kept between runs with the component list, so `component` in a project whose integration replaces Core components no longer loads every one of that integration's component docs on each run: about 40 to 60 ms faster per call in a project with a large integration. It is decided again whenever a doc's `replaces`, the package's CLI range, the integration's components folder, its configuration or its manifest changes. Output does not change.
- A kept catalog entry now names the kept entries it builds on and stores only the file states they do not hold. A run checks each kept entry once, however many entries build on it, so an entry checks no file that the entries it builds on already checked. A warm `component`, `search` or `template` in a project with a large integration checks about 3,800 fewer files; output does not change.
- In a project with an integration, `astryx` commands that read back what they kept (`component`, `search`, `template`, `docs`, `build` and others) finish about 10 ms sooner. A kept gather no longer checks the CLI's own files one by one: as the per-user cache record already says, the CLI's build id stands for them, and now so does the folder the CLI runs from, so a copy installed in another folder, such as a patched one, keeps its own entries. In-place edits to an installed CLI stay unsupported; deleting the per-user `astryx/catalogs` folder clears what was kept. A package in the node_modules folder inside the CLI's is still checked, as before. Output does not change, except `astryx doctor`'s cache row, which now names the folder beside the build id.
- `doctor` keeps its scan of how the app wires its themes between runs, like its docs checks, so a repeat `doctor` answers about 20 to 35 ms sooner. An edit to the app's source, a theme or a theme package scans again on the very next run.
- The theme build loads jiti, which transpiles TypeScript theme sources, through the module loader's lazy CommonJS loader, instead of importing jiti's ES module entry whenever any command loads the theme API. `component` in text and `doctor` no longer load jiti and start about 15 to 30 ms sooner. `theme build` still loads it, but no longer through the ES module entry, which made Node scan jiti's whole CommonJS bundle for export names; it starts about 15 to 30 ms sooner too. Output does not change.
- The CLI reads a project's lockfile only for an Astryx package the project has not installed, and reads it once per lookup for all such packages. In an app whose `node_modules` holds the Astryx packages it declares, no command parses the lockfile. With a large lockfile (2 MB in our measurement), that saves about 50 ms per command and about 200 ms per `doctor` run.
- In a project with an integration, `astryx` commands that keep what they gather (`component`, `search`, `template`, `docs`, `doctor` and others) load the installed CLI's own modules by their path in its folder, without Node first checking that each file exists and where it really lives, so they finish sooner.
- `astryx doctor` starts about 6 to 10 ms sooner, and a first lookup in a project whose integration imports the CLI's API about 15 ms sooner. Doctor's theme checks and the codemods' parser loaded postcss as they loaded, so every importer of the CLI's API loaded it too; they now load it only when they read a stylesheet. Output does not change.
- `astryx component` and the `astryx theme` commands start about 5–10 ms sooner again. The theme build module they load loaded postcss at once, through the module that reads a built theme's imports; postcss now loads only when a stylesheet's imports are read. The font stylesheet reader uses the same first-use postcss. Output does not change.
- What the CLI keeps between runs is checked against what each check it made returned, and no more. A check whether a file is there is checked by whether it is still there, and a real-path lookup by the path it answered. An edit to a file the CLI only checked for, or only resolved, no longer makes the next run work its kept data out again. A file whose content any kept step read is checked by its stamp, as before, and so is an ignore file a check looks for before it asks npm what a package packs. Output does not change.
- A command that reuses kept data hands each kept list of what it read to the run's records once, instead of once for every step that reuses it, and works out the CLI-file states a derived value keys on only when one is asked for. In a project with a large integration, `component`, `docs`, `doctor`, `search`, `template` and `theme list` finish 4 to 14 ms sooner. Output does not change.
- A warm `astryx search` reads back from its kept entry table only the word lists the query names, not every list, so it allocates less and spends less time collecting garbage. Every answer is unchanged.
- `search` answers sooner: a name or keyword word that starts with another letter than a query word is no longer expanded into its plural and stem forms to compare them, since every form of a word keeps its first letter, and an entry's description words are read only when a spelled-out name needs them. Output is unchanged.
- `astryx search` loads its icon-section code only where icon features are on, so a search in a project without them no longer loads it. Each such search is about 6–8 ms faster, and every answer is unchanged.
- `astryx search` and `astryx build` use the scores they already worked out for each word of a request when they order the results, so a long request ranks sooner. The results do not change.
- `search` lowercases each candidate's names, keywords and prose once per run instead of on every term and synonym, and scores a one-word query once instead of twice, so a warm search answers up to about 20 ms sooner, most for one-word and typo queries. Results are unchanged.
- The published CLI stores Core's component list and imports at publish, and uses them while the installed Core's files are unchanged, so `component --list` answers about 30 to 60 ms sooner in a project with no integrations. Another Core version, or a change to any Core file or folder the list reads, reads Core live, as before.
- The published CLI reads its own shipped docs as already checked against their schema at publish, instead of checking each one on every read, so `docs` answers about 25 ms sooner. A doc that was edited or is not shipped is checked as before. Output is unchanged.
- The published CLI stores search's catalog at publish, and uses it in a project that adds nothing to a catalog while the CLI's and Core's files are unchanged, so a machine's first `search` answers about 350 ms sooner and its first `build` about 290 ms sooner. The catalog is gathered live, as before, in a project with an integration, a package that adds docs or blocks, or a local theme; with another Core version; and after a change to any file or folder the catalog reads. Output is the same.
- `astryx template` works out the components its "Read the components it uses in one call" line names in one pass: a name the component list holds under Core or a configured integration needs no lookup, a chart library's import needs none, and the names it does look up share each folder listing and doc read. In a project with an integration, a template answer is about 0.3–0.7 s faster again. Every answer is unchanged.
- `astryx template` keeps what it reads from a template's source to name the components it uses, by the source's text and the parser's release, so a warm answer no longer parses the source to name them. Every template answer is unchanged; `doctor --json`'s kept-catalog message names the new kept value.
- `astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` gather the parts of each source file the template walks judge once per check, instead of walking the file's whole syntax tree again for every template that reaches it. For a package with many templates that share helpers, each check finished about 0.4 seconds sooner. Output does not change.
- `search`, component lookups, `build`, `doctor`, `integration` and `theme list` no longer load Node's zlib module, which they never use; `theme add` loads it only to unpack a shared theme's `.tgz`. Those commands are about 2 ms faster, and every answer is unchanged.
- `astryx theme build` of a theme with a local TypeScript or JSX module, such as an icon registry, finishes about 200 ms sooner when the module has not changed since the last build. The JavaScript it compiles from the module is kept beside the kept gathers and read back while the source, the compile options, the imports it rewrites and every file of the Babel that compiled it are unchanged, so such a build loads neither `@babel/core` nor its TypeScript and JSX plugins. A first build, and a build after an edit to the module, compile as before. The written files do not change.
- `astryx theme build` of a theme whose part styles hold pseudo-class keys (`':hover'`, `'::before'`) or whose tokens hold names without two dashes finishes about 20 to 30 ms sooner on a repeat build. What its css-tree checks of those keys and names find is kept beside the kept gathers and read back while the keys and every file of css-tree's code and data are unchanged, so such a build loads no css-tree. The build's warnings, errors and written files do not change.
- `theme build` reads each Core component doc at most once per run. A theme whose component overrides name prop values (such as `variant:ghost` or `size:sm`) was checked against up to three views of Core's docs (the theming targets, the known prop values, and the components a new value augments), and each view read and checked every doc again. Such a build now finishes about 50 to 110 ms sooner. A theme with no such overrides reads the docs once, as before. Output does not change.
- In a project where an integration can load, `theme build` keeps what it checks a theme against in Core's component docs between runs, while every doc and folder they were worked out from is unchanged. It works them out before it reads the theme, so they do not depend on the theme: building a theme again, with or without an edit to it, finishes about 120 to 150 ms sooner. A Core-only project keeps nothing and works out only what a build needs, as before. `doctor`'s row for the per-user cache names the new entry; output does not change otherwise.
- `theme build` keeps the transpiled code of the theme sources it loads in the transpile cache the CLI already uses for integration manifests and TypeScript docs, so a build of an unchanged theme no longer transpiles it again: about 150 ms faster per build. An edited theme is transpiled again. On systems with user ids, that cache is the per-user one, which now stays within the same size limit as the kept catalogs: once it has grown, a run removes its least recently used transpiled copies, never one written in the last day or read in the last day where the file system records reads. `doctor`'s "Kept catalog cache" row now names that limit. Other output does not change.
- The first `theme build` after a CLI upgrade reads back the JavaScript it compiled from a theme's local TypeScript or JSX modules, as long as the upgrade leaves the code that compiles them and Babel's installed files as they are, so it loads no Babel compiler. For a theme with an icon registry, that first build is about 0.15–0.3 s faster, and about 0.4 s when Node's compile cache is empty too. An invalid browserslist setting in the project no longer makes that compile fail. Every other answer is unchanged.
- The theme entry loads the theme build, add, eject and targets code on its first call, so a `component` read that only resolves the project's theme no longer loads it. Output is unchanged.
- A `theme build` of an unchanged theme reads back what its check of settings that do not show as written parsed last time, and loads no css-tree. A warm build of a theme with component styles is about 46 ms faster. Every answer is unchanged.
- `astryx integration check` and `astryx doctor integration validate` parse each of a package's source files once for the walks that follow each template's imports, instead of once for every template that reaches the file. For a package with many templates that share helpers, each check finishes about a second sooner. Output does not change.
- A warm `astryx component` or `astryx template` lookup that misses in a project with only Core answers about 55–60 ms faster, because template discovery is now kept for those commands. Every answer is unchanged. (#12585)

#### Documentation

- The agent docs `astryx init` writes, and the computer-level skill, name the Astryx prop names that differ from other libraries in the workflow's third step: buttons, badges, tokens and tabs take their text in `label` (Text, Heading and Link take children), booleans start with `is` or `has`, and every input takes `value` and `onChange`. An agent that writes props before it reads a component now writes these right far more often. Run `astryx upgrade` or `astryx init` to refresh a project's agent docs.
- The AI Chat Landing template's keywords name its greeting, its suggestion cards and its composer. `astryx search` now finds it for an idea about a greeting, and `astryx build` lists it as an alternative start for more ideas that name a greeting, suggestions or a composer.
- The `ai-chat` page template now gives its dead buttons and menu items a behavior: the composer's send, mention and attach buttons, the document version menu, and the document's share action now show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and Copy copies the document to the clipboard (desktop and narrow screens). No layout or styling changes.
- The `build()` API description says a whole-page idea that would start on the app shell starts from the closest page template.
- The `build` API doc and the build kit's comments say that for a whole page the page-pick model chooses the start from the ranker's list and its own word tables, so the start can differ from the ranker's first template.
- The `theme` row of the bare `astryx docs` list says what the topic is in one sentence; the theme editor's how-to lines (make or change a theme, look after each change, a denser or roomier app, one kind of part, a starter app with no app yet) are now the first sections of the `theme` topic, each shown whole where `astryx docs theme` opens.
- The theme authoring doc shows `defineTheme({palette})` with `themePalette()` from `@astryxdesign/core/palette`. `astryx theme palette generate` and the theme editor's colors give the same output as before: the CLI now runs a copy of the palette engine and its token mapping generated from Core's source.
- The Astryx skill the CLI writes for agents on the computer, and the Claude Code and Codex plugin skill made from it, now say to start a page with `astryx build "<what the page is for>"`, and to start anything else with `astryx search`.
- The Astryx skill the CLI writes for agents on the computer, and the Claude Code and Codex plugin skill made from it, now say to pin `@astryxdesign/cli` exactly when the project pins `@astryxdesign/core` exactly. Before, agents added the CLI at Core's version with a `^` range beside an exactly pinned Core.
- The `useContainerReveal` usage block says the actions stay visible under a coarse primary pointer (a phone or tablet), not on any touch device, matching the hook's behavior on a touchscreen laptop used with a mouse.
- The documentation, technical documentation, design documentation, order detail, work item detail and library page templates now list keywords in the words their users use for those pages, so `astryx search` and `astryx build` find them for more ideas. The template authoring guide now asks authors to describe each page that way.
- The content page templates now give their dead buttons and menu items a behavior: in `course-detail`, `documentation`, `documentation-technical`, `detail-page` and `work-item-detail`, the buttons, cards and menu items that did nothing now either work or show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), the documentation banner's Get started is a link, and toasts that claimed an action had happened now say it would happen. Refund on `detail-page` and Delete in `work-item-detail`'s attachment menus are left unwired, because an irreversible action needs a confirm step. No layout or styling changes.
- The typography docs say what Core builds, in one rule: a heading with no `family` takes the body's whole font list; with its own `family`, only its own `fallbacks`; `fallbacks` with no `family` build nothing. `TypographyConfig`, its `heading` field, `defineTheme`'s `typography`, the `fonts-and-assets` doc page and the theme template say it; the `font-setup` page says a heading with no family uses the body's and points to `fonts-and-assets` for the rest.
- The debug event's `project.integrationCount` is documented as what it counts: the integrations the project's astryx.config names, not integrations loaded from dependencies the config does not name.
- `astryx docs use-a-theme` now says how to make dark mode the default: pass `mode="dark"` to the root `Theme`. A server-rendered app also sets `<html data-theme="dark">`, so the first paint is dark.
- `astryx docs --help` shows `astryx docs skills` and `astryx docs skills/astryx` among its examples, and the `docs` command reference says what `skills` and `skills/<name>` read.
- `astryx docs cli/skill-places` says where to keep the Astryx guidance for AI agents: the AGENTS.md block in a project (the default, read by every agent), a project skills folder when a team keeps its guidance as skills, and the computer skill for agents outside a project, with the `init --to` command, file, and saved record for each place and how each is kept current. `astryx init --help` links to it.
- The `theme` topic has a section on publishing a theme so other teams can use it (ship it in a package; another team runs `theme add <name> --package <package>`), in English, dense and Chinese, and its summary no longer calls its steps "sections", so a search for a section or a scoped section theme finds Section and MediaTheme first again.
- The agent block and the theme docs send a denser or roomier app to the theme (`astryx experimental theme editor set <name> spacing tight`, or `roomy`), as they send colors, instead of gap and padding changes page by page.
- The response types reference says `astryx experimental theme editor show` leaves `look` out when no picture was taken, as the result does, instead of returning it as null.
- The response types reference describes the change result of `astryx experimental theme editor set` and `undo` as it is: `missed` counts the misses the change leaves and `missedParts` the parts they are on, and an undo of a setting listed more than once names the other entries it removed (`alsoRemoved`).
- The agent block and the theme docs say a change to one kind of part (the sidebar, its selected item, the gaps in a form) is a theme change too, not props or styles on one page, and that `astryx experimental theme editor how "<ask>"` names the `set … --on <part>` line for it.
- With no app yet, the agent block, the theme docs and `astryx experimental theme --help` point to `astryx experimental theme preview app <dir>`, which makes a starter app that shows the theme, instead of building an app by hand.
- The export guide says that the exported file's CSS keeps only the web font faces its page, stylesheet or script can use, and that text the file cannot know (typed text, text built from character codes, and dates, numbers and date-field placeholders in the reader's or the page's locale) draws in the next font of its font list.
- The export guide's column-floor advice says a table heading wraps like its cells, so a column's floor must fit the longest word of its heading.
- `astryx --help` now describes `export` in the `experimental` group as "one self-contained HTML file from a page built with Astryx components (not for other pages)". Agents can now tell from the help what `experimental export` makes and which pages it is for.
- The hero and gallery page templates' call-to-action buttons (Get started, Learn more, Explore in `centered-hero`, `gallery-hero`, `product-gallery` and `side-gallery`) are now links to `#`, so they behave as the links they stand in for instead of doing nothing. The Get started arrows in `centered-hero` and `product-gallery` now point toward the end of the line in right-to-left, as in `gallery-hero`; nothing else changes in layout or styling.
- Hook docs for `useChatDictation`, so `astryx hook useChatDictation` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useChatDictation — Voice input` example block: a start and stop control that stays off when the browser has no speech recognition.
- Hook docs for `useChatPasteAsToken`, so `astryx hook useChatPasteAsToken` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useChatPasteAsToken — Long paste` example block: a composer that uses a threshold of 40 and a Pasted note label.
- Hook docs for `useSpeechRecognition`, so `astryx hook useSpeechRecognition` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useSpeechRecognition — Transcript` example block: a headless control that shows whether the browser can listen and the interim transcript.
- Hook docs for `useSyntaxTheme`, so `astryx hook useSyntaxTheme` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useSyntaxTheme — Keyword color` example block: the word const painted with the keyword color of the GitHub Light syntax theme.
- The internationalization guide says provider `overrides` change Astryx wording across an app, and that a component is reworded through its own prop for that string, such as `placeholder` or `cancelLabel`. The InternationalizationProvider overrides example applies its override to every Selector in the app, and shows one Selector rewording its own placeholder through its prop.
- The IDE page template's description now says what its middle pane is: a single read-only code pane, not tabbed documents.
- `astryx init --help` is about half as long: each option and exit code keeps what an agent needs to run it (what it writes, what it refuses, the error codes), and the rare cases (file deletion on `--remove-agents`, the `--user` link details, the five soft exit-0 cases) move to `astryx docs cli/commands/init`.
- Markdown's anatomy now says when its Image part shows alternative text: for an empty image URL, while an unsafe URL renders as source text. Its guidance adds two don'ts: plugins cannot cross a Server Component boundary, and Markdown does not sanitize renderer output. Prop docs now describe `density`, `isStreaming`, `onLinkClick`, and `components`; `inlinePlugins` keeps its own description instead of lending it to `plugins`; `contentWidth` names its 680 default; and the `contentAlign="start"` description now says inline start instead of left. The `onLinkClick` docs say that a custom `link` renderer does not receive the handler.
- The messaging shell template notes what must hold before it is marked ready: build keeps the default app shell for parts and edits whose words the template does not use, and the page-pick model is retrained to include it.
- MetadataListItem's prop docs now list `xstyle`, `className`, `style`, `ref`, and `data-testid`, and say which element each one reaches: the label `dt` when the item is side by side, or the wrapper when it is stacked. The `data-testid` docs say that a side-by-side item puts `-label` and `-value` on its two cells.
- MobileNav's prop docs now list `label`, `xstyle`, `className`, `style`, `ref`, and `data-testid`, and the `label` docs say what names the drawer when it is not set. MobileNav's Chinese and dense prop text now reaches the docs: it was written where the doc compiler does not read it for a doc with two components, so those docs showed the English text. The Chinese text no longer marks `isOpen` and `onOpenChange` as required; inside AppShell the drawer reads them from context.
- MobileNavToggle's docs now say every case where it renders nothing: above the mobile breakpoint, without an AppShell mobile context (AppShell's, or an `AppShellMobileContext` you provide), and when AppShell has no mobile navigation (no side or top nav, `mobileNav={false}`, or a `mobileNav` node).
- MoreMenu's prop docs now list `isMenuOpen` and say that without `size` the trigger takes the surrounding size (from a SizeProvider, ButtonGroup, or Toolbar), else `md`. The Chinese docs gain `isMenuOpen` and `onOpenChange` and the note on where host `data-*` attributes land.
- `astryx docs layout` and `astryx docs tokens` carry the core rules on the namespace page itself: layout names the frame, structure, spacing and breakpoint rules with a three-region example, and tokens shows the StyleX import and the tokens most code needs, so one read is enough to start.
- NavHeadingMenu's docs now document NavHeadingMenuItem and its props (`label`, `description`, `icon`, `href`, `onClick`, `isDisabled`, `ref`, `xstyle`), add `ref` to the menu, and say that `minWidth` wins over the size's minimum width. New best practices name the WAI-ARIA menu pattern and its keys, say to name a standalone menu, and explain how a disabled row stays reachable.
- The npm descriptions of `@astryxdesign/core` and `@astryxdesign/cli` name Astryx, so a search for "astryx" on npm lists them with the other Astryx packages.
- The install page now says that registry calls use Astryx's own short retry and timeout, not npm's fetch-retry or fetch-timeout settings: one retry after a 2-second wait, and at most 30 seconds per request.
- A new experimental guide, `astryx docs cli/experimental/share-a-page`, walks through making a shareable page: write it with Astryx components, render it to one HTML file, share or upload that file, and turn the file back into source to change it.
- The shareable-page guide (`astryx docs cli/experimental/share-a-page`) names the layouts that go wrong on a phone in a file with no script, and how to write each one: a Badge beside text in an HStack (StackItem `static` and `fill`, as its example now does), a Badge on its own line in a VStack (`<StackItem crossAlignSelf="start">`), a long string ListItem label (pass an element), and a table wider than the screen (the file cannot scroll it sideways: keep it within about 310 px with shares that match the floors or `pixel()` columns, each floor fitting its column's longest word and header, padding included). It also suggests `isWrapped`, which shows long CodeBlock lines whole. `astryx experimental render --help` and its doc now point to the guide.
- Some controls in the app shell page templates did nothing when clicked. Now `shell-nav`'s Run project and Share, `shell-top-nav`'s Search products, Sign in and Checkout, and in `theme-showcase` the chat's Export, Close, Attach and Voice input buttons, Add item, the list and grid view buttons, and the inventory row menu's Edit, Duplicate and Move to each show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"). No layout or styling changes.
- `astryx docs layout` and the scaffold guide say that a short form keeps its own 640 column, even when the page starts from a template with a wide frame or a multi-column grid.
- `astryx docs styling` and `astryx docs typography` state their core rules on the namespace page itself, with one short example each, so one read is enough to start; each page still points to its guides for the details.
- The table page templates now give their dead buttons and menu items a behavior: in `table-inbox`, `table-tree`, `table-grouped`, `table-page` and `table-filter`, the buttons and menu items that did nothing now either work or show a toast saying what the real app would do there ("Demo: … would … here"), and toasts that claimed an action had happened now say it would happen. Delete actions are left unwired on purpose, because a destructive action needs a confirm step these templates do not have. Text fields, form inputs and some menus are not part of this change. No layout or styling changes.
